News.title: Body found in water off popular seaside town as cops release pics of wetsuit to help identify mystery swimmer
News.content:
URGENT APPEAL Body found in water off popular seaside town as cops release pics of wetsuit to help identify mystery swimmer







Next

A BODY has been found in the water near to a popular seaside town as cops release pictures of a wetsuit to help identify the swimmer.

Officers scrambled to Sandbanks Quay in Poole, Dorset, on Wednesday morning to reports the body of a man had been found in the area.



Dorset Police said the man was recovered by the coastguard and the force’s marine unit after racing to the scene shortly after 8.38am.

The force is now appealing for anyone with information to come forward as they work to identify the body.



The man is described as white, around five feet eight inches tall, of medium to stocky build and believed to be aged in his 50s with short brown hair. He was unshaven but had no beard.

He was also wearing a full wetsuit with black swim leggings and a navy blue Adidas T-shirt with red writing over the top of the wetsuit.



On his forehead were grey Speedo goggles and he was also wearing black swimming shoes.

Detective Inspector Edmund Murray, of BCP CID, said: “We are carrying out an investigation into the circumstances of this death and, while there is nothing to suggest it is suspicious at this time, we have not been able to identify the deceased despite extensive enquiries.

“We are therefore releasing a description of the man and images of the clothing he was found in and would urge anyone with information regarding this man’s identity to please contact us immediately.”

Anyone with information is urged to contact Dorset Police online or by calling 101, quoting occurrence number 55260157164.

News.title: Girl, 15, stumbled into class & told teacher ‘sir, I’ve been stabbed’ after being ‘attacked by boy who hated women’
News.content:
CHILLING WORDS Girl, 15, stumbled into class & told teacher ‘sir, I’ve been stabbed’ after being ‘attacked by boy who hated women’







Next

A 15-YEAR-OLD girl stumbled into class and told her teacher “Sir, I’ve been stabbed” after she was knifed in the back at school, a court heard.

A boy, who was aged 15 at the time, is on trial accused of her attempted murder at Thorpe St Andrew School near Norwich, Norfolk on March 11.



The teenager – who is now 16 and, along with his alleged victim, can’t be identified for legal reasons – went to the mixed secondary school for 11-18-year-olds with the knife on March 11 this year, King’s Lynn Crown Court heard.

The girl – then aged 15 – told police in a video-recorded interview played to jurors on Thursday that she had seen a masked person dressed “head to toe in black, no school uniform on whatsoever”.



The attack, in a corridor in the morning, was captured by CCTV at the school, the court heard.

The girl said she turned away and it “felt like he touched me on the shoulder, then it felt like he punched me”.

She said she “didn’t know I was stabbed at this point” but she “started running”.

Meanwhile, jurors were told the boy did not say anything to her and she did not recognise him.

The teenager said she was “struggling because everything was going numb and feeling weak” as she attempted to open a door.

The girl then fled into a classroom and “I went ‘Sir, I’ve been stabbed'”.



The girl said the school lockdown bell went off and staff gave first aid.

Of the incident itself, she said that once she had opened the door, “I felt sharp pain shooting through my back, I went like that and it was blood all over my hands”.

She said in the interview, carried out days after the incident: “I don’t think it’s hit me properly yet. It’s just a bit of a shock.”



Asked if she had had any issues with anyone at school, she replied: “No.”

She said that when she first saw the person dressed in black, “he had his hands in his pockets and he was just standing there”.

He was wearing a black mask and had his hood “over his forehead”.

She said she had looked at him and did not “think much of it”, but when she turned away she was attacked.

“It felt like he punched me. I thought he was about to keep throwing punches,” she said.



Stephen Rose KC, defending, asked the girl, who came to court to give evidence, whether she had had any issues with the boy and she said she had not.

She wiped tears from her eyes and asked for a break during her evidence.

Another female pupil at the school, who witnessed the attack, said in a video-recorded police interview that the boy “came up behind (the girl) and just stabbed her in the back near her shoulder”.

She said she “didn’t think he realised I was there until after he did it”, and that she ran off and told a teacher.

“After he stabbed her she said ‘what the f***’, I don’t think she realised she had been stabbed,” she said.



Asked at what point she had first seen the knife, she said “as he raised it”.

Christopher Paxton KC, opening the prosecution case, said yesterday the boy was arrested by police and “remained silent” in interview.

Today, he revealed the boy had written notes including about his “hatred for women” and had an interest in serial killers.

Mr Paxton said one note, pinned up in the boy’s bedroom, said: “My barren world… Hello to all readers out there in the UK and perhaps even the world. If you’re reading this, I am either dead or in custody.

“I imagine the police will be the first to read this and seize it as evidence, so I will make something very clear.



“I made this decision to do so on my own. Nobody told me to. Just me.

“Nobody knew I wanted to do this. Not a single soul.”

In another note, Mr Paxton said the boy wrote: “My whole life I’ve felt an attraction to violence.

“I don’t know the reason. My brain clicks at the thought of chaos. Of blood. Of murder.”

The note continued: “I’ve seen killers being admired. I want admiration.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Paxton told jurors: “We the prosecution say his intention is made plain not just by those moments of the stabbing, but made plain by his notes and his obsession with killing and being fuelled by hatred.”

The boy denies attempted murder and the trial continues.

News.title: Mystery as Russia lifts quarantine after scientist ‘killed by plague’ but death remains shrouded in secrecy
News.content:
Next

RUSSIA has made a sudden decision to lift a quarantine just one week after a scientist allegedly died of the plague.

It comes as Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old researcher, died on October 2 after developing what officials claimed was unexplained “pneumonia”, but it remains a mystery what the infectious bacteria was.



Russian authorities say they have conducted thousands of laboratory tests and deemed the health emergency over, as announced by the Irkutsk Region governor, Igor Kobzev.

Kobzev said: “Medical monitoring of all close contacts has also been completed. No health issues related to infectious diseases have been identified. […] The public health and epidemiological situation in Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable.”



During his speech, Kobzev repeatedly referred to Darya using neutral language such as “the infected” and an “employee.”

He did not name her, express condolences to her traumatised family, or detail whether she would be buried in a zinc coffin to prevent the infection spreading.



The shocking move has confused many around the world amid rumours on social media of a second case of the Plague from a person who came into contact with the laboratory worker.

Russia’s consumer welfare ministry has denied any new cases and says the information online is “fake”, according to Russian state news agency TASS.



Darya died while working at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East when a test tube containing live bacteria “broke”.

Her mother, Svetlana Shipilova, is also a medical professional and believes the cause of death is bogus.

She told Russian outlet Glubina that “she knows the truth” because “even if you throw it at a wall” it is impossible to break a test tube.

She added: “They simply let her die.

“I’m having to fend off stupid acquaintances who believed all this – the clever ones didn’t believe it, of course.”



Svetlana had previously complained that the family’s quarantine left them unable to make arrangements for their daughter’s funeral.

She said: “Who is going to bury her if we’re sitting here in confinement?”

Kobzev offered no state support for her funeral.

Many have criticised his failure to offer any praise for Darya’s work as a scientist or sympathy for her family.

Kobzev claimed that Darya “had been vaccinated and had immunity to the dangerous infections she worked with” – which included the plague, despite these vaccines being far from foolproof.



He insisted that “no accidents involving pathogenic microorganisms were identified at the institute.”

The staunchly pro-Putin governor claimed the episode was a victory for the Putin regime.

He said: “Amid information pressure, specialists thoroughly investigated the situation.

“It was a test. But we came through it with dignity.”

Despite pressure from the World Health Organisation and the US, Russia strongly denies that she contracted the plague.



Darya, a high-flying young medical biochemist, worked in the institute’s plague microbiology department and is known to have conducted research involving Yersinia pestis — the bacterium responsible for one of history’s most feared diseases which triggered the medieval Black Death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Her death led to almost 200 contacts being quarantined and 5,000 tests carried out with international concern of a dangerous and infectious outbreak.

There were also fears that Russia’s disease laboratories may have links to secret bio-warfare bodies.

News.title: Our quiet town is heart of new migrant crisis with mega dinghies & massive detention centre – we don’t feel safe anymore
News.content:
Next

A HISTORIC naval town is now being used as a new landing site for mega dinghies full of migrants and a massive new immigration detention centre.

Locals have said they “don’t feel safe” following balaclava-clad protestors flooding the area on Sunday night, and have accused the government of “sitting on their hands”.



In Gosport, Hampshire, an increasing number of asylum seekers are using the quiet town as a landing spot when crossing the English Channel.

Almost 150 migrants arrived at Gosport on Sunday (October 4), with a dozen protesters arrested following scuffles with cops as RNLI boats brought the migrants to shore.



It marks a change from the typical Calais to Dover route, with French officials telling The Sun that groups are now setting off from Normandy and actively looking at different areas to land on the UK coast.

The rise in migrant arrivals in Gosport has led to plans for both an immigration removal centre and an immigration processing centre.



This has sparked anti-migrant protests in the area – with Sunday night seeing around 300 protesters across all ages contained by a riot police cordon on Haslar Road, near to the harbour.

They have been dubbed “the black balaclava brigade” by locals after they left a “mess” in the streets, including nails, broken glass and barricades to stop migrant coaches.



Diane Croombs, 70, has lived in Gosport since she was five and says she feels things are getting “out of control” in the small town.

She said: “It used to be lovely around here, but now I don’t feel safe.

“I think the protests are good but they get out of hand – both the police and protesters.



“There were roadblocks and a portaloo – they pushed it over for a barricade.

“There were faeces and chemicals leaking out onto the street – but where were they when it came to clean up the next day?

“It’s getting beyond a joke and we’re all fed up with it here.



“The black balaclava brigade might come to smash my windows and I don’t want that.

“The protesters are all drinking out of beer cans when they come down here. You don’t get trollied to peacefully protest.

“The government has got to do something about it because otherwise there will be a massive, massive riot around here.”

Ray and Bernice Hursell are a couple, both in their 80s, living in the same neighbourhood and are disappointed after they moved to the area to have a peaceful life by the sea.

Ray said: “On Sunday night all the roads were blocked and police weren’t letting anyone through. If you had any visitors they would need to somehow prove they knew you.”



Bernice said: “There was broken glass in the street afterwards and they tipped over a portable loo. It’s just a mess.

“We haven’t got the room for any of it here, the migrants or the protests.

“I don’t know where the protesters come from but I don’t think they’re all locals.”

The Haslar Immigration Removal Centre, a new 600-person immigration centre, is being built in the area, which Bernice said has made the value of their house go down.

She said: “Of course the value of our house has gone down too. We know a couple of people who have been trying to sell but they just can’t.



“Who would want to move here without knowing what’s going on? It’s not what anybody wants.”

It is understood that authorities had been preparing for the arrival on the south-coast after the migrants’ boat were shadowed by the French coastguard.

The newest arrivals were taken from the boats and formed a long queue before they could be processed.

They were then taken into a large building and two white coaches were seen next to the building, believed to be their transport.

Another local, Susan Edwards who is 72, said: “It’s disgusting what happened on Sunday night, to be honest. I’m not happy with it at all.



“All of the police had been down there. What if there had been a robbery on the high street? They couldn’t have done anything.

“The police were requiring us to show documents to walk on the streets where we live – our own streets.

“But at the very same time they’re bringing in undocumented migrants.

“I’ve lived in Gosport all my life. It used to be a lovely place but it is at the centre of this.”

A spokesperson for Hampshire Police said: “We are continuing to carry out patrols and speak to residents in the area to understand their concerns and to explain the policing response undertaken to balance the needs of the wider community while enabling peaceful protest.”



Talking about Sunday’s protest, Gosport Borough Council Leader Cllr Zoe Huggins said: “The decision to bring migrants ashore in Gosport rests solely with the Government and their decision to use vacant MOD land, with no consideration to our warnings.

“Gosport Borough Council and our MP have made it crystal clear to the Home Office that Gosport is not the right place to dock small boats.

“Gosport’s position as a peninsula means limited access in and out, the two recent operations required a huge emergency service and partner response and cost by already stretched services, so far these concerns are being completely ignored.

“Gosport residents are understandably worried and angry; many were trapped in their houses for hours on Sunday.

“The vast majority of protestors conducted themselves peacefully, but residents should not be put in that position and they deserve a clear explanation from the Government about why this operation took place here, despite the concerns that have repeatedly been raised.



“The council should also not be expected to cover the cost of clean-up and local resourcing, we call for the Home Office to reimburse these costs.

“We also note that there has been a significant impact to local businesses.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The Government must do more to prevent small boat crossings organised by criminal gangs, and to urgently identify a safe and suitable site for disembarkations or Border Forces to resource boats for interception to take the illegal migrants straight to Dover.

“The Home Office’s silence is deafening , I have made Gosport’s position clear, the Government should respond and act.”

News.title: Britain’s nuclear submarine fleet’s only defence against air attacks revealed as FIRE HOSES despite Putin drone threat
News.content:
Next

SAILORS are being trained to use fire hoses to defend Britain’s nuclear-armed submarines from drone attacks.

The high-pressure jets of water are the only “air defence weapon” on the £4billion Vanguard-class subs.



They are packed with Trident 2 missiles which carry more explosive power than all sides dropped in World War Two.

Yet their last line of defence is hoses — with a source admitting: “You have to use what you’ve got.”



The hoses known as “centre fed reels” are placed on the submarine decks as a precaution when the vessels are tied alongside at the home of the fleet, HMNB Clyde in Faslane.

The Navy insists there are several layers of defence including “physical barriers, patrols, surveillance, monitoring, and counter-drone capabilities”.

Those capabilities include submariners standing on deck and firing water at any drones that evade land-based defences.

The hoses are fitted with pistol-grip nozzles to help sailors aim at aerial targets.

The source added: “We always thought this would be for small spy drones or civilian dicking around — but the threats moved on a lot.”

The Faslane base is the UK’s most sensitive military site and is believed to have been a target of suspicious drones since at least 2018.



It is particularly vulnerable to short-range drones due to being located on a 1km wide stretch of the Scottish sea loch.

A Navy source said: “Gare Loch has excellent natural protection against enemy submarines but the topography leaves it at risk of drones.

“There are lots of public roads, people can roam on the hills. If several drones were launched nearby there is less time to react.”

Meanwhile Vladimir Putin’s Russia has built metal cages to defend its Black Sea subs from drones, Britain’s Defence Intelligence revealed in July.



And US submarine bases — such as King’s Bay in Georgia — are several times bigger than HMNB Clyde, giving defenders more time to react if drones launch near the perimeter.

Drone flights near military bases have soared from nine a year in 2019 to 340 in the last 12 months.

And Russia flew hundreds over nuclear sites across Europe according to the London based IISS think tank.

Targets included France’s Ile Longue nuclear submarine base, Belgium’s Klien Brogel nuclear airfield and RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, which is due to store US air-launched nukes.



The report’s author, Charlie Williams, told The Sun: “Faslane is very clearly of interest to hostile states. We know it has been targeted before and it would not be surprising if it was targeted again.

“It is very surprising they are relying on fire hoses to defend the submarines. We have to hope the MoD is investing in the right kind of capability to defend it.”

Details of Britain’s threadbare defences emerged after US Air Force bombers abandoned RAF Fairford, Gloucs, over fears of an Iran-backed attack.

Specialist anti-drone troops from the RAF Regiment surged into the base last month.

The long-range B-1B Lancers returned to the US on Sunday just days after five men were arrested nearby on suspicion of terror and explosives offences.



Two other men have been arrested. Six of the seven were released on bail.

US officials claimed Iran-backed agents were planning to launch waves of drones in a plot appeared to echo Ukraine’s Operation Spiders Web.

This saw more than 100 drones launched from lorries deep inside Russia to hit airfields.



The Navy’s hose pipe defence drills are designed to defend the nuclear submarines against small and medium range FPV drones.

Long-range attack drones such as Iranian Shadeds or Russian Gerbera drones could be intercepted by RAF fighter jets.

The Vanguard subs are most at risk when sailing on the surface or tied alongside at port. And they spend months, even years, in port at a time.

The source added: “In a worst case scenario, the plan is to grab the centre fed hose reel and use it to knock a drone off course or even knock it down.”

Ukraine has repeatedly hit Russian submarines, including with British Storm Shadow missiles which damaged the Kilo-class Krasnodar submarine when it was in dry dock in Crimea for repairs.



Ukraine has also blitzed Russian submarines with surface, sub- surface and aerial drones at its port in Novorossiysk at the eastern edge of the Black Sea.

The MoD said: “The first duty of Government is national security, and we take the security of our people, sites and local communities extremely seriously, in particular those housing nuclear capabilities.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The protection of our bases is kept under constant review, with a multi-layered approach that includes physical barriers, patrols, surveillance, monitoring, and counter-drone capabilities.

“Through the Defence Investment Plan, we are investing an additional £470million over the next four years to strengthen the protection of military sites across the UK.”

News.title: Shameless Tinder Swindler unveils new dating app to ‘protect’ women with ‘SOS button’ sparking furious backlash
News.content:
MATCH MADE IN HELL Shameless Tinder Swindler unveils new dating app to ‘protect’ women with ‘SOS button’ sparking furious backlash







Next

THE convicted fraudster known as the Tinder Swindler has launched a new dating app which he claims will protect women.

Simon Leviev, 36, who admits he lived for a decade using a fake passport, allegedly used dating app Tinder to scam £7.5million out of women who thought he was the son of a diamond mogul.



Leviev, born Shimon Yehuda Hayut, was convicted of fraud, theft and forgery charges in Israel and Finland in 2015 and 2019.

But now he claims he is a “rehabilitated man” and has launched a new app to protect women from liars and fake users.



He unveiled his soon-to-be-released app, Safe Love, in an ITV interview, where he said the app would have an SOS button to keep users safe.

Leviev insists he is innocent of claims he scammed £7.5million from women, but admitted: “I did live 10 years on a false passport.

“I do know how to lie, I do know how to cheat, I do know how to manipulate. It’s not something that I hide.”

He added: “Obviously, I’ve been convicted. Obviously, I’m not proud of it but obviously it’s maybe a set of skills that others don’t have out there.”

He compared himself to famed fraudster Frank Abagnale Jr., who became a fraud-prevention specialist after committing fraud, theft and forgery.



Leviev said his new app would force users to upload a government ID card and a selfie.

Pictures uploaded to the profile would be scrapped if they differed more than 15 per cent from the original selfie.

He claimed he wants to make sure matches on the app line up – in terms of appearance and identity – with the people a dater meets in real life.

Leviev said: “The idea came from me being the Tinder Swindler.



“They say I made the dating environment unsafe. So I thought, ‘All right. Let’s make it safe.’”

He said he would use his expertise for good, claiming: “I know how fake passports look.”

The convicted fraudster said he maybe even knew “better than a passport controller in the airport, because I did pass hundreds or if not thousands of … fake passports.

“No one ever questioned me once. I know I know how to challenge the system.”

Safe Love is still passing through the regulation stage before its release.



Leviev said it could launch in “a few days, could be a few weeks, but hopefully as soon as possible”.

The Online Dating and Discovery Association (ODDA) slammed the fraudster’s plans for his own app.

It wrote to Apple and Google, urging the tech giants to bar the app from their devices.

ODDA wrote: “We do not believe either app store wishes to be the platform that hosted a fraudster’s return to the very environment in which his crimes were committed.

“Allowing a convicted romance fraud offender to operate a dating platform, an environment built entirely on trust and on the very emotional and financial vulnerabilities he has already been proven to exploit, completely undermines the efforts our sector has made and represents a very real risk to users.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Women who said they were scammed by Leviev alleged they were left in severe financial debt and “mentally scarred” after dating him.

News.title: Teenager arrested for murder after celeb BBL doctor executed in front of customers at Marbella clinic
News.content:
GUNNED DOWN Teenager arrested for murder after celeb BBL doctor executed in front of customers at Marbella clinic







Next

A TEEN has been arrested on suspicion of murder after allegedly executing a supercharged BBL specialist plastic surgeon in front of horrified customers at his Marbella clinic.

UK-trained Dr Alexander Aslani, 57, was shot dead yesterday evening after a gunman charged into his Costa del Sol clinic.



He died after being shot several times in the head inside his clinic in the east of the city, which specialises in BBLs, supercharged BBLs and boob jobs.

The shooter fled the scene, sparking a huge manhunt before a Swedish teen was arrested 24 hours later.



Cops confirmed in a short statement: “A man aged 18 has just been arrested as the suspected author of the homicide committed yesterday evening in Marbella.”

Police sources told El Mundo the gunman was not alone.

Investigators said he had entered the clinic with several customers inside and opened fire.

Dr Aslani was pronounced dead at the scene.

Tragically, the surgeon’s wife Jeannine, who was his director of nursing, was in the clinic when her husband was killed.

The shooter was reportedly dressed in black head-to-toe, fleeing on a motorbike driven by an accomplice.



It comes as police probed whether the killing was a revenge attack linked to a disgruntled client who had repeatedly complained about the results of a cosmetic procedure.

The woman reportedly sent threatening messages to his Cirumed clinic the day before the murder, demanding a refund for her treatment.

Her partner had also allegedly visited the clinic and made threats against staff during an earlier confrontation.



The chilling lead raised fears that the celebrity surgeon was deliberately targeted by a hitman in a contract killing.

Spanish police are investigating whether the gunman was acting on someone else’s orders, although no motive has yet been established.

Dr Aslani previously worked as a consultant plastic surgeon at the London Highgate Hospital.

The UK-trained doctor also worked as a consultant plastic surgeon at Birmingham’s Dolan Park Hospital from 2006 to 2007.

He is known for pioneering the supercharged BBL, which uses implants as well as transferring a patient’s body fat to the buttock area.



He also offered tummy tucks, rib cage reshaping and a “Bikini makeover”, which combines breast augmentation, liposculpture and BBL into a “simple surgery”, according to the clinic’s website.

The Malaga Medical Association condemned the killing, saying: “We firmly and unequivocally reject any act of violence and express our deep concern regarding these extremely serious events that have resulted in the death of a doctor while he was carrying out his professional duties.”

Devastated patients have also paid tribute to the surgeon, who was described as the plastic surgeon of choice for celebrities, models and royalty.



Friend and former patient Nance Lala Van der Veken wrote: “I’m absolutely devastated.

“You didn’t just change my body – you helped shape a part of my life.

“You were truly one of the best plastic surgeons, but to me, you were so much more than my doctor.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You were my friend, someone I trusted completely, and someone whose work I will carry with me for the rest of my life.”

The search for a second suspect, thought to have helped the shooter escape, continues.

News.title: Two women smothered & repeatedly stabbed their friend to death before eating her Cheerios and ransacking flat for money
News.content:
MURDER BETRAYAL Two women smothered & repeatedly stabbed their friend to death before eating her Cheerios and ransacking flat for money







Next

TWO women smothered and stabbed their vulnerable friend to death before helping themselves to her Cheerios and ransacking her flat.

Charlotte James and Amy Keeley were found responsible for the murder of Helen Bloomfield, 52, at her flat in Braintree, Essex, on April 19, 2024.



Keely, 40, of no fixed address, and James, 29, of Braintree, were charged at Chelmsford Crown Court today and will be sentenced on October 16.

Cops discovered Helen’s body on a blood-stained mattress nearly a month after the violent assault, which left her with 44 injuries – although initial enquiries could not determine the “cause of death”.



The women – who’d claimed to be Helen’s friend – unleashed the horrific attack after raiding her flat and failing to find any cash or drugs.

They then stabbed and smothered the victim with a pillow in the early hours of March 20 before leaving her for dead and eating her Cheerios.



Following her death, officers received reports indicating the two friends, James and Keeley, had been responsible.

A number of witnesses told officers that the women had confessed their wicked crime to them – with Helen’s injuries matching their descriptions of the attack.

Forensic analysis identified Keely’s DNA on pillow cases, a broken mirror and a pair of scissors – including some items with blood stains on them.

DNA fingerprints belonging to James were also discovered at the property.



Keely first met Helen in 2022, describing her victim as a “friend” and a “cracking girl”.

She said they would often drink and take drugs together, and that she had personally been taking cocaine and heroin for over 20 years.

In a chilling display of deceit, Keely claimed she had been “gutted” to learn about Helen’s death.

Detective Chief Inspector Greg Wood, who led the investigation, said: “My thoughts, and those of team, are with Helen’s family and friends.

“No conviction will bring her back but I hope this result will help them move forward and represents justice being served.



“Helen was brutally and cynically murdered by Amy Keely and Charlotte James for their own benefit.

“It is difficult to imagine how scared she must have been as two people she knew and may have trusted worked together to take her life.

“Keely and James now face a life sentence and significant time behind bars.”

News.title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says
News.content:
Thames Valley Police has accepted warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes at the time of his arrest in February were unlawful, the High Court has been told.

Following Thursday's hearing, items seized in the raid continue to be held by the police, with a further hearing to take place in 2027 to decide whether the material can be used as evidence.

Meanwhile, the criminal investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor is ongoing.

The former prince, who denies any wrongdoing, was arrested by police on 19 February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, after which he launched a legal challenge over the legality of the search warrants.

The force said it accepted that the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" before they searched the properties.

On Thursday at the High Court, judge Mr Justice Hilliard said Mountbatten-Windsor and the police had agreed that the search warrants had been unlawful.

However, he added: "The fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring the investigation to an end or mean that the whole of the investigation is unlawful."

Mountbatten-Windsor opposes the police's bid to retain the evidence, the judge said, and another hearing is expected in 2027.

News.title: Two Latvian men arrested on suspicion of trespass at RAF base in Cambridgeshire
News.content:
Two Latvian men were arrested after a fence was breached at an RAF base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations, counter-terrorism police have said.

The alert was raised when a Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) security patrol at RAF Molesworth identified an abandoned vehicle at about 22:00 BST on Wednesday.

Searches revealed a small breach of the fence at the site in Cambridgeshire, and a few hours later, police said the pair were arrested inside the perimeter.

The two men are aged 36 and 32 and live in the UK, the Met Police said.

The force's Counter Terrorism Policing London is investigating and commander Helen Flanagan said officers were not currently linking it to the high-profile incident in Gloucestershire.

"We're very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week," said Flanagan.

However, she stressed the inquiry was in its "very early stages".

They were initially arrested on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and criminal damage - after Cambridgeshire Police officers joined the search - and were taken to a local station.

The pair were later arrested on suspicion of an offence under Section 4 of the National Security Act 2023, external â namely entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK.

RAF Molesworth is home to the US's intelligence operations centres for Europe and Africa, as well as a Nato intelligence hub.

It is not used as a flying station.

News.title: Three sisters who drowned in sea off Brighton took own lives, inquest finds
News.content:
Three sisters who drowned in the sea off Brighton took their own lives, a coroner has ruled.

Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, had been living "very secluded lives" following the death of their mother, who drowned in 2010, senior coroner Penelope Schofield said.

On 11 May, the women - who had all been living together in Greenford, London - visited an area of Birmingham close to where their mother died before travelling the next day to Brighton beach, where they drowned in adverse sea conditions in the early hours of 13 May. The coroner said they could not swim.

Their father Joseph Jacobsen said it was heartbreaking to lose "all three of my precious daughters".

He was among family members who followed proceedings via video link.

In an emotional statement read out on his behalf, he said he watched his daughters grow from little girls to beautiful, intelligent women "with a special place in my heart".

He said: "There are no words that can adequately express the pain of losing a child.

"To lose all three of my precious daughters is a heartbreak beyond anything I could ever have imagined."

He could not understand why his daughters' lives ended so suddenly, and hoped they were reunited with their mother "in God's eternal care", he added.

If you are experiencing emotional stress, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line here.

The coroner told the court: "These three sisters lived very secluded lives, they were incredibly private, we don't know why they took this course of action or indeed why they chose to do it in Brighton.

"It is not for the court to speculate and sadly these reasons may never be known."

News.title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia
News.content:
A junior Royal Navy sailor accused of preparing to spy for Russia has appeared in court.

Able Seaman Teddy Young, who specialised in warfare intelligence, allegedly retained UK defence and intelligence material that he had access to and made preparations to disclose sensitive information, a court was told.

The 24-year-old appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday after being charged under the National Security Act.

The BBC understands that the allegations against Young include translating a message into Russian and looking for a web portal that invited people to submit information to Russia.

Wearing a police-issue grey sweatshirt, Young spoke in court to confirm his name, date of birth and his address in Clapham, near Bedford.

He is formally charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for disclosing protected information, and obtaining, copying, recording or retaining protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power.

The charges cover a period between 26 November 2024 and 21 May 2025.

"The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power," the Crown Prosecution Service told the court in a written summary of the allegations.

Police said the alleged offences were not related to the recent RAF Fairford incident that resulted in a number of arrests after suspicious activity was reported near the base.

In total, seven men have been arrested and later released on bail in connection with the incident, which is being investigated by counter-terror police.

Young was arrested at his home address in Bedfordshire on Tuesday.

He is the first member of the armed forces to be charged under the new National Security Act 2023.

Cdr Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces.

"We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter."

A Royal Navy spokesperson confirmed a service member had been charged and added: "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

Judge Annabel Pilling remanded Young in custody. He will next appear at the Old Bailey on 16 October.

News.title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings
News.content:
Assistant coroner Briony Ballard listened to evidence at London Inner South Coroner's Court before publishing a narrative conclusion on Mia's death.

In a statement read after the conclusion of the inquest, Mia's parents Adrian St Hilaire and Chanel Spence said families with food allergies should not be "at risk" when eating out.

"We hope that lessons will be learned from Mia's death and that changes will be made to prevent other families enduring the devastation that we now have to live with," they said.

"Consumers rely on food hygiene ratings when deciding where it is safe to eat, but they do not tell us anything about the way a food business runs allergy management systems.

"There should be a separate, clearly displayed rating dedicated to the allergy management, like the food hygiene rating.

"This would mean that people with allergies could make more informed choices about where they eat."

Natasha's Foundation founder Tanya Ednan-Laperouse, whose daughter died aged 15 from an allergy to sesame in a Pret A Manger baguette, said allergies were "a serious, unpredictable medical condition".

"The inquest into Mia's death illustrates just how far we still have to go to improve awareness, understanding and regulation of food allergies," she said.

"Natasha's Foundation is working hard with business, schools, communities and the government to increase awareness and understanding of food allergies to try to prevent other families from having to go through the terrible loss that Mia's family endure."

Rebecca Sudworth, director of food policy at the Food Standards Agency, said her "deepest sympathies" were with Mia's family.

"Food businesses must take allergen risks seriously, every time," she said. "People have the right to know exactly what is in their food and drink, and it is a business's legal duty to provide accurate allergen information.

"We recently produced new guidance for businesses to make sure they understand their responsibilities to inform consumers about allergens, including the risk of cross-contact, and we are keeping this policy under review. We also have free allergy training and practical tools that businesses can use."

News.title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows in England
News.content:
There are "ominous signs" that winter pressures are already affecting the NHS in England, according to senior health leaders.

The warning comes as new data reveals the waiting list for routine hospital treatment in England rose for the second month in a row.

An estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.

The numbers are the highest since October 2025 and have raised questions over whether the NHS will meet a government target of treating 92% of patients within 18 weeks by 2029.

The rise in waiting lists comes despite the NHS in England delivering what were described as record levels of planned, elective care over the summer, while demand for services also reached its highest level ever.

A record 4.7 million planned treatments, procedures and appointments occurred across June, July and August â more than in any previous summer.

But both A&Es and ambulance services also saw a record number of patients for the month of September.

NHS England's national medical director, Professor Frankie Swords, warned that despite the progress delivered by frontline teams, winter pressure was already building.

"Staff are already seeing the ominous early signs of pressure, with more patients coming to A&E with flu and other respiratory viruses than usual for this time of year, and unfortunately many people are still waiting longer than we would like them to," she said.

News.title: Forty-five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable
News.content:
Police Scotland has said 45 serving officers are currently suspended over allegations of violence against women and girls.

Chief constable Jo Farrell said she expected more would face sanctions over their behaviour following a spate of former officers being convicted for sexual offences.

Farrell said a review into the handling of the case surrounding officer Alan Greer â who was exposed as a serial rapist after taking his own life â was under way.

She added about 8,000 members of staff were still to be "re-vetted" for their roles after a change in regulations earlier this year.

First minister John Swinney said he had "full confidence" in Police Scotland and the renewed vetting process.

In an interview with BBC Scotland News, Farrell described the scale of violence against women and girls in Scotland as an "epidemic", and that police forces were not immune to the problem.

She said: "We've got in the order of between currently 40 and 50 people currently suspended, so not at work, who are being investigated for offences that relate to violence against women and girls.

"Those investigations are at various stages."

News.title: Harry says he 'slipped into depression' after leaving UK
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex has said he "slipped into depression for about two weeks" after relocating to Canada in 2019 ahead of his move to the US.

Prince Harry, who recently returned to the UK with his wife Meghan and their two children, said he had originally left the country to "get some space."

The duke also discussed feeling "emotionally numb" after the death of his mother Diana, Princess of Wales, because he felt "disloyal and guilty for the possibility of being happy and joyful without her".

He opened up about his mental health with a neuroscientist in a session for a video learning platform.

He and his brother, the Prince of Wales, have previously been candid about their mental health struggles, including over their mother's death, and both are involved in mental health charities.

Prince Harry, who stepped back from royal duties to move to California with Meghan, made the latest comments as part of a paid-for online masterclass on dealing with grief.

"Being in Canada, away from the stressful environment where presumably my body was just pumped full of adrenaline, within two or three days, I experienced this adrenaline crash, something that I'd never experienced before," he recalled.

"It was as if I needed stress in order to get the adrenaline to make my brain function because I became useless around the house.

"I actually slipped into depression for about two weeks and I felt like I couldn't function without adrenaline."

News.title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
News.content:
Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth are now in the hands of criminals.

One victim told the BBC it was "very unsettling" that the hackers now know these things about her.

The criminals also have access to the searches customers have made on the website. Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.

Harriet has been using Asos since 2019 - another detail the hackers now know.

"What I find particularly worrying is the possibility that stolen data can be used as a tool for for future attacks, meaning the impact of a breach could extend well beyond the initial incident," she said.

With the stolen information, scammers may be able to create convincing phishing attack emails or phone calls.

The risk to individuals is now higher and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.

In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.

"Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.

"We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call."

The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.

News.title: Birmingham Airport announces £2bn expansion
News.content:
Birmingham Airport has announced a Â£2bn expansion plan which bosses say could more than double passenger numbers and create thousands of jobs.

The draft plan, a spokesperson said, sets out the use of existing runway capacity alongside "significantly enhanced" passenger facilities over the next 15 years.

Unveiling an eight-week public consultation, chief executive Nick Barton said the scheme aims to ensure the airport was "ready for the future" but needed a "fair and stable taxation environment".

Transport secretary Heidi Alexander said the government was "backing our aviation sector to continue growing, right across the country".

In 2025, the airport said it had seen a record year with more than 13 million passengers travelling through it. Bosses want to see this rise by more than double, up to 30 million a year.

Airport chiefs said the proposals set out a "clear commitment" to continue serving the region and create more than 50,000 jobs, including 3,800 at the airport site.

They added that they wanted to make sure the growth was "delivered responsibly and sustainably" for the people living closes to the site.

The first stage of development could start in 2027, with significant investments in areas such as baggage and terminal facilities, additional aircraft stands and improvements in surface access.

Hundreds of passengers were affected by issues with the airport's baggage system in August, with many left without their luggage.

People can give feedback on the plans online, by post or attend any of the 20 events, which start in Hampton on Arden on 16 October, external.

News.title: E-bike battery in fatal fire had repairs - inquest
News.content:
An e-bike battery linked to a fire which killed a mother and two children had issues prior to the blaze, an inquest has heard.

Gemma Germeney, 31, and children Lilly, eight, and Oliver, four, lost their lives in the fire on Sackville Close in Cambridge on 30 June 2023. The children's father, Scott Peden, survived.

Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service said at the time the most probable cause of the fire was an e-bike that was charging.

Scott Peden told the inquest he had bought a replacement battery after the previous one had been stolen and the bike later cut out, and had visited a repairman twice for work done.

Peden told the inquest he had purchased the bike online for Â£900 and it was in "perfect working order", apart from an incident where he lost the key on a fairground ride.

He said the battery was stolen a few months later and they researched a new one, but it would have been "quite a lot of money and I couldn't afford it at the time".

News.title: Woman told PC 'get off me' 300 times as he raped her
News.content:
A woman told a police officer to "get off me" more than 300 times as he subjected her to an 82-minute violent rape in a Liverpool hotel room.

Former Merseyside Police constable Ryan Theaker, 30, was secretly recorded by the victim after a night out in 2023.

The woman, who cannot be named to protect her anonymity, read an emotional statement at Liverpool Crown Court and faced the dock as she told Theaker "monsters never win".

He was designated a "dangerous" offender by a judge and jailed for 11 years with an extended five-year licence period.

Warning: This story contains distressing details of sexual violence.

Theaker, from Park Lane in Netherton, had been convicted of rape, sexual assault and assault by penetration after a trial last month.

Gareth Roberts, prosecuting, said the audio recordings captured Theaker demanding the woman let him take naked pictures of her, despite her saying she did not want him to.

He also assaulted her with sex toys he had brought to the hotel, the court heard.

News.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
News.content:
Most diplomats will leave the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, Israel says, but the UK insists the building "will not be closing" and will operate as a "UK Mission".

"We did not want it to come to this," Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar wrote on social media, as he said 20 diplomats and the consul general would leave while a task force of seven could remain in the building "with a very limited scope of activity".

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responded that some staff had been "temporarily withdrawn" for security reasons, and stressed the mission would continue "our work with the Palestinian people".

Israel said in September it would shut the consulate in retaliation for UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, which are illegal under international law.

The new steps appear to prevent the diplomatic row between two allies from escalating further.

The British consulate, which was founded in 1838, handles UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza.

It is distinct from the UK embassy in Tel Aviv, which is the UK's main diplomatic hub with Israel and is not affected.

Israel's foreign minister said it had implemented the order to shut the consulate within 30 days, which was one of a series of measures announced on 8 September in response to the UK's sanctions.

"The British Consulate in Jerusalem is closing its operations today. Accordingly, the sign of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed," Saar posted on X.

However, the British flag could still be seen outside on Thursday morning, and several staff were seen entering the building.

Saar said talks with the UK government had resulted in agreement on certain principles, including that "the consul general and 20 diplomats (including the consul general) are ending their duties and will leave Israel".

But he acknowledged that the building was "the property of the British government" and said Israel had authorised "a task force of only seven diplomats with a very limited scope of activity" to operate from there.

As a result of this agreement with the UK, he said, "no steps will be taken against Israel".

Israeli media had reported earlier this week that the UK was threatening to expel Israeli diplomats from London.

This agreement is a compromise of sorts and means - for the moment - the heat has been taken out of a dispute that could have further worsened UK-Israel relations.

Israel can claim that the British consulate is "closing its operations". A score of British diplomats, including the consul general, are leaving Jerusalem.

But Miliband said they were going only temporarily and only for their safety and security.

He also insisted that Israel had no legal right to close the consulate.

"The UK government reiterates its long-standing view that East Jerusalem is occupied territory," the foreign secretary wrote in a statement.

Following discussions with the Israeli government, he said, the building would "not be closing" and would be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem.

However, Miliband said an understanding had not been reached on "necessary assurances for the security and protections of our staff and premises".

"Accordingly the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security," he added.

"We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence, and we will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible."

He said the seven UK diplomats remaining in Jerusalem would be "independent and operational" and would "continue to deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people".

News.title: Body found in Colombia in search for missing Anton Green
News.content:
The family of a British man missing in Colombia have been told a body has been found in the search for him.

Anton Green from Manchester had been living in the South American country for two-and-a-half years, but stopped responding to messages in August.

Earlier, his family in Whalley Range were told that a body had been discovered, and that it was believed to be the 43-year-old.

They told the BBC that the news - which came just hours after they had renewed their appeal for help finding him - had devastated them and that they were "trying to come to terms with what's happened".

A Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) spokesman confirmed that the body of a British man had been found in Colombia.

News.title: UK and Germany will face threats together, says Burnham in Berlin
News.content:
The UK and Germany will face threats together, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said as he reaffirmed a series of defence and security partnerships.

On his first official European trip, apart from visits to Ukraine, Burnham met German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and was greeted with military honours in Berlin.

Speaking to reporters at the German capital's Federal Chancellery, the prime minister said both countries were facing hybrid attacks "on a regular basis" and "it makes sense" to take them on together.

The pair formally ratified the 2025 Kensington Treaty, a partnership committing both countries to tackle hostile activity.

Burnham said the treaty would "improve our security here in Europe" but also help grow the economy and living standards.

"The Kensington Treaty [is] the first treaty between Germany and the UK since the Second World War - it really is a significant moment," he said.

He added that the UK government would now "seek to progress" Germany joining Gcap, the Global Combat Air Programme led by Italy, Japan and the UK to develop a next-generation fighter aircraft.

He outlined partnerships "countering hybrid attacks" and "countering interference in our democratic processes".

He mentioned collaboration on quantum technology and space, adding he was aiming to host the first joint meeting of the UK and German cabinets next year.

The Berlin talks come after intelligence services warned of rising threats, including last month when Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

News.title: 45 serving officers suspended from major police force over alleged violence against women and girls
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Some 45 serving officers from a major police force are currently suspended over allegations of violence against women and girls.

The officers, from Police Scotland, are currently being investigated over the alleged offences, chief constable Jo Farrell told the BBC.

She said she is expecting to see more officers face sanctions.

Ms Farrell added that 8,000 officers are still to be revetted for their roles following a change in regulations introduced earlier this year.

She said: “We’ve got in the order of between 40 and 50 people currently suspended, so not at work, who are being investigated for offences that relate to violence against women and girls.

“Those investigations are at various stages.”

She added: “My focus is on identifying where there is wrongdoing, criminality, particularly in relation to violence against women and girls, and if that has been committed by our officers and our staff, that we identify it and we ensure that those people feel the full force of the law.”

open image in gallery Chief constable Jo Farrell said 8,000 officers are still to be revetted for their roles ( Andrew Milligan/PA )

The news comes in a year that has seen a number of high-profile cases of police officers being charged or convicted in relation to sexual assaults.

Alan Greer, a long-serving police officer, took his own life aged 47 in May this year after being arrested in connection with allegations he raped a woman in her home in 2012.

He is now being investigated over violent sex offences and attempted murder against multiple women.

In September, retired officer Campbell Petrie was convicted of nine charges, including two of rape, committed over a 17-year period while he was a serving officer.

A third officer, Cameron Ross, was jailed for 10 years in July after being found guilty of raping two women and abusing a third in the Highlands and Western Isles.

open image in gallery The news comes in a year that has seen a number of high-profile cases of police officers being charged or convicted in relation to sexual assaults ( PA )

Craig Naylor, chief inspector at HM Inspectorate of Constabulary in Scotland, said it is “absolutely abhorrent” that some officers abuse their power and break the law.

“We put trust and faith in police officers to uphold the law to keep us safe,” he said.

“And when a police officer is alleged to have broken that law and broken that trust, then there’s got to be a really effective investigation.

“The people (Police Scotland) put in to investigate police officers are skilled, they’re experienced, and they are expected to do a thorough and rigorous investigation, and to root out those who are a danger to the public or to their colleagues.”

He also said victims are at the “heart” of any investigation into wrongdoing by officers, and that the “main focus” has to be on supporting and encouraging them to come forward.

He added: “I joined policing to make society better for everyone within it and I find it absolutely abhorrent when I hear of a police officer breaking the law and of abusing their position of power, which is what they have within the community.

“So, I want them rooted out. I want them kicked out of the organisation. And, if it’s appropriate, for them to face the full might of the law and to serve time in prison, if that’s an appropriate outcome.”

News.title: Costco’s new dessert is convincing people to sign up for memberships: ‘You got me’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Costco is breaking out sweet treats that fans are willing to pay a yearly membership for.

The warehouse chain is known to sell classic bakery items like croissants and sheet cakes, but is now trying out new pastry recipes that have left shoppers raving online.

After the beloved Blueberry Caramelized Cheesecake Croissants became popular last year, the wholesale store has now released its latest endeavor: the Kirkland Signature Lemon Cream Caramelized Croissant.

The lemon dessert is exactly what its name describes: flaky dough and a lemon filling baked into a crispy pastry. But these treats are baked in a round paper liner and get their name, in part, due to sugar at the bottom of the liner that caramelizes while in the oven.

Influencer Laura Jayne Lamb, who has amassed more than three million Instagram followers for her Costco-related content, said it is “one of the best things the Costco bakery has ever done,” adding, “The outside is crisp, buttery, and caramelized, and the middle has this soft tangy lemon cream that balances it out perfectly.”

In the comments of Lamb’s video reviewing the new treat, which costs $12.99 for half a dozen, fans were eager to get their hands on the croissant. “Do I have a membership? No, am I gonna buy one JUST FOR THIS? Maybe,” one person wrote, referencing the store’s $65 annual fee.

“Ok Costco…you got me..I’m gonna get a membership. Idc anymore that I have to drive over an hr to get there and over an hr back,” another person commented. A third added, “Say less I’ll be there tomorrow.”

Other Costco shoppers were excited to see a variation of the fan-favorite blueberry pastries. “The blueberry ones were so good I can only imagine how delicious this will be. Must try!” one person wrote on TikTok.

“The blueberry ones were delish and lemon is one of my favorite flavors…problem is I’ll eat them all myself,” another customer admitted.

Costco is putting out a new pastry ( Getty )

The croissants are rolling out to Costco locations across the U.S., and shoppers can call their local store to see when they will hit shelves.

Costco has not released any information about how long the pastries will remain available, and did not immediately return The Independent’s request for comment.

It comes months after Costco began selling buttermilk biscuits in its bakery section. A 10-count box costs around $6.99, depending on location, and is still available for purchase in many stores.

However, the lemon croissants have been met with more excitement than the butter biscuits, which shoppers criticized online as being dry to the taste.

News.title: Trump finally clarifies his ‘take out’ LA comment after three days of uproar
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump insisted Thursday that he never invited Iran to bomb Los Angeles and San Diego, three days after telling a rally crowd in Nebraska to "let them take out" both cities while defending his war, which has pushed gasoline past $4.40 a gallon.

"The Fake and Artificial News is out there trying to say that I'm inviting the enemy to bomb San Diego and Los Angeles when, in actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"All I was doing was making a comparison between paying a little more, for a short time, for Gasoline, versus the bombing of our Major Cities.”

The president then claimed that “everybody knew” what he’d meant and accused news outlets of continuing “to go out and say that I am asking the enemy to bomb two Cities that I love” while calling journalists who covered the incendiary comments “degenerates.”

Trump’s post was a tardy attempt to walk back what was widely interpreted at the time as a verbal swipe at anti-war Democrats and Republicans who he has falsely accused of being in favor of Tehran’s pursuit of nuclear weapons.

Trump had suggested Iran could attack two California cities with nuclear weapons while trying to justify the war he started eight months ago ( Reuters )

Speaking in Grand Island, Nebraska in support of GOP Senator Pete Ricketts, Trump said higher gas prices that have roiled his party’s approval ratings were worth bearing because Iran “could take out a city.”

“Let them take out Los Angeles; let them take out San Diego.” he said, as the partisan crowd booed at the mention of both California cities.

He repeated similar comments during a Wednesday rally in support of Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton.

"You want to see trauma? You want to see problems? And I said it the other day. Let them hit a missile into San Diego or Los Angeles. You want to see a horror show? Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles if you want to see some bad things happen,” Trump said.

Only then did he add the caveat that Thursday's post treats as having been obvious all along: "We're not gonna let that happen. We protect our cities; we protect our country."

In the days following the unhinged remarks ,the president's own staff had tried to close the matter without him even as he ducked reporter questions on the matter.

White House communications director Steven Cheung dismissed the reaction as a "media freakout" that was "not rooted in reality," writing on X that Trump "was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped."

That staff-led cleanup effort did little to quiet California's leaders.

"After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego," Gov. Gavin Newsom wrote. "He is deranged and dangerous."

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass put it more plainly, writing on X that Trump had “suggested that a foreign government attack Los Angeles."

News.title: It’s unclear what Trump does and doesn’t know anymore. His Texas rally exposed that dilemma
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

When you’re a Republican president a month out from the midterms and you have to campaign in Texas, you know something’s gone awry. Or at least, you should. But it’s unclear what Donald Trump does and doesn’t know any more.

At a rally in San Antonio on Wednesday night, the president tossed out the usual insults at James Talarico — the man who polls show might be about to become the first Democrat to win statewide in Texas in over 30 years — and then directly threatened the people who might vote for him. He also told some odd, meandering stories about veganism and his wife Melania, during which he (presumably) mistakenly said that Melania calls him “sir.”

After a long rant intended to attack Talarico’s masculinity — he doesn’t eat manly, manly meat! He’s not as masculine as Trump, a man who wants to kill people by firing squad! He’s a “weak, gutless, self-hating, transgender-promoting freak show”! — Trump added that his wife had corrected him on the pronunciation of vegan (central to his claims about Talarico are that he’s a closeted vegan who only talks about liking ribs to get votes.) “You know, my wife, she told me, ‘Sir, it’s not vay-gan, it’s vee-gan,’” he said. Because of course, someone like Donald is so masculine he wouldn’t even know how to say the word.

Puzzling, indeed, the idea that Melania might call her husband “sir.” And it was a small slip-up in the grand scheme of things — there were some stranger ones in the Oval Office the day before — but it was telling. Because Trump seems to be losing his train of thought halfway through a sentence a lot these days, and the fact that he didn’t seem to realize he’d mashed together an anecdote about his wife and one of his lackeys in the space of a few seconds isn’t encouraging. Then again, perhaps he just likes being called “sir” in all areas of his life.

Trump’s insults used to hit hard, but now they’re getting a little half-baked. His repeated assertions during the rally that Talarico goes behind a tent to throw up after eating barbecue during campaign events were silly and desperate. And even though the “you ain’t man enough” stuff in Texas is a favorite of Republicans, it hasn’t been doing much to move to polls in Republican Ken Paxton’s favor.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump also suggested that at his Ken Paxton rally in Texas Wednesday night that James Talarico had become ill after eating too much meat, alleging that the Democrat is a vegan despite him previously denying that he followed a plant-based diet ( Getty )

While the Paxton campaign has been running ads that claim Talarico is “too low-T for Texas” and promoting an old clip of Talarico saying God is non-binary, Talarico’s single-note response — that this is all just a distraction to cover up Republican “corruption” — seems to have been more convincing to Texans. He has shrugged off attacks, called his own past comments “cringey,” and witheringly said that people of his age don’t really worry about having low testosterone. Meanwhile, pretty much every poll — including Fox News — shows Talarico in the lead.

To make matters worse, Trump has been calling for a public debate between Talarico and Paxton. That might be a clever move, if Paxton wasn’t the least charismatic man who’s ever been seen at a podium.

If the rage-baity, chest-beating, Trump rally-style campaigning has run its course in red Texas, this is bad news for MAGA Republicans across the country. And indeed, the San Antonio rally had an unusual amount of protesters, noticeable enough to make Trump stand back from the mic at one point and numerous enough that police escorts had to be called on twelve occasions. That kind of regular interruption really puts a dampener on a rally.

San Antonio is a majority Hispanic city and a working-class city, and these are two intersecting demographics where Trump won big in 2024. But now his support is bottoming out among Hispanic voters, especially working-class ones, driven by concerns about the economy and immigration. Those concerns weren’t going to dissipate by seeing the president stand next to a bunch of flags and make jokes about Talarico barfing barbecue. Who cares about whether your candidate eats “a little bit of lettuce” when your gas prices are through the roof?

Trump’s attack line on the Democrats in general — that there’ll “be a depression” if they get in and they’ll “destroy the economy,” which relies on people entering into his delusion that the economy is doing just fine and attacking Iran was worth it — is also unfathomably weak. And his threatening claim at the San Antonio rally that he will “never forgive you” if you vote for Talarico doesn’t do much to move the needle, either.

Yes, we’ve watched Trump exact petty revenge against people in his social and political circles over the past few years, but what does “never forgiving” Texans even look like for a man in the final two years of his final presidential term? Nothing very consequential, that’s for sure.

open image in gallery While the Paxton campaign has run ads that claim Texas state Rep. James Talarico is “too low-T for Texas” and promoting an old clip of Talarico saying God is non-binary, Talarico’s single-note response — that this is all just a distraction to cover up Republican “corruption” — seems to have been more convincing to Texans. ( AP )

open image in gallery Texas AG Ken Paxton has been trashing President Donald Trump’s war in Iran and the consequent high consumer and gas prices in private conversations but would have lost the primary to Sen. John Cornyn had Trump not wanted to get back at the incumbent ( AFP/Getty )

Halfway through Wednesday’s rally, the president also repeated his claim that he will give every American citizen $5,000 if the Republicans hold the House and the Senate after the midterms. He claimed that this is something he can do because the economy is doing so well, but of course, it’s really a tacit admission that people are suffering under untenable cost-of-living conditions right now. It’s also generally a bad look to brazenly offer bribes for votes at the podium. Ethics aside, and whether or not your supporters cheer the idea, it can’t help but make you look weak.

And yet Trump’s plan to personally campaign throughout the country — possibly every day until the midterms, according to what we’ve heard from Susie Wiles — is based on his idea that he is so popular he can turn the numbers around for some Republican candidates who are floundering. He’s told people to imagine it’s him on the ballot when they go vote. And he seems pathologically incapable of considering that that is what people are already imagining, and perhaps why Republicans across the country aren’t polling very well.

When you turn up to try and save the show as the most unpopular member of it, you really need to have something better to say than that you’ve just approved a firing squad execution. Even the most ardent supporter of Second Amendment rights isn’t going to change their vote based on that. You should consider that perhaps the people of Texas don’t care that much about veganism and they don’t actually even care that much about transgender scaremongering.

If you decide to go ahead with all of these because you simply can’t help yourself, then you really, really should at least remember, if you want to keep any of those female voters who quietly broke for you last time, that your wife doesn’t call you “sir”.

News.title: Man fowls around and finds out while sneaking 10 birds through Florida airport in his pants
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in
