Read our Privacy notice

A man has been arrested after allegedly sneaking 10 exotic birds through a Florida airport in his pants, according to federal authorities.

Alberto Hernandez Castillo, a Cuban native and permanent legal U.S. resident, was going through Miami International Airport on Sunday when authorities flagged him for a secondary inspection, according to a Homeland Security Investigations complaint obtained by several local news outlets.

Hernandez Castillo, who traveled to Miami from Havana, allegedly indicated on a signed Customs Entry Declaration that he did not bring any animals or wildlife — but an unexplained bulge near his waist gave him away, according to the complaint.

During a pat-down, authorities allegedly found six plastic tubes sewn into his underwear that contained eight yellow-faced grassquits and two blue grosbeaks.

The two species are typically sold in the illegal pet trade, according to reports. All 10 birds were found alive.

open image in gallery Alberto Hernandez Castillo, a Cuban native and permanent legal U.S. resident, has been arrested after sneaking 10 exotic birds through a Florida airport in his pants, according to federal authorities ( U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida )

open image in gallery During a pat-down, authorities allegedly found six plastic tubes sewn into his underwear that contained eight yellow-faced grassquits and two blue grosbeaks ( U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida )

Yellow-faced grassquits are grayish-green birds found from southeastern Mexico to northern South America. The birds can also be found throughout the Greater Antilles, of which Cuba is part.

Blue grosbeaks, which can often be seen singing while perched atop trees and power lines, can also be found in Mexico, Central America, and the Greater Antilles, as well as most of the U.S.

After Hernandez Castillo was busted, he allegedly told authorities the birds were for his “personal use,” according to the complaint.

Authorities reportedly determined he did not have the proper documentation or required clearance from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for importing the birds, and he was taken into custody.

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service told The Independent its Office of Law Enforcement was investigating the incident, adding, “Per our policy we do not comment on open investigations”.

Hernandez Castillo was later released on a $25,000 personal surety bond, according to records reviewed by People. He is set to be arraigned on October 26.

News.title: Hayden Panettiere's ex Wladimir Klitschko gets legal status to protect their daughter's inheritance
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Actor Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancée, former boxer Wladimir Klitschko, was granted legal authority by a California court Thursday to protect Panettiere's property for their 11-year-old daughter after the television star's accidental overdose death left the girl as her sole heir.

Klitschko had filed the urgent petition last week, saying that pieces of Panettiere's property were being taken by federal law enforcement agents investigating her death and by an unnamed nonfamily member looking to sell them, with no one in a position to try to recover them for her daughter.

Klitschko, a Ukrainian former world champion boxer, has had full custody of the girl, Kaya, for most of her life, and she has lived with him in Ukraine. The father and daughter appeared in Los Angeles County court remotely via videoconference. They spoke only to introduce themselves at the brief hearing with only Kaya visible on camera, sitting at a table in front of curtains.

Judge Stephanie Santoro granted Klitschko the status of temporary guardian of Kaya's estate until a long-term administrator can be appointed.

Santoro asked Klitschko's lawyer, Diane Park, why the matter was urgent. Park said they believed a person described only as a nonrelative had taken items after Panettiere's death and had tried to sell some of her jewelry at a pawn shop. And she said assets were in danger of going unaccounted for during the death investigation. Court documents said authority was needed to deal with both the pawnshop owner and police agencies. Panettiere’s taxes also need to be filed this month, the lawyer said. Santoro, satisfied with the explanation, approved the move.

Panettiere, the former star of the TV series “Heroes” and “Nashville,” was pronounced dead in an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on Aug. 16 at age 36 after paramedics found her unresponsive. A coroner’s report obtained by The Associated Press said her death was from an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl. She had been in rehab just weeks before. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the home.

Park told Santoro that the property, the pawnshop and the nonfamily member were in Los Angeles County, where the judge's ruling held authority. Park declined to comment outside the courtroom.

Klitschko's Sept. 24 petition emphasized that his intention is solely to protect his daughter’s future assets until a permanent administrator can be put in place.

“There is a high probability that property belonging to Hayden’s Estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated," the document said.

The filing says that before her death, Panettiere and Klitschko hired security to protect her home because an unnamed person had gained unauthorized access, and it's expected the same person would continue to try to “misappropriate” her property.

Panettiere's mother, Lesley Vogel, filed a document saying she consented to Klitschko being appointed.

Klitschko, 50, an Olympic gold medalist, held several heavyweight titles between 2000 and 2015. He and Panettiere began dating in 2009 and got engaged in 2013.

His older brother Vitali, also a former champion boxer, is mayor of Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital. The two brothers, sons of a Soviet major general, have been prominent public figures in Ukraine during its war with Russia.

In her memoir released earlier this year, Panettiere acknowledged being addicted to alcohol and having postpartum depression after her daughter's birth in 2014. Kaya went to live with Klitschko full-time when she was 2. Panettiere's father told investigators that when she died she had plans to visit her daughter in Ukraine days later.

News.title: Here’s who will get a payout from the $15M Cash App settlement
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Cash App users who had claims approved in a $15 million class-action settlement could receive payments this month.

Payments are scheduled for October, according to the official Cash App security settlement website.

Cash App is a mobile platform for sending, saving and investing money. The settlement stems from a lawsuit accusing the app and parent company Block Inc. of failing to adequately protect customers’ information following two security incidents.

In 2022, a former Cash App Investing employee allegedly accessed customer information without authorization. In 2023, an unauthorized access incident involved accounts connected to recycled phone numbers. Block and Cash App dispute the allegations and deny any wrongdoing but agreed to settle.

Current and former Cash App users whose accounts or personal information were accessed without permission, or who experienced fraudulent withdrawals, from August 23, 2018 to August 20, 2024, were eligible to file claims.

open image in gallery The settlement stems from two security incidents in 2022 and 2023 involving unauthorized access to Cash App customer account information ( Getty Images for Alex Wang )

The deadline to file a claim was November 18, 2024, and new claims are no longer being accepted.

Approved claimants can receive up to $2,500 for documented out-of-pocket losses related to the incidents, including certain bank fees and credit-related costs. They may also receive compensation for up to three hours of lost time at $25 per hour.

Not every claimant will receive the maximum amount. Payments will depend on approved claims and the terms of the settlement, which established a $15 million fund for eligible users.

A federal court granted final approval to the settlement on March 27, 2025.

The Cash App settlement is separate from other legal actions involving Block, including a $45 million multi-state settlement and federal enforcement actions related to fraud protections and customer service.

Approved claimants can find payment updates and other information on the official settlement website.

The Independent has contacted Cash App for comment.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

News.title: From Yale to the Congo: The mathematician who became one of Africa’s most intrepid reporters
News.content:
Sundaram has a lot of experience with the Rwandan methods of control. After spending 17 months in DRC, he moved to Kigali and he is eloquent about the convoluted effects of dictatorship. “Living in Rwanda taught me so much about how dictatorships function internally and how counter-intuitive they can be. A friend of mine who was working in public health told me ‘When we ask people in India to wash their hands we get a 30 per cent success rate from a campaign, but when we need people in Rwanda to wash their hands, we just need to slip a line in one of Kagame’s speeches and we get a 90 per cent success rate. That’s fantastic isn’t it?’

“And I said, ‘well is it? It’s great for short term health outcomes but what does that say about society? Isn’t democracy about people choosing freely? What if the government tells them to do something bad – like what happened in the genocide when people were told to kill all the Tutsis?’

“Kagame and his army stopped the genocide, and he has restored peace, but he governs using the same system that was used to perpetrate the genocide.”

In Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship, the book Sundaram went on to write about his time in Rwanda teaching journalists, he describes a more extreme version of this phenomenon, recalling how Kagame once commented that thatched roofs on huts were primitive. “And the local authorities took that as a sign that he didn’t like thatched roofs, and that they should get rid of them. And without replacements being built, people climbed up and dismantled their own thatched roofs. And I saw these villages with houses which just had mud walls without roofs, and the families were sitting outside with their children and their goats, the thatch strewn on the ground. In the rain, quite often. The children would get sick, and it was like a war zone.

“At the end of my time in Congo, I was at a UN base and they were digging latrines, when they found some human bones. They stopped digging and alerted the press, and I happened to be in Goma nearby.” He subsequently found out that it was one of a series of mass graves containing the bodies of Congolese killed by forces controlled by Kagame. “And so when I arrived I had a sense of what Rwanda had done in Congo, but I didn’t fully appreciate the extent to which it was totalitarian. I’d heard that the country was a shining example of progress – aid programs were successful, and poverty reduction programs. The streets were clean, public services functioned. I was living in a nice house with a big garden provided by the journalism programme I was working in.”

Many European governments, including Britain, are enamoured with Rwanda, because, says Sundaram, “dictatorships can be very efficient”. But it is a “mirage of a country”, he says.

The teaching programme he was running was briefed not to challenge the government on any level, and an embassy official told him that if any of the journalists mentioned repression they would be expelled.

“Layer by layer, as I began to talk to the journalists I was training, the true story unravelled. The first instance was when one of them left the programme, and I heard him on the radio one day praising the president, but with a degree of flattery that was completely exaggerated, and I didn’t understand why. The rest of the class were reluctant to talk about it but eventually I learned that another student had been beaten to a coma on the day he criticised the president.

“I started to realise that my class contained some of the most courageous journalists in the country.” As a foreigner, if he transgressed, Sundaram could have his visa cancelled or get kicked out, or even locked up for a couple of days, but for the Rwandan journalists, everything was at stake. They could be killed or their families threatened.

“But still they persisted, and they took me around the country and showed me all the things the government didn’t want anyone to see – things they couldn’t report on because it was too dangerous, so they wanted to show me because they wanted somebody to speak up. It’s really a book about them – they’ve been my greatest teachers in journalism.”

News.title: I tried Amazon’s new iPad rival – and there’s one standout feature
News.content:
Amazon says that this tablet has three times the computing power and nine times the graphics power of any previous Amazon tablet, so this is a significant boost in performance to previous models.

That will make light tasks, such as crunching through emails, browser-based activity like online shopping and document work. With a keyboard factored in, it could work as a laptop alternative for some. The same could be said of the iPad Air, although with recent price increases from Apple and the matte screen, for my money, this is a better proposition.

The premium makeover that comes with the Alexa Tablet Pro includes a slim aluminium design, with flattened edges, so it looks like an iPad or Samsung tablet, only 6.5mm thick. The Pro version only comes in the Graphite colour seen here. All models in the new line-up feel more grown-up and less like kid’s tablets than the Fire range. Plus the switch to proper Android over Fire OS is welcome and will result in better app compatibility (although I noticed that these tablets were running Android 16, which is now an old version).

It has a battery that’s good for 16 hours of video playback and supports 27W charging. There are cameras front and rear although like any tablet, these won’t be as good as your phone, while there’s support for Dolby Atmos from the speakers, so your movies will sound decent.

The AI capabilities are a step up

As the name suggests, Amazon is keen to promote the AI element here. It has customised the interface slightly with access to Alexa+ meaning you can utilise Amazon’s AI at any time to ask about what’s on the screen, to control smart home devices or search for content. If you are a keen Alexa user, then that will be a plus, but for me it’s not the headline news.

News.title: Kenyan authorities scramble to find passengers on Ebola flight
News.content:
Authorities are racing to track down passengers who boarded a flight from Uganda to Kenya on Saturday alongside a man infected with Ebola.

The man travelled by bus from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of an Ebola outbreak that has killed 4,000 people, to Kampala, Uganda. He then boarded a flight to Nairobi on Saturday, October 3, which was operated by the African airline Jambojet.

The patient went to a hospital in Nairobi and died just 48 hours later, meaning the journey took place in the final days of infection, the stage at which patients who die of the disease are most contagious. By October 6 authorities had tracked down 28 contacts, including family members of the deceased, but said they urgently needed to track down 23 passengers and crew who had travelled on the same flight.

The man is Kenya’s first ever case of the disease. Ebola does not typically spread through the air like Covid-19 or measles, requiring close contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person to spread. However, an aeroplane cabin significantly intensifies these risks because passengers share cramped spaces for prolonged periods and touch the same surfaces, such as a cabin toilet.

“We are working closely with the Ministry of Health, Port Health Services and other relevant authorities to support the ongoing public health response, including the identification and management of the other guests and crew who may have been in contact with the individual,” a spokesperson for Jambojet said on Tuesday.

After landing in Kenya, airport staff screened the patient, standard protocol for people travelling from at-risk countries during the current Ebola outbreak, but allowed him to continue his journey into Nairobi.

Kenya’s health ministry director-general, Patrick Amoth, said the patient may have passed through airport screening because medication had masked his symptoms.

News.title: Africa embraces ‘Go to Work on an Egg’ to boost maternal health and nutrition
News.content:
The sun is barely up when villagers start queuing for eggs at the metal gate of Shamim Haried’s home.

By noon, all that day’s supply is usually sold out, but people keep coming and asking if there are any left.

Demand is so high that arguments can break out in the queue, says the mother-of-two who lives outside Malawi’s capital, Lilongwe.

Her eggs are cheaper and fresher than those sold in the market.

“The people almost fight for eggs: it’s hard to watch,” she explains.

“Eggs are the cheapest healthy protein that they can get and it’s better for them to buy here than anywhere else.”

Her flock of 1,400 chickens lay around 1,000 eggs each day, but she reckons she could sell three times that.

News.title: What is pneumonic plague? Symptoms and how it spreads
News.content:
The death of a researcher at a plague laboratory in Siberia has prompted the World Health Organization to press Moscow for answers.

Russian officials have yet to share details of what caused the worker’s illness, and this information vacuum has fuelled speculation.

But what is the disease, and how much of a threat does it pose?

What is pneumonic plague?

Plague is a rare and serious infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, usually found in small mammals such as rodents and their fleas. Pneumonic plague is the most virulent of plague’s three forms, and is a severe infection of the lungs.

The other types are bubonic plague – the Black Death that laid waste to much of Europe during the Middle Ages – which attacks the lymph nodes, and septicaemic plague, which attacks the blood. Either can develop into the pneumonic form if the infection spreads.

Pneumonic plague is rarer than the bubonic form, but more dangerous.

Each year, the world records an estimated 1,000 to 3,000 plague cases of all types, though the number fluctuates.

Most cases are bubonic, and spread by the bite of an infected flea, and most occur in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of Congo. But infections are also found in countries including Russia, India, China and the United States.

Sports.title: ‘Didn’t give us anything’ – Benin boss slams Argentina for refusing to swap shirts or take pics after Messi’s final game
Sports.content:
Next

BENIN’s manager has accused Argentina of snubbing his players’ attempts to commemorate their part in Lionel Messi’s international swansong.

The Cheetahs were chosen as the final opponent of Messi’s historic Argentina career.



After Wednesday’s match, footage of the footie icon seemingly deliberately snubbing Benin players’ attempts to take a post-match selfie with him spread like wildfire on social media.

And manager Gernot Rohr has now claimed his troops were prevented from exchanging shirts with the opposition.



He said: “We are very happy to be part of history, especially for a football legend like Lionel Messi.

“And to play this match at the Monumental Stadium was an extraordinary adventure for my young players.

“The only downside was that the Argentinians gave our players nothing. Not even a photo of Messi.”

Rohr added: “We wanted to exchange jerseys, but we didn’t get a single one. They wouldn’t even let us into their tunnel (changing room).

“Security was turning everyone away. Some players were even bringing their jerseys to exchange with other players.

“We tried everything, but to no avail.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“However, I gave Messi’s 2018 shirt to coach [Lionel] Scaloni, who got him to sign it for me and then returned it to me, but that was all.

“He had me sign it and then gave it back to me. I waited half an hour, but it’s not a big deal.”

Argentina ran out 3-0 winners in an emotional night in Buenos Aires.

An emotional Messi called time on his international with a goal from the penalty spot.



After the match, he said: “It was a huge source of pride for me to defend this jersey for more than 20 years.

“Not coming anymore is going to be deeply painful.

“I swear I’d like to play for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you,”

Messi and the Argentine FA have yet to respond to Rohr’s claims.

Sports.title: Everton striker Martin Sherif admits to breaching FA betting rules and is handed major punishment by football chiefs
Sports.content:
Next

EVERTON star Martin Sherif has been fined £5,000 after he admitted breaching the FA’s betting rules.

The forward, 20, was found to have “caused, permitted or enabled” 61 bets on matches between November 20, 2024 and February 12, 2026.



Sherif did not place any of the bets himself, but they did come out of his bank accounts.

However, the commission said it was “difficult to accept” that he wasn’t aware of the bets.



The ruling found the player had “apologised and expressed remorse for his actions”.

It added he was 18 or 19 at the time and did not receive a financial benefit from the bets.

And Sherif was said to have been left “out of pocket” by them.

The verdict went on to say he had warned Everton youngsters about the dangers of betting and had closed his betting accounts.

An FA statement read: “Martin Sherif of Everton FC has been fined £5,000 for breaching The FA’s betting rules.

“The player admitted breaching FA Rule E1.2 by causing, permitting, or enabling 61 bets to be placed on football matches between 20 November 2024 and 12 February 2026.”



It went on to say: “Having considered all of the above factors, the Commission considered that a fine of £5,000, represents a fair and proportionate sanction for Mr Sherif’s conduct.

“The Commission considered that Mr Sherif’s conduct did not warrant a sporting sanction.”

Sherif was born in Liberia before joining Almere City as a youngster.

He moved to Everton aged 13 before being loaned out to Rotherham and Port Vale last season.



Sherif is yet to make a senior appearance for the Toffees under David Moyes.

He has represented the Netherlands at Under-17 level.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard breaks silence on Man City trophy fears after guilty verdict as he insists ‘titles should be in your head’
Sports.content:
Next

FRANK LAMPARD says Manchester City’s trophies will always “be in the players’ heads”.

Former City midfielder Lampard admits it would be “very hard” to take away any individual’s personal success during their years at the Etihad.



And he hinted players should not be the ones punished by the guilty verdict over financial breaches, which the club are in the process of appealing.

Lampard played for City during the 2014/15 season after collecting a string of trophies with Chelsea.



The club’s charges relate to a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

Asked if City’s trophies should be stripped from them during that period, Lampard said: “I’m not in those shoes. But I have titles and I don’t have them hanging on my wall at home – I have them in my head.



“Most players are competing against the best in the Premier League. A lot of things are out of control, but they’re still very difficult to win.

“So I think it would be very hard to take someone’s title away as a player individually. I think they should be in your head as opposed to in this beautiful glass cabinet. I know there are some who do that.”

After his season at City, Lampard then moved to the USA to play for New York City.

New York are owned by City Football Group, a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi United.

“Then Manchester City came along and it was a quick decision, I probably felt flattered to go to the champions and play for them.



“I got really well looked after – we played City a month ago and I saw lots of friendly faces. They was warm to me as they were during my time there.

“That continued in New York. To play for Chelsea for 13 years and when Roman Abramovich turned up and we had that squad, people said, ‘You bought the title’.

“But we had to beat Manchester United to win it – it’s high-level football. All you think about is: ‘Can we try and win something’.

“City have done it and now all this conversation will happen – I didn’t want to be part of that as a footballer.

The EFL and also docked them four points ahead of this season.



A separate FA investigation was then launched against Eckert, which was widely anticipated to result in a ban for the Southampton manager.

That leaves the 33-year-old free to take his place in the dugout when Southampton host south-coast rivals Portsmouth at St Mary’s Stadium on Sunday.

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca has issued a message after the club were found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules

Enzo Maresca has claimed the Manchester City hierarchy have the club's "complete trust" ahead of Sunday's Premier League trip to Liverpool, despite their guilty verdict.

‌



‌



On September 30, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

‌



City, however, have strongly denied any wrongdoing and lodged an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club insisted they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and say they have "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to back their position.

"Personally I'm very calm to be honest," Maresca told City's website. "The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side. The feeling is fantastic, to be honest. The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league.

"The players are just focused on that. They know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has Sir Alex Ferguson to thank for outrageous £20m-a-year Arsenal contract
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has Sir Alex Ferguson to thank for outrageous £20m-a-year Arsenal contract

Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract with Arsenal to make him the highest-paid manager in the Premier League, and he now has the financial power that few bosses before him were afforded

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has extended his stay with Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Rooney Rule is an important policy adopted by the National Football League in the United States that requires professional teams to interview diverse candidates for senior coaching, operational and front-office positions.

‌



‌



Originally established in 2003, it has been one of sport’s most important developments. Infinitely less important is another Rooney rule, established in 2010 by Sir Alex Ferguson, who wrote this in his 2015 book, Leading.

‌



“I told them (the Manchester United owners) I did not think it fair that (Wayne) Rooney should earn twice what I made and Joel Glazer immediately said: ‘I totally agree with you but what should we do? It was simple. We just agreed that no player should be paid more than me.”

‌



To be fair, not many managers get into the position of strength that Sir Alex enjoyed in 2010. Pep Guardiola, possibly Jose Mourinho in his pomp. And now Mikel Arteta.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



For as long as he stays at Arsenal, the manager will be the highest-paid employee. The most conservative estimate of the value of his new contract, which runs until 2030, comes in at around £20million a year.

Bukayo Saka is believed to be the highest-paid player, his recent extension taking his wages into the £18m-a-year bracket. Declan Rice will soon join him there.

No one can possibly begrudge Arteta his phenomenally lucrative deal. He has reestablished Arsenal as a true powerhouse of domestic and European football.

‌



He has become a more measured figure in the technical area, is extremely bright and has a very personable manner. But the figures involved are ridiculous. And that, of course, does not just relate to Arteta’s new contract, which some publications believe to be in the £25m-a-year ballpark.

Is Mikel Arteta the best manager in the Premier League? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson made sure to be paid more than Wayne Rooney (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



The Manchester City case will not only undermine the integrity of this Premier League season, it undermines the integrity of a couple of decades’ worth of seasons. How will that affect the next broadcasting deal, which provides the financial lifeblood of the Premier League?

Managers’ salaries count towards the Premier League’s financial regulations, which now take the form of Squad Cost Ratio. Arsenal are not anticipated to have any issues on that front but others well might. Nottingham Forest are said to be paying Oliver Glasner around £12m a year.

And while you definitely should not begrudge Arteta or Glasner, or any other manager, their preposterously handsome pay packets, the money does have to come from somewhere. Eventually, it comes from the fans.

‌



Envy is not a good look but when you see a manager being given a deal that pays him not far off £500,000 a week, you have to wonder if the elite game is heading in the right direction. Arteta’s most recent result - a chastening 3-0 defeat at Brighton - has no relevance, but consistent excellence is hard to maintain.

In recent years, the accounts of Premier League clubs - well, those apart from Arsenal, City and Liverpool - are festooned with pay-offs to sacked managers and their staff. And the money comes from you. From your TV subscription, from your replica shirt, from your ticket, from your over-priced food and drink.

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola enjoyed special status at Manchester City (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images)

‌



For now, Arsenal supporters will not care about that. What is important is that Arteta and the club seem a perfect match and the manager has committed himself to the ‘project’ for another four years, at least.

It is developing into a dynasty. But there was a time - well before Ferguson’s Rooney rule - when managers were modestly paid, when there was a view that the talent that mattered most was out on the pitch.

We can safely say that time has gone.

Sports.title: Everton star learns fate after admitting 61 breaches of FA betting rules
Sports.content:
Everton star learns fate after admitting 61 breaches of FA betting rules

Everton striker Martin Sherif admitted breaching the FA's rules against gambling after 61 bets, with a total stake of £1,974.77, were uncovered between November 2024 and February 2026

View 2 Images Martin Sherif admitted the breaches (Image: Malcolm Couzens/Getty Images)

Everton striker Martin Sherif has been fined £5,000 by the FA after admitting to breaching betting rules.

‌



‌



The 20-year-old was found to have six gambling accounts in his name, with 61 bets laid on football matches between November 2024 and February 2026.

‌



Sherif told the FA's regulatory commission that he did not place any of the bets himself. However, the accounts were in his name and he funded them, with £1,974.77 staked in total and £1,539.02 returned, equating to a net loss of £435.75.

‌



Sherif, who has spent time on loan with Port Vale and Rotherham United last season, emphasised that he had apologised, felt remorseful for his actions and has since warned his Everton academy team-mates about the dangers of gambling.

He also stressed his youth and inexperience and noted that he had been left "considerably out of pocket" due to the losses incurred.

‌



The commission found "his suggestion that he was not aware of the football bets difficult to accept" and also noted that Sherif had "attended education sessions" on gambling and was aware that he was not allowed to bet.

The commission deemed that a £5,000 fine was sufficient and that his actions didn't warrant a sporting sanction.

View 2 Images Martin Sherif has spent time on loan with Rotherham United and Port Vale (Image: Pete Norton/Getty Images)

‌



He scored two goals in 10 appearances for Rotherham in the first half of the 2025/26 season before heading to Port Vale. The forward netted twice in 19 games for Vale after joining them in February on loan, but could not stop them from being relegated from League One.

Sherif, who was born in Liberia, joined Everton's youth set-up in 2019 and has made numerous appearances for the club's under-18s and under-21s side, but is yet to make his senior debut for the Toffees.

Sherif's contract with Everton is due to expire in June and he is yet to make an appearance this season.

The club continue to deny any wrongdoing, insisting they have a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' that they believe will clear them of the charges. In the aftermath of the verdict, a number of potential punishments have been discussed, with possible sanctions ranging from a points deduction and financial penalty to the stripping of previous trophies or even expulsion from the Premier League.

‌



City's appeal is expected to be heard before the end of the year, with an independent three-person panel set to consider the case and reach a decision in the months ahead.

‌



On Thursday, Coventry City boss Frank Lampard held his press conference, while fellow managers Daniel Farke, Regis Le Bris, Marco Rose and Matthias Jaissle also faced the media.

With that in mind, Mirror Football brings you everything said by the five Premier League managers who faced the media on Thursday...

Coventry City -

Asked about the City guilty verdict, the Coventry City boss Lampard replied: "We've all seen the news, it's obviously big news, Man City are appealing.

‌



"I guess my reaction is that, right? What can you say when an appeal is going on? I'm not inside the story, I'm outside it completely.

"I played for Man City a long time ago now, for one year. We'll wait and see what the result of the appeal is and onwards. I don't know the timelines at all."

View 3 Images Frank Lampard was among the managers asked about Man City's situation (Image: Getty Images)

‌



On the impact on season: "I don't know, for Man City? I'm outside the loop. I have this job and my, not problems, but things I need to work on and I always respect a manager for whatever situation, there are a lot of things you don't know.

"This is obviously something we do know but they are obviously a huge football club now, a huge squad of quality players so we will see."

Leeds United - Daniel Farke

"Not my topic," Farke said. "There are more qualified people to speak about this. It's not up to me, I was not involved in the title race during these years. Only won one game with Norwich so can't really complain. Makes no sense if everyone in the world talks about this."

‌



Meanwhile, Leeds chairman Paraag Marathe told the BBC: "We'll let everything play out through the proper channels. Obviously I have some certain opinions on it that it is probably best I don't share at the moment.

"Whatever is the just result is I am sure going to be delivered. When the platform is there and the money is right (I'll respond). I want to make sure I am educated on it before I deliver an opinion. It just has to be what is just.

"Whatever is right and just, but I don't enough on it personally yet. In any sport everybody wants to play by the same rules and for any sport, you want a level playing field. Everyone is focussed on the task at hand and right now that is Saturday at Arsenal, that is our focus."

‌

Sunderland - Regis Le Bris

The Sunderland manager, Le Bris was not asked about City's guilty charges.

Bournemouth -

View 3 Images Bournemouth manager Marco Rose also gave his view (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

‌



The Cherries boss Rose says he trusts the people involved in dealing with City's situation. He said: "I played many times against Manchester City in the Champions League with my former clubs and for me it was always the best thing to challenge with the best players and the best clubs in the world.

"That's what I felt. I'm not this kind of guy who blames someone with not enough information. Of course, I hear everything, I read everything, but I do not have all the information.

‌



"I trust in the guys who are involved in these kinds of things and situations and then we will see what happens. I'm a football coach not a politician and I love to be a football coach and it should stay like this."

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Newcastle United -

"I think as a manager of another club, I am not able to judge and it is not my job. Especially it is not in my job description to judge on that," Jaissle told reporters.

‌



"The authorities are taking care of it and there is a clear process now which will be followed and speaking on behalf of the whole club, it is the right approach to focus on what we we can do better and what we can influence on the pitch.

"We should just focus on what we can influence and, in general, as a club, to improve and strive forward. Just focus on what we can do better."

With the Premier League returning this weekend, City face a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool on Sunday (4:30pm). There will no doubt be plenty of noise from supporters on Merseyside, as well as around other fixtures. However, no verdict is anticipated until the end of the year.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta still bears scar of Champions League heartbreak - 'I have poison in my veins'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta still bears scar of Champions League heartbreak - 'I have poison in my veins'

Mikel Arteta is excited about the future with Arsenal after signing a lucrative new contract, but the Spaniard is also driven by what happened against Paris Saint-Germain in May

View 2 Images Arsenal were left devastated in last season's Champions League final (Image: 2026 Marc Atkins)

Mikel Arteta has revealed that the pain of losing the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain is acting as "poison in my veins" as he looks to avenge Arsenal's defeat.

‌



‌



Arteta ended Arsenal's 22-year wait for the Premier League title in May, but their breakthrough season after three successive second-place finishes was tinged with sadness. The Gunners were beaten on penalties by PSG after a tense 1-1 draw in Budapest just 11 days after they lifted the Premier League trophy.

‌



Arteta took over as Arsenal manager in December 2019 and has overseen an upturn in the club's fortunes. His work was recognised this week when the owners handed him a new contract until 2030 which makes him the Premier League's highest-paid manager, on nearly £20million per year.

‌



Arsenal are focused on trying to defend their Premier League crown this season, but Arteta is clearly motivated to challenge PSG in the Champions League as well following the French giants' back-to-back titles. Asked by The Athletic whether the defeat on May 30 was akin to what Arsene Wenger called a "scar on my heart", Arteta was unequivocal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I still have the scar, like Arsene says. I still have that poison in my veins," he said. "It has to stay there because that’s when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody.”

Arteta has signed up for another four years at the helm in north London and is clearly relishing every aspect of the challenge of keeping Arsenal at the top of the game.

“Globally, with our supporters? Great," he said. "How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we’re going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta recently signed a new contract at Arsenal (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite.”

His words echo those he said after signing his new contract. “It’s a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal,” Arteta said.

Article continues below

“This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue. We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."

After a three-week international break to reflect on the 3-0 defeat by Brighton, Arsenal are back in action on Saturday against Leeds. They are then in Champions League action against Lille at the Emirates Stadium, with fixtures coming thick and fast across all competitions.

Sports.title: Man City discover stance on playing in EFL as chiefs 'make punishment feelings clear'
Sports.content:
Man City discover stance on playing in EFL as chiefs 'make punishment feelings clear'

Manchester City have launched an appeal after being found guilty of 114 charges brought against them by the Premier League

View 2 Images Man City could be forced to play in the EFL (Image: AP)

Manchester City have been told they should drop to the bottom of the English football pyramid and work their way back up following last week's verdict on their financial charges. An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.

‌



‌



The club were found to have used 'sham' contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018. However, City continue to strongly deny any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict.

‌



The club have adopted a siege mentality in the aftermath of the ruling, reassuring players and staff that they have 'irrefutable evidence' which they believe will clear their name. An independent three-person panel will now oversee City's appeal, with a decision expected before the end of the year.

‌



A key part of the club’s defence is expected to centre on the claim that the 'sham' deals were legitimate and funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than City's owners at the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG). The commission has the power to relegate City, impose unlimited fines, hand out points deductions or issue a transfer ban.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It also remains to be seen whether the club could be stripped of the titles they won during the nine-year period in question. There has been plenty of debate over what punishment City should receive, with several senior figures from the Premier League and English Football League (EFL) speaking to the i Paper about what they believe should happen.

‌



"They should go all the way to the bottom of the pyramid," one EFL source told The i Paper.

One EFL club executive added: "I don’t know all the details, but if they are guilty of all this, at the end of the day, depending on how passionately you believe in it, the integrity of the game is at stake.

"Why should we be forced to play alongside City as their punishment? Does it make it okay for League One clubs to cheat, if they are playing against Manchester City for points? You have to earn your place in any league in English football. Why should City be placed anywhere?"

‌



Leicester City's presence in League One this season has already demonstrated the potential impact of having a major club in the division, with one senior EFL executive pointing to the increased interest surrounding their fixtures.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca could end up managing City in the Championship - or lower (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

"We are seeing what having a giant of a club like Leicester City in League One this season does for interest," a senior EFL executive told the newspaper. "We sold out straight away for that. Imagine the demand for City tickets.

‌



"We have never made losses like this before. We cannot keep going like this, so anything that helps that is a bonus. The chance to go up against a giant like City would get more eyes on the league, attract investors, and get us gate receipts we wouldn’t normally get."

According to Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's handbook, City could face a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion from the competition.

A source close to the youth recruitment process in Manchester also highlighted the potential knock-on effect of any severe punishment for City. "Local clubs thrive off getting players who drop out of City’s academy, who have had a fantastic footballing upbringing there.

Article continues below

"If they went down the divisions, so many clubs would lose that." There is still a long way to go before the outcome of City's appeal becomes clear, with the independent panel now set to consider the club's case.

Sports.title: Man City charges: Club facing second sanction as Pep Guardiola's return confirmed
Sports.content:
Man City charges: Club facing second sanction as Pep Guardiola's return confirmed

Manchester City face a tense wait as they appeal after being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola is doubling down in his support for Manchester City (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

With the international break now over eyes turn back to the Premier League for Manchester City. The full squad return to training on Thursday as they gear up for the clash against Liverpool at Anfield, but the talk pre-match is bound to be dominated by the charges handing over City.

‌



‌



It was confirmed during the break that the club have been found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules. An independent panel rules that City used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their revenue between 2009 and 2018, something that City strongly deny.

‌



The club have submitted an appeal against the ruling, with a new three-person panel set to hear evidence. City claim to have 'irrefutable evidence' that proves their innocence in the case.

‌



Why Pep Guardiola is returning to Man City for the first time since guilty verdict READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Should City's appeal prove unsuccessful and the guilty verdict remains, the club faces a range of potential sanctions, including fines, points deductions, transfer bans, or relegation from the Premier League.

It appears there is still much to unfold before the matter reaches its conclusion. Here's a look at the latest developments:.

‌



Pep Guardiola's return

Former City manager Pep Guardiola will make his maiden return to the Etihad Stadium since his departure, for Wednesday night's Champions League fixture against Paris Saint-Germain. The Spaniard demonstrated his backing for City on social media the day following the confirmation of the guilty verdicts.

He wrote: "I want every single fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano, CEO], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

In a further show of solidarity, Guardiola will be present at the match against PSG.

‌



View 3 Images Pep Guardiola will be back to show his support (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Double jeopardy

City face the prospect of a second sanction should the guilty verdict survive an appeal, with Sky Sports reporting that UEFA are monitoring the situation closely. The governing body will reportedly weigh up whether to intervene once a definitive outcome has been reached.

City were handed a two-year ban from European football back in 2020 after being found guilty of breaching UEFA's financial fair play regulations. The club, however, successfully overturned the ban on appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS ).

‌



The report indicates that the Premier League had access to documents and evidence that were unavailable to UEFA when they were building their own case against City in 2020.

Dressing room reassurances

City's players have been given assurances by the club that 'sporting justice' will prevail, according to the representative of goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. The full squad are due to return to training for the first time since the verdict on Thursday, as they gear up for Sunday's Premier League showdown against Liverpool.

Speaking to Radio Napoli Centrale, Enzo Raiola said: "Will the Manchester City chaos change anything? No, nothing will change for us or for Gigio.

‌



"News comes out periodically. The club has spoken with Gigio and everyone is calm.

"Now there are important games against Liverpool and PSG, then sporting justice will take its course. But Gigio has had reassurances from Manchester City."

View 3 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma's agent has spoken about the Man City charges. (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

‌



HMRC investigation

City were reportedly placed under scrutiny by HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) in 2018 over potential tax evasion. The Financial Times reports that a civil investigation was launched into the club's tax affairs following the leak of emails by Der Spiegel in the same year.

The report indicates that the investigation was never formally concluded, having been carried out under the Code of Practice 8 framework, which does not encompass suspicions of deliberate fraud.

City sought guidance from external lawyers over the matter. HMRC ultimately took no action following the probe.

‌



Former captain speaks out

Former City skipper Kyle Walker has stated that the memories of his achievements at the club cannot be erased, despite the prospect of titles being stripped. The full-back was an integral figure between 2017 and 2025, claiming the Champions League and 13 domestic honours across his eight years at the club.

Speaking to talkSPORT, he said: "Obviously it doesn't look great. I know it's in an appeal stage so, for me to start commenting on the legal action and everything like that, probably it's not going to do myself justice or anyone involved in it.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"But, at a personal level, I can say the lads, we spent many and many a great year celebrating many trophies and everything like that and that's something that, whatever happens, they can't take away from us because we've experienced them nights.

"So, whatever will be, will be, and it's just down to the appeal now and what goes from there."

He added: It's something that we probably don't want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning them trophies, winning them the right way.

Article continues below

"It's very difficult because we've worked very hard for them, and not just us, I look at the fans as well.

"I look at the fans that have travelled up and down the country, travelled abroad to Istanbul when we won the treble and stuff like that, and they deserve that night as well."

Sports.title: Hunter Bell celebrates in Team GB's 'glam' female track success
Sports.content:
Georgia Hunter Bell has enjoyed quite the year, winning a hat-trick of gold medals at the World Indoor Championships, for England at the Commonwealth Games, and again for Team GB at the European Championships.

But British female track success in 2025 certainly didn't stop there. Sprinter Amy Hunt made headlines with a record four-gold display in the Europeans in Birmingham, while Dina Asher-Smith now tops the all-time medal table at the championships after winning her 11th, eight of which are gold.

Among other successes, Keely Hodgkinson claimed World Indoor gold in the 800m in March - in the second-fastest indoor time in history - and set a new British record at that distance in the summer, though she'd be pipped to gold at the Europeans after sitting out the Commonwealth Games due to muscle tightness.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Keely Hodgkinson reacts after winning the 800m at the London Diamond League in July - but failing in her bid to break the world record

"It's really cool. just being part of this era. It's really fun," Hunter Bell told Sky Sports.

"We all know each other very well. We all travel together, see each other a lot throughout the year, so it's fun to tune in and be like, 'Oh, Amy's racing tonight'.

"We're locked into everyone's goals and what they're trying to do. And when you're on a team together, someone winning or bringing home a medal, it makes you even more keen to do well because you want to contribute."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amy Hunt reflects on her record-breaking European Championships, after the Great Britain sprinter secured four gold medals in Birmingham

In addition to her statement performances on the track during her record-breaking Europeans, Hunt earned attention for her curated nail art that gave nod to landmarks within Birmingham, like the Bull Ring.

"Everyone knows I love a bit of glam and I love my nails," Hunt told the BBC at the time.

Hunter Bell says it's something the GB squad share, as feeling your best self on the start line can provide "that extra one or two per cent" to make you "feel like you can do anything".

Image: Georgia Hunter-Bell celebrated winning Commonwealth gold in the 800m this summer

"I enjoy the whole process of getting ready. We get ready like we're going to a club, we're quite glammed up," Hunter Bell said.

"We definitely put effort into it, for sure. We want to look nice.

"It's about doing whatever you need to feel confident on the start line - and I just think it makes you race better if you're feeling good about yourself.

"So much of that comes from the training and the lead up, of course. But it's that extra one or two per cent that makes you stand on the start line and feel like you can do anything, feel like you're a winner."

In terms of eye-catching track looks, Hodgkinson dominated the final race of her 2026 season by winning the 800m at Athlos in London last month as she debuted a new full-length, hooded speed suit.

Image: Keely Hodgkinson ran in a special new Nike speed suit at Athlos in London in September

Hodgkinson's outfit reminded people of Australian Cathy Freeman's which she won the women's 400m in at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, and it could be a feature for athletes at the next Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028.

Hunter Bell didn't rule out being one of them to don the suit.

"The first time you see it, it's like, 'Whoa! Haven't seen that before'," she said. "It will be interesting to see whether it becomes the norm.

"They do say it's quicker, so I'm definitely not ruling it out."

Sports.title: 'It's about time!' - F1 drivers excited amid Rwanda GP rumours
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and George Russell have expressed their excitement at the possibility of Rwanda hosting a Formula 1 race amid speculation the African nation could soon be added to the sport's calendar.

With Africa not having hosted an F1 race since the 1993 South African Grand Prix, Hamilton has been pushing hard over the last few years for the continent to return to the F1 schedule.

Several reports on Thursday claim an agreement has been struck and that an announcement could be made as soon as next week to confirm Rwanda's addition to the calendar for the 2030 season.

Asked about the speculation ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, Hamilton said: "I haven't really got any news for you. I saw something on people posting online, but I've always said that we need to have a Grand Prix in Africa.

"It is, for me, the most important continent, to be honest, the most beautiful continent. We're on all the other continents but that one and there should be no reason for it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter Craig Slater talks to the CEO of Formula One Stefano Domenicali about the F1 season so far

Hamilton has repeatedly publicly encouraged F1 president Stefano Domenicali to prioritise adding a race in Africa, and the seven-time world champion is pleased with the Italian's efforts.

"It is something I've been pushing for in the background, and Stefano has been amazing," Hamilton added.

"He's flown to Africa so many times over the last couple of years, speaking to lots and lots of different people, so I hope that he has some news for me soon."

'I would be very excited if rumours were true'

Formula 1 already has a packed 24-race schedule confirmed for 2027, but the hosting deals of several of the circuits on next year's calendar expire before 2030.

Portugal is returning as a host in 2027 but has just a two-year deal, while races in Mexico and Singapore are only currently agreed until 2028, and the Japanese Grand Prix is only confirmed until 2029.

Mercedes driver Russell said: "I would be very excited if these rumours were to come true.

"I was in Africa earlier this year and I really, really loved my time there.

"Formula 1 is a worldwide sport. Africa is the only continent we don't race on, and it's about time we had a race there."

Image: Max Verstappen (left) and Lewis Hamilton are both keen to race in Africa

Four-time world champion Verstappen added: "For sure, if that's possible, it would be great.

"We want to race in a lot of different places in the world, so I really hope that it can be pushed through.

"I've been once to Rwanda.

"We have to wait to see if it's all going to go through, but I think we're all very excited if that would happen."
