Sports.title: Bill Haney Targets November 28 for Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Bill Haney wants Shakur Stevenson to fight Devin Haney on November 28 in Atlanta, putting a specific date and location behind a matchup that has spent months tangled in negotiations.

The date would leave Shakur just over seven weeks to prepare if the deal were completed immediately. Each additional week spent arguing would reduce that window, making the schedule another potential obstacle after the prolonged dispute over weight.

“There has been a challenge to their team to take the fight at 145 and a half and take it on the 28th of November in Atlanta,” Bill said to True Media podcast.

Bill later repeatedly identified 145 pounds as the final offer, consistent with the catchweight already discussed publicly. Asked again about the timing, he confirmed: “The offer is on the table for him to fight in November.”

Shakur looks more likely to reject Bill’s proposed date than agree to fight on November 28. An old-school fighter might accept the date and get to work after spending months pursuing the matchup. Shakur’s approach has been more cautious, with lengthy arguments over the conditions under which he will face the bigger Haney.

Accepting November 28 would also mean allowing the Haney camp to set the timetable. Shakur has negotiated as though he views himself as the A-side, or at least Devin’s equal. He could reject the date or push for a later fight rather than appear to be working to Bill’s schedule.

His current training situation is unknown, but any further delay would make November 28 harder to meet. The two camps could settle the weight dispute only to spend more time arguing over when to fight.

Bill said DAZN has made an offer, and he isn’t talking about anyone else for Devin. He wants Shakur next, but naming November 28 in Atlanta doesn’t mean Shakur will take it. Bill can push for that date all he wants. He still needs Shakur to agree, and after months of back-and-forth, that could take longer than he hopes.

Sports.title: Imam Khataev Targets Third Straight Win Against Padraig McCrory
Sports.content:
Imam Khataev seeks his third consecutive victory tonight against Padraig McCrory in a 10-round light heavyweight contest on DAZN at Capitole de Québec in Quebec City. The Olympic bronze medalist defends his NABF title on the Osleys Iglesias–Oliver Zaren undercard.

Khataev (12-1, 11 KOs) has stopped both opponents he has faced since his disputed split-decision loss to David Morrell in July 2025. Adam Deines lasted three rounds last December, while Mickael Diallo was stopped in the opening round in June. McCrory (20-2, 10 KOs) now gets the task of interrupting that run.

The Morrell performance remains the strongest evidence of what Khataev can do against higher-level opposition. He dropped the Cuban with a right hand in the fifth round and pushed him through a hard 10-round fight. Morrell got the decision, but Khataev’s promoter disputed the scoring and called for a rematch.

That leaves Khataev in a different position from a prospect whose potential rests entirely on knocking out overmatched opponents. He has already shown that his power and pressure can trouble a leading contender. The defeat added a loss to his record without settling how far he can go at 175 pounds.

McCrory offers another opportunity to build on that performance, although beating him would not answer every question left by the Morrell fight. Khataev needs opponents who can withstand his early attacks and force him to sustain his work deeper into a contest. His two quick stoppages have provided little opportunity to demonstrate that.

The temptation tonight will be to chase another early finish. Khataev’s power makes that a realistic outcome, but applying pressure without wasting punches would also serve him well when he returns to tougher opposition.

A third straight win would keep Khataev moving toward those fights. After the showing against Morrell, the next step should be another opponent capable of testing whether he can turn a competitive performance at that level into a victory.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Wants Oleksandr Usyk Again After Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury wants a third fight with Oleksandr Usyk after Anthony Joshua, telling Rick Reno that his preferred finish would be victory in Cardiff followed by revenge at Madison Square Garden.

Usyk has already beaten him twice, but Fury remains interested in another attempt rather than a fresh opponent from the heavyweight division’s leading contenders.

“I want that rematch with him, that trilogy, because I know deep in my heart that I won those fights. And for whatever reason, he’s been given a decision over me,” Fury said to the Mr. Verzace podcast.

Fury described his ideal ending as beating Joshua in front of 80,000 in Cardiff, then going to Madison Square Garden to “get the revenge on the rabbit finally.” That is his preferred route, rather than an agreement for a third Usyk fight.

The appeal is understandable financially. Another meeting would likely produce an enormous payday, with two established names and a revenge story to sell. Fury could struggle to earn comparable money against Frank Sanchez, Filip Hrgovic or Moses Itauma.

There is also the knockout risk. Usyk isn’t a big puncher by heavyweight standards and is considerably smaller than Fury. He badly hurt Fury in their first meeting, so another fight would hardly be harmless, but Fury has twice completed 12 rounds against him.

Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley, Itauma, Hrgovic and Sanchez present different physical threats. They have the power to stop Fury, and facing one of them could mean accepting that danger for less money. Another points loss to Usyk would be easier to explain than getting knocked out by a new opponent.

Fury claiming robbery gives him the narrative hook to sell a trilogy. It lets him pitch a third bout as settling unfinished business rather than admitting he sits on two official losses to the same fighter.

Joshua remains the immediate hurdle in Cardiff. Fury must get past that domestic clash before any retirement tour holds weight. Overcoming Joshua opens the door to another massive payday against Usyk, all while keeping the division’s lethal young punchers safely locked on the outside.

Sports.title: Lewis Crocker Gets Soft Landing Against Owen Cooper
Sports.content:
Lewis Crocker will face Owen Cooper in Belfast on December 19, Queensberry Promotions announced, in a matchup that looks designed to get the former IBF welterweight champion winning again after his defeat to Liam Paro.

The fight joins the Anthony Cacace–Nick Ball card, giving Crocker a return in front of his home crowd against an opponent he should be expected to beat. Cooper has experience at the domestic level, but this is a considerable step up against someone who recently held a world title.

Queensberry hyped the matchup as a “welterweight war” on X, but choosing Cooper suggests Crocker’s team is taking few chances with his comeback. It gives him an opportunity to regain confidence before facing another leading contender. Cooper has beaten Chris Kongo and stopped Eithan James, giving him enough experience to offer resistance. However, defeats to Ekow Essuman and Constantin Ursu leave questions about his ability to beat a fighter of Crocker’s level. Queensberry’s fighter profile lists those results, including his February points loss to Ursu.

Choosing Cooper makes sense for Crocker’s team after the Paro defeat. He should give Crocker a chance to get some rounds and rebuild his confidence before facing stronger opposition. Returning to Belfast adds the support of his home crowd.

The pressure is on Crocker to beat Cooper clearly. Struggling against an opponent well below world level would raise questions about his chances against the division’s top fighters, even if he comes away with a win.

Cooper has plenty of reason to take his chance. Beating a former world champion would give him the biggest win of his career and could lead to fights beyond the domestic level. This fight serves as a calculated soft landing for Crocker. His job is to dismantle Cooper convincingly and prove to his handlers that he can handle a stiffer test in his next outing.

Sports.title: Oliver Zaren Trusts His Chin Against Osleys Iglesias
Sports.content:
Oliver Zaren is counting on his chin against Osleys Iglesias tonight in Quebec. The unbeaten challenger told The Ring that sparring with heavier punchers has given him confidence that he can take the IBF super middleweight champion’s power.

Zaren (19-0-1, 8 KOs) has yet to beat a notable opponent, making this a steep jump for his first world title fight. He now faces arguably the most dangerous puncher at 168 pounds, with little in his record to suggest he’s ready.

“My team, we have our concerns on the power he’s coming with, but I’ve sparred some heavy guys who can really punch, and I can take one, so it’s going to be a good fight. I’m not coming just to take part; I’m here to win,” Zaren told The Ring.

Iglesias (15-0, 14 KOs) defends his IBF title for the first time tonight at Capitole de Quebec, headlining an Eye of the Tiger show on DAZN. The Cuban stopped Vladimir Shishkin in the eighth round, then won the vacant belt in April when Pavel Silyagin retired after eight rounds.

Those results make this a difficult jump for Zaren. Taking punches from heavier fighters in sparring can build confidence, but it offers limited evidence of how he will respond when Iglesias lands cleanly with smaller gloves under fight conditions.

The danger also goes beyond surviving one hard shot. If Iglesias hurts him, Zaren will need the defensive skills to prevent the champion from following up.

Zaren, 26, is trained by former unified super middleweight champion Mikkel Kessler and believes his June fight with Jose Navarro Jr. showed he was ready for world-level opposition. That European title bout ended in a technical draw after bad weather forced a stoppage following three rounds. Zaren felt he was winning, but he never had to prove he could sustain that success through a full fight.

Without a victory over a leading contender, Zaren is going straight into a title challenge against Iglesias, whose power has been too much for all but one of his opponents. His willingness to accept the opportunity is clear. His record offers much less reason to expect him to win it.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Challenges Emanuel Navarrete’s Dominant Image
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster believes Emanuel Navarrete’s destruction of Eduardo “Sugar” Nunez came against an opponent who couldn’t offer enough resistance, telling Lance Pugmire that the Mexican champion’s size helped him dominate.

Foster faces Navarrete in a super featherweight unification on October 24 in San Antonio. He acknowledges that Navarrete looked sharp against Nunez, but says he’ll present a different challenge.

“He looked sharp, but Nunez didn’t give us anything,” Foster told BoxingScene. “Nunez is too small. He was at 122lbs a couple years ago, so he’s a naturally smaller guy. When he tried to turn it up on Navarrete, he was too small. He couldn’t hurt him. Navarrete treated him like a little kid.”

Foster’s weight-history claim is inaccurate. Nunez’s last appearance near 122 pounds was in 2017, and he was slightly above that limit. More recent weight reports list him at 132.4 pounds against Oscar Escandon in 2023 and 133 against Miguel Marriaga in 2024. He was an established super featherweight champion when Navarrete beat him.

The stronger explanation is stylistic. Nunez is a straightforward slugger who gave Navarrete the kind of punching contest he thrives in. Navarrete proved better at it, overwhelming an opponent whose approach left him available for punishment.

That performance doesn’t erase the vulnerabilities exposed against Denys Berinchyk, Robson Conceicao and Charly Suarez. Berinchyk beat him at lightweight, while Conceicao and Suarez made his work difficult at 130. Navarrete can look destructive without being difficult to hit or impossible to outbox.

Foster’s opportunity is to make Navarrete work for his openings. Movement, counters, and changes of pace could force him into a less comfortable fight than Nunez provided. Trading for extended stretches would give away that advantage.

The uncertainty is whether Foster can sustain that discipline under pressure. His uneven majority-decision victory over Ray Ford leaves room for doubt.

Foster doesn’t need Nunez to have been undersized for his argument to work. He needs to demonstrate that Navarrete’s success against one slugger won’t translate against a champion offering a different style.

Ghana News.title: You need to fake it sometimes to make it fun – Stephanie Benson tells partners
Ghana News.content:
Celebrated singer, breast cancer survivor, and advocate Stephanie Benson has advised partners and couples on how to spice up and strengthen their relationships without getting tired of each other.

According to her, one does not become soulmates overnight; rather, it takes intentionality, effort, and hard work to build a strong relationship with a partner.

She made these remarks while speaking with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes show, where she explained how she has been able to sustain her relationship with her husband, John Benson, over the years.

She said that sometimes, partners need to “fake” certain things to keep the relationship fun and exciting.

“When you have that connection, you have to work on it. It doesn’t just happen. Some people say, there’s something called soulmate. Listen, anyone could be my soulmate if I put energy into it. So yes, John is my soulmate because we worked towards creating it. That’s why I’m always telling people take your time; don’t rush it. People rush it to find just anybody and even if you do, please take your time and get to know the person; understand what make them tick, what make the sexy. Sometimes, you have to fake it a little bit even if the person is grating, you tell them they’re looking really good.”

She further said that many people are struggling to make their relationships work and are ending them prematurely because they become bored with their partners early in the relationship.

She noted that most couples assume their partners should understand their needs and expectations in the relationship, even when they do not communicate them openly.

“I feel like now a days, relationships end too quickly because nobody wants to create anything; they always go like I’m bored with her so I’m going to get a different lady and that’s what cracks relationships; people don’t understand it. The think the lady should understand because they have high libido. Do you know my libido? Listen, if I had my way, I would sleep with all of you right here,” she explained.

The performer emphasized that both partners need to prioritize each other, never take communication for granted, and always resist the urge to give up on each other or on their love in order to sustain their unions.

Ghana News.title: Mahama Cares says political affiliation will not determine access to medical support
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Medical Trust Fund, popularly known as Mahama Cares, has reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that political affiliation does not determine access to life-saving medical support under the initiative.

The assurance was given by the Fund’s Administrator, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, during a stakeholder engagement at the Greater Accra Regional Coordinating Council on Thursday, October 8.

The engagement, hosted by the Greater Accra Regional Minister, Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo, marked the beginning of the Fund’s stakeholder sensitisation tour in the Greater Accra Region.

Speaking to regional officials and other stakeholders, Ms Darko-Opoku stressed that Mahama Cares operates on a strictly non-partisan basis, particularly where health and human life are concerned.

She said healthcare assistance would be determined by medical needs rather than political affiliations.

“There’s nothing political with what we do, and we want to emphasise that because when it comes to your health, there’s nothing like political colours,” she said.

She added that the Fund would not allow political considerations to influence decisions concerning the lives and wellbeing of Ghanaians.

Medical professionals to determine beneficiaries

Ms Darko-Opoku explained that qualified medical professionals would play the key role in assessing patients and determining those who qualify for support.

According to her, this approach would help protect vulnerable patients and their families from discrimination based on their political backgrounds.

She also stressed the need for the Fund’s operations to remain aligned with its core objective of providing meaningful healthcare support to Ghanaians.

Beyond settling individual medical bills, the Ghana Medical Trust Fund is also seeking to strengthen public healthcare facilities through the provision of critical equipment and infrastructure.

The Fund has identified the need for functional CT scanners, MRI machines and mammography units, particularly in response to the growing burden of chronic non-communicable diseases such as cancer and kidney disease.

Ms Darko-Opoku said the Fund would pursue strategic partnerships with private-sector organisations to improve diagnostic and treatment capacity in public hospitals.

One such partnership is a US$10 million commitment from the KGL Group towards the construction of a modern Diagnostic and Imaging Centre at Ridge Hospital.

The Greater Accra engagement forms part of Mahama Cares’ nationwide sensitisation campaign aimed at reducing the financial burden associated with specialised treatment for chronic diseases.

The initiative is expected to provide financial support for specialised healthcare services that are not adequately covered under the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), creating an additional safety net for vulnerable patients.

The Ghana Medical Trust Fund is undertaking a 16-region sensitisation tour, with a focus on strengthening healthcare institutions, improving transparency, using clinical data to guide decisions and promoting fair access to specialised healthcare across the country.

Ghana News.title: Government inherited GH¢111bn debt burden but continues infrastructure projects – Lands Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, says the government inherited a debt burden of about GH¢111 billion, placing significant pressure on public finances.

He said despite the debt obligations and the billions of cedis being committed to debt servicing, the government had continued to undertake major infrastructure projects across the country.

Speaking during an engagement with chiefs of the Eastern Nzema Traditional Area, Mr Buah said the government had paid more than GH¢2 billion in debt obligations in 2025 and 2026.

He added that the government is expected to pay more than GH¢10 billion next year, describing the repayment schedule as an obligation that cannot be avoided.

“All we have been doing is paying debt. Yet, in the midst of paying all the debt, we have been delivering several infrastructural projects,” he said.

Mr Buah argued that the financial obligations had not prevented the government from investing in infrastructure and other development projects.

He said the administration remained committed to using available resources to address infrastructure deficits and improve living conditions while meeting the country’s debt obligations.

The Minister’s comments come amid ongoing discussions over public debt management and the government’s ability to balance debt servicing with its development priorities.

Ghana News.title: Mallam Atta traders urge government to speed up 24-hour market redevelopment
Ghana News.content:
Traders at the Mallam Atta Market in Accra have appealed to the government to expedite ongoing redevelopment works, saying the displacement of businesses has affected their customer base and sales.

The traders said that while they support the redevelopment of the market under the government’s 24-hour economy agenda, the demolition and relocation of some shops have made it difficult for customers to locate their usual businesses.

They raised concerns during an engagement with the Ayawaso Central Municipal Assembly on the annual revenue collection rates.

One of the traders, Tawulo, who sells food at the market, said business was continuing despite the demolition but appealed to the government to accelerate the project.

“It is true they have demolished the market, but it is only phases one and two. We only plead with the government to speed up the work so we can get more customers,” she said.

The traders also cited choked gutters, inadequate street lighting and security concerns as some of the challenges affecting businesses at the market.

They called for urgent attention to the drainage system to improve sanitation and help prevent flooding around the market.

The traders further appealed to the Assembly to maintain the existing revenue fees, citing the difficulties businesses are facing amid the ongoing redevelopment.

The Presiding Member of the Ayawaso Central Municipal Assembly, Alexander Kwame Mensah Tumasi, said the engagement formed part of the Assembly’s annual consultations with ratepayers before determining revenue rates for the year.

He said the consultations allow the Assembly to hear directly from traders and assess whether existing rates should be increased, maintained or reduced.

“Looking at their grievances with the coming of the 24-hour economy, most of the traders have been displaced, and it has affected them because some of the customers they have do not know where they are. So sales have come down. So we will maintain the fee rather than increase. We have heard their challenges,” he said.

The Municipal Chief Executive for Ayawaso Central, Rudolf Collinwoode Williams, said the Assembly engages traders annually to discuss revenue rates and make collection easier for both the Assembly and businesses.

He said the consultations were intended to ensure that the concerns of ratepayers were considered in determining the rates.

The traders are now calling for faster completion of the redevelopment works, improved drainage, adequate street lighting and better security.

While acknowledging the need to modernise the market, they said the transition should also take into account the livelihoods of traders who depend on the market for their daily income.

Ghana News.title: Catholic Church has a duty to speak on issues affecting human dignity – Bishop Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
Catholic Bishop Kwasi Gyamfi has defended the Catholic Church’s involvement in national issues, saying its interventions are driven by a responsibility to protect human dignity.

According to him, the Church’s mandate extends beyond spiritual matters to include moral issues and matters affecting the well-being of the human person.

“The Catholic Church deals not only with spiritual issues, it deals also with moral issues and anything that enhances human dignity,” he said.

Bishop Gyamfi explained that the Church considers the human person sacred and therefore has a responsibility to speak against issues it believes dehumanise people or undermine their dignity.

Speaking to Joy News' Gemma Appiah, He rejected suggestions that such interventions amount to the Church entering the political arena.

“We do not do politics. We call it the enhancement of the human person,” he said.

He acknowledged that some of the issues raised by the Church may be viewed as political by others, but said the Church considers them matters of human development and community welfare.

On the Church’s call for qualified Catholic students to have access to Catholic schools, Bishop Gyamfi said the demand should not be interpreted as a quota system.

He explained that Catholic schools were established to provide academic and skills training alongside moral and spiritual formation.

“We believe skills training alone, academic excellence alone, is not enough for the human person,” he said.

Bishop Gyamfi said Catholic schools remain open to people of other faiths who share their values, but stressed that this should not result in the dilution of the Catholic character and purpose of the institutions.

He maintained that qualified Catholic students who choose Catholic schools should have the opportunity to attend them because of the specific formation the Church seeks to provide.

According to him, preventing such students from accessing the schools could undermine the purpose for which the Catholic Church established them.

He also pointed to the Church’s investment in establishing many of the schools before the state assumed responsibility for paying teachers’ salaries.

“The fact that the state pays salaries of teachers does not make the schools state schools,” Bishop Gyamfi said.

He stressed that the schools were established with a distinct educational philosophy that combines academic excellence with human, moral and spiritual formation.

Bishop Gyamfi further cited the history of formal education in Ghana, noting that missionary groups, including the Presbyterians, Methodists and Catholics, played a major role in establishing formal education before government became involved.

Ghana News.title: KATH sickle cell, blood bank project stalled over $1.6m legal dispute – CEO
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), Dr Paa Kwesi Baidoo, has disclosed that the hospital’s Sickle Cell and Blood Bank project has stalled due to a $1.6 million legal dispute between the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) and the contractor.

He made the disclosure when he appeared before the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Thursday, October 8, to provide an update on the project, which had been raised in the hospital’s previous audit report.

Dr Baidoo said the project was being sponsored by GNPC, with the Ghana Sickle Cell Foundation playing a leading role in discussions towards its implementation.

He said KATH had subsequently written to the foundation requesting that the project be handed over to the hospital if GNPC was no longer prepared to fund it.

“We've written to the Sickle Cell Foundation to let us have the project if the GNPC is not ready to fund it,” he said.

Dr Baidoo added that he had also met the Chief Executive Officer of GNPC to appeal for action to be expedited, given the importance of the project to the hospital.

However, he said efforts to move the project forward had been complicated by a legal dispute between GNPC and the contractor, which was before the courts.

“They have some legal issues between the contractor and GNPC, which they are resolving in the courts,” Dr Baidoo said.

Contractor demands $1.6m

Dr Baidoo explained that the contractor had resorted to legal action after the project made no progress since 2022.

“The project since 2022 hasn’t seen any progress, so the contractor went to court demanding $1.6 million from GNPC,” he said.

He said GNPC had indicated that up to $2 million would be required to complete the project and would prefer to use the funds to complete the facility rather than pay the contractor as a judgment debt.

“GNPC is saying they have up to $2 million that is needed to complete their project. And they would rather give it to their contractor to complete their project instead of their judgment debt,” he said.

Dr Baidoo said KATH was taking steps to encourage GNPC and the contractor to resolve the dispute and allow work to resume.

“And that’s why we said these legal issues are beyond my pay grade,” he added.

PAC demands evidence of follow-up

The explanation prompted PAC Chairperson Abena Osei-Asare to question the extent of KATH’s efforts to resolve the matter, particularly as the project was reportedly 72 per cent complete.

She demanded evidence that the hospital had formally written to GNPC and followed up on the matter.

“I don’t think you did anything. You just went to sleep. You just went to sleep,” she said.

Ms Osei-Asare questioned why the remaining 28 per cent of the project had not been completed and warned that prolonged abandonment could increase the eventual cost of completion.

“When we abandon the project for a long time, it increases the cost of completion,” she said.

She also rejected reliance on verbal explanations concerning the legal dispute and insisted that KATH provide formal correspondence to support its account.

“Usually, we don’t use our mouth to talk about legal issues. We should see formal letters from you to GNPC and for GNPC to respond, say that I have received your letter and this is our position,” she said.

“But to come and just say by word of mouth that this is it, respectfully, that is not the way to go,” she added.

Ms Osei-Asare further criticised KATH management over its 2024 report, accusing the institution of failing to address the issues as expected.

She nevertheless assured the hospital that the committee would work with management to resolve the outstanding matters.

Ghana News.title: Restricting preaching in moving vehicles is an attempt to gag the church – Rev. Kwadwo Bempah
Ghana News.content:
The Head Pastor of Holy Hill Chapel of the Assemblies of God, Rev. Kwadwo Boateng Bempah, has described the restriction on preaching in moving public service vehicles as an attempt to gag the church.

This is in spite of the fact that the amended Road Traffic Regulations Act also prohibits hawking on buses in motion.

According to him, the church will not remain silent or stop spreading the gospel despite the new restriction.

“Now they say we shouldn't preach in the bus as if they bought a bus for somebody. When those little attempts begin, they are trying to shut the mouth of the church,” he said.

Rev. Bempah made the remarks in a message delivered to his congregation and widely circulated on social media.

He questioned why preaching on buses should be prohibited while other people continue to use loudspeakers in public spaces.

“But others are screaming early in the morning at 4.30 a.m. on loudspeakers. You didn't buy a bus for anybody. You say we shouldn't preach in the bus. When my bus is going, come and tell me,” he said.

The pastor insisted that efforts to stop the practice would not succeed, stressing that the church would continue to reach people wherever they gather.

“You will not succeed. Oh, what you are trying to do, you will not succeed. You will not succeed. Wherever human beings gather, we will preach. Wherever human beings gather, the word must go forth. They enter the car. We will bring them. Even at the back of Okada, we will be shouting the name Jesus,” he added.

Read Also: Explainer: Why preaching in moving tro-tros could mean eight months in jail

Rev Bempah also cautioned Christians against compromising their faith to please others.

“Never please people to displease God,” he said.

His comments follow the enforcement of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519), which prohibits preaching and hawking on public service vehicles while they are in motion.

Under the regulations, persons found preaching in moving public or commercial vehicles may face a fine of between 10 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both.

Ghana News.title: Central Charismatic Baptist Church marks 30 years, urges review of law restricting preaching on buses
Ghana News.content:
The Central Charismatic Baptist Church (CCBC) at Atonsu-Gyinyase in Kumasi has marked its 30th anniversary with a thanksgiving service and a call for a review of the law restricting preaching on public transport.

The anniversary climaxed 30 days of prayer and fasting under the theme “Open Doors”, anchored on Revelation 3:8: “See, I have placed before you an open door that no one can shut.”

The celebration brought together past and present members, clergy, traditional leaders, government officials and other well-wishers to reflect on the church’s three decades of ministry and community impact.

Among the dignitaries present were the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, and the Asokwa Municipal Chief Executive, Amoh Kamel.

The thanksgiving service featured praise and worship, choral performances and a drama depicting the church’s beginnings, challenges and growth over the past 30 years.

In his address, the Founder and Senior Pastor, Rev. Dr Steve Owusu Ampomah Paintsil, expressed gratitude to God, the church’s founding members, past and present leaders and the congregation for their commitment.

“This is not just about a building or numbers; it is about 30 years of God's grace, of lives saved, families restored, and hope given to the hopeless. The Lord has been our Ebenezer, and He is opening greater doors for us,” he said.

Re.v Dr Paintsil said the church would, in its next phase, intensify its missions, youth mentorship, educational support and community development initiatives.

Call to review preaching restriction

The anniversary comes amid the enforcement of a new regulation restricting preaching and hawking in public service vehicles while they are in motion.

Reacting to the regulation in an interview after the service, Rev Dr Paintsil acknowledged concerns about noise, nuisance and passenger safety but said an outright ban and custodial punishment could undermine grassroots evangelism.

He argued that preaching on buses had been an effective means of reaching people who might otherwise never enter a church.

“My born-again journey started with a preaching I heard on a bus,” he revealed.

He called for the regulation to be reviewed and for clear guidelines to be introduced to allow evangelism without disturbing passengers.

“This law has already been passed, but we are appealing that it should be revised. Instead of criminalising evangelism with prison terms and fines, we should rather regulate it. We can have clear guidelines on how to preach respectfully without disturbing or harassing passengers,” Rev Dr Paintsil appealed.

He urged Parliament, the Ministry of Transport and city authorities to engage the clergy on a balanced approach that protects public order while respecting religious liberty.

Church outlines next 30-year vision

The church’s Senior Deacon, Dr Kwasi Osei Agyemang, said the anniversary marked a new phase rather than an end point.

Speaking on behalf of the Board of Deacons, he said the church’s vision for the next 30 years was to win more souls, expand its missions, plant more branches and increase its investment in youth development, education, skills training and community projects.

“For 30 years, God has been faithful. In the next 30 years, we want to see C.C.B.C become a mega church in Ashanti - a church that is not only large in numbers but deep in impact, winning more souls for God, raising godly leaders, and transforming communities,” Dr Agyemang said.

He called on members to remain committed and united to help achieve the vision.

The anniversary celebration ended with prayers for the church, the nation and the next generation, followed by the cutting of the anniversary cake and fellowship.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: ‘War lives in me’: Gaza playwright Ali Abu Yasin wins English PEN award
World.content:
Ali Abu Yasin, honoured for his artistic resilience, has endured Israeli bombardment, displacement and personal loss over the past three years.

London, United Kingdom – Ali Abu Yassin, a playwright from Gaza who continued writing even as Israel’s genocidal campaign devastated the world around him, has won a prestigious award in London.

“This prize is great not only for me, but for Gaza, Palestine, and all the Palestinian people,” Ali Abu Yasin, who was named on Thursday as “Writer of Courage 2026” by the literary group English PEN, told Al Jazeera.

The 62-year-old began writing plays and mastering the oud as a teenager in al-Shati refugee camp in Gaza, one of the largest in the Strip and a target of recent attacks.

“It’s how I was born, I’ve wanted to express myself using art since my childhood,” he told Al Jazeera.

After the war began in October, 2023, Abu Yasin stopped writing plays and instead wrote about life under Israeli bombardment.

Abu Yasin said for the first two years, he wrote about the situation in Gaza as Palestinians fled and feared for their lives.

“There was no theatre; it was impossible to have a theatre because Gaza was being destroyed,” the writer said, shaking his head.

Since 2023, Israel has killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza and the majority of survivors have been displaced several times over.

Abu Yasin works with actors who now rehearse their lines in makeshift tents, against the sound of gunfire.

“I was near death four, five times. I saw people around me die. We lived by chance, and those who died, died by chance,” Abu Yasin told Al Jazeera.

“My son was trapped under rubble; my house was bombed. So, during those two years, I was trying just to provide some safety to my family. To protect them from famine. And to document what was happening, so the world can hear my voice before I die.”



After a break, he wrote several screenplays that he hid and carried with him throughout displacement.

In 2004, Abu Yasin began working with the Said Al-Mishal Theatre, a hub for Palestinian culture in Gaza City that was levelled in a 2018 Israeli bombing.

Leading playwrights and theatre directors described the attack as “obliteration of this symbol of Palestinian culture and identity” in a letter to The Guardian newspaper.

In 2008, Abu Yasin began writing the Gaza Monologues, a series illustrating life in Gaza, both moments of joy and of pain.

A few weeks ago, Abu Yasin left Gaza with the support of an artist residency programme in France.

“I didn’t actually leave the war. The war lives in me, Gaza lives in me,” he said.

He has found himself conserving small amounts of water and minimising waste, habits he developed by living through the humanitarian crisis.

The award ceremony aligns with his trip to France, allowing him to attend in person largely by fortunate coincidence. For English PEN, the privilege of an in-person ceremony at the British Library is not taken for granted.

“For many years, writers living in Gaza have been among those with the most limited freedom of movement in the world. We recognise this and the direct impact it has on their freedom of expression,” an English PEN spokesperson told Al Jazeera.

Abu Yasin’s recent play, 50 Minutes, was shown in Gaza and tells the story of genocide and mourning. Actors rehearsed in a makeshift tent in a car park, many of them without any previous theatre experience.

Abu Yasin was nominated by the British academic and cultural critic Jacqueline Rose, who won the 2026 PEN Pinter Prize.

The Writer of Courage “is awarded to an author who is active in defence of freedom of expression, often at great risk to their own safety and liberty, and shares the PEN Pinter Prize with the winner,” says English PEN.

The organisation is the United Kingdom branch of PEN International, a global association of writers dedicated to “championing freedom of expression and literary advocacy worldwide”.

PEN America, its United States counterpart, came under fire in recent years as some alleged it did not support Palestinian writers. PEN America faced a boycott, leading to the resignation of its president in 2025.

English PEN, which operates independently from the US group, joined PEN International in calling for an arms embargo on Israel and condemning the killing of Palestinian writers.

Rose described his work as “a call for justice, a cry of outrage and a spiritual quest” in a press release.



“He has been the consistent chronicler of the harshness and cruelty of Palestinian existence, and the mentor of young people struggling to pluck meaning from the debris of their lives.”

Rose came to prominence with her 2005 book, The Question of Zion, a psychoanalysis of Zionism.

Abu Yasin has three children and 16 grandchildren. All are in Gaza except for his son, Amjad Abu Yasin, who is an actor in France.

“In Gaza, we have simple dreams. We want to live in peace and to live in freedom. We want the sky and the seas to be open,” he said. “We just want some freedom.”

World.title: Philippines ex-President Duterte fit to stand trial, ICC rules
World.content:
The former president is able to understand the charges and follow the proceedings, panel of experts find.

Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) have found former Philippine President Rodrigo ⁠Duterte fit to stand trial and able to face charges of crimes against humanity related to the so-called “war on drugs” he waged while in office.

The ex-leader is accused of murder and attempted murder for his alleged involvement in dozens of killings. He denies the charges, but faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment if convicted.

The court in The Hague said on Thursday that independent medical experts had examined the 81-year-old’s health and concluded he was mentally fit to understand evidence and discuss his defence with his lawyers.

“The chamber was satisfied that the accused is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings,” the court said.

His legal team had previously attempted to get the case thrown out on medical grounds, arguing that serious memory loss had left him unable to absorb new information or reliably recall the past.

The trial is scheduled to open on November 30.

Duterte, who served as president from 2016 to 2022, was arrested in the Philippines in March 2025 and sent to the ICC’s headquarters in The Hague following a lengthy ICC investigation.

Last month, he appeared in person for the first time at the ICC.

Duterte denies the charges against him, saying he only ordered police to act in self-defence as part of his anti-drugs offensive. Judges also denied a request for him to be released from custody.

Estimates of the death toll in the crackdown on drugs during his presidential term vary, from the more than 6,000 reported by the national police to up to 30,000 claimed by human rights groups.



Prosecutors say that police and government hit squads carried out dozens of killings at his orders, motivated by the promise of money or to avoid becoming targets themselves.

Throughout his presidency, Duterte enjoyed a high approval rating from the public, allowing him to push for his brutal anti-drugs agenda.

He became the first Asian ex-leader to be arrested by the ICC, which prosecutes individuals for the world’s worst crimes, such as war crimes and crimes against humanity.

World.title: Israel opens first-ever pavilion at Morocco defence show
World.content:
Israel opened its first national pavilion at Morocco’s Marrakech Air Show, joined by Israel’s top military contractors.

Israel’s Ministry of Defence says it is participating for the first time in a defence exhibition in Morocco, as it announced its first-ever national pavilion at the Marrakesh Air Show 2026.

“This marks Israel’s first official participation in the defence exhibition held in Morocco since the signing of the Abraham Accords”, Israel’s Defence Ministry said in a statement on Thursday.

The ministry said eight Israeli defence companies exhibited “advanced, combat-proven technologies at the show” in Marrakesh, which runs until Saturday.

The Marrakech Air Show, taking place from October 7 to October 10 this year at the Marrakech Royal Moroccan Air Force Base, is organised every two years and is meant for civil and military aeronautics and space industries to highlight their latest offerings.

“Israel’s three major defence industries, Elbit Systems, IAI, and Rafael, also exhibited, presenting solutions across the air, land, sea, space, intelligence, cyber, and digital domains,” it said.

The announcement is the latest sign of increasing ties between the Arabic-speaking North African country and Israel, since the two established ties in 2020 as part of the US-backed Abraham Accords.

Last month, Israel and Morocco agreed to upgrade their diplomatic ties, including elevating their respective missions to embassies and appointing ambassadors to both countries.



The move followed a meeting between the two countries’ foreign ministers, hosted by the US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

They also agreed to expand air travel, including by reinstating direct flights operated by carriers from both nations, and confirmed plans for high-level bilateral visits in the coming months.

Morocco is also one of the five countries that have pledged to send troops to Gaza, under the US-backed International Stabilization Force (ISF) as part of US President Donald Trump’s so-called Board of Peace.

World.title: Colombian embassy to open in Jerusalem, Israeli FM says
World.content:
Colombian President Abelardo De la Espriella had promised closer ties with Israel on the campaign trail.

Israel has announced that Colombia will open an embassy in Jerusalem, becoming the latest country to establish a diplomatic mission in the disputed city claimed as a capital by Israelis and Palestinians. Most countries have their embassies in Israel in Tel Aviv.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said Thursday the Latin American country’s embassy would open next week as he touted expanding relations with the region.

“Next Wednesday, we are going to inaugurate … the Colombian embassy,” Saar told attendees at a conference in Jerusalem.

An official at the Colombian Foreign Ministry in Bogota told AFP news agency the country’s Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar would travel to Jerusalem on Sunday ahead of the opening.

Colombian President Abelardo De la Espriella, who was sworn in as president in August, promised close relations with Israel during his election campaign. When he came into office, he restored diplomatic ties between Colombia and Israel. Colombia had previously severed ties with the country over Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.

The announcement comes as a small but growing list of countries has opted to route their diplomatic ties with Israel through Jerusalem.

Since 2018, the US, Guatemala, Paraguay, Kosovo, Honduras, Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Nauru and Somaliland, which has been recognised as an independent entity only by Israel, have opened embassies in the city.

Other countries that have diplomatic relations with Israel have located their embassies in Tel Aviv, as Jerusalem is not recognised by the international community as Israel’s capital.

“We will work hard because this is the diplomatic battle over the truth. And the truth is, Jerusalem was always the capital of one nation,” Saar said, dismissing Palestinian claims to the capital.



The Israeli minister said the Democratic Republic of the Congo would open its embassy in Jerusalem “very soon” and hinted at another opening.

“I think that with the possible results in Brazil, they might have the same move,” he said after right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro won the first round in the country’s presidential election.

Protesters in Colombia took to the streets of Bogota on Wednesday to rally against the new far-right government’s policy towards Israel, including the decision to open the Jerusalem embassy.

“When diplomatic relations with Israel were broken off, the message was that we would not be a nation complicit in their atrocities,” Nicolas Isaza, who took part in the protest, told Al Jazeera.

“Today our government is no longer drawing a line against the atrocities being committed in Palestine,” he added.

World.title: Two Latvian men arrested inside UK military base after breach
World.content:
Police say nothing so far suggests the incident at RAF Molesworth is linked ​to events surrounding RAF Fairford last month.

Two Latvian men have been arrested inside a military base in southeast England that houses United States and NATO intelligence hubs after the perimeter fence was breached, police have said.

The arrests come amid heightened concerns about security at military bases in the United Kingdom after a separate incident last month.

Counterterrorism police said on Thursday that the two men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested at the Royal Air Force (RAF) Molesworth base in Cambridgeshire.

They are being held on suspicion of trespass and of entering a prohibited place “for a purpose prejudicial to the UK”, said police.

A security patrol had spotted an abandoned vehicle near the base late on Wednesday night. Police found a “small breach” in the perimeter fence before locating and arresting the men in the early hours of Thursday, they said.

The men were taken to a police station in Cambridgeshire where they are still in custody. Both are Latvian nationals residing in the UK.

The arrests come after a major incident at RAF Fairford in western England on September 27 that led to the arrest of seven men, all in their 20s, who have since been released on bail. One is a dual UK-Iranian national.

No connection to RAF Fairford

Due to the nature of the incident, UK counterterrorism police are leading the investigation into the security breach, police said.

“We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites,” said Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London.



“But at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford,” she added.

Flanagan said that the investigation at RAF Molesworth is at an early stage but added that enquiries would home in on “any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site”.

RAF Molesworth, formerly a World War II airbase, is now a non-flying facility managed by the United States Air Force.

US intelligence has based its operation centres for Europe and Africa at the base near Huntingdon. It is also a NATO intelligence hub, according to a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) website.

On Sunday, US military planes were abruptly flown out of the RAF base at Fairford in Gloucestershire, after three suspicious vehicles were seen near the base, prompting a major incident to be declared.

That base had been used by the US military to conduct strikes in its war against Iran.

World.title: Hurricane Isaias charges towards the US Gulf Coast with dangerous winds
World.content:
The storm is forecast to strike Florida, Alabama and Mississippi with up to 10 inches of rain this weekend.

Share Hurricane Isaias charges towards the US Gulf Coast with dangerous winds on social media

Hurricane Isaias has intensified into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season as it barrels over record-warm water toward the northern shoreline of the United States Gulf Coast, prompting school closures and local government shutdowns.

According to the Miami-based National Hurricane Center, the storm is forecast to make landfall in parts of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi late Friday or early Saturday. The low-lying areas are especially vulnerable to flooding and storm surges.

The center warned residents in likely impact zones on Thursday to complete all emergency life-safety and property protections without delay.

It has also issued a hurricane watch from Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, through Indian Pass in the northwestern part of Florida in anticipation of torrential downpours and the substantial risk of localised flash and urban flooding.

A rainfall total of 3-6 inches is forecast with isolated peaks up to 10 inches.

“We are expecting Isaias to be a dangerous hurricane when it makes landfall,” Michael Brennan, director of the National Hurricane Center, said in a Thursday morning update, adding that he expects “up to near-major hurricane strength” by Friday as the storm pounds north of Mexico’s Yucatan Peninsula.

On Thursday morning, Isaias was packing maximum sustained winds of nearly 130km/h (80mph) with higher gusts. Heavy rain and flash flooding also threaten the inland areas throughout the weekend, extending as far as the Tennessee Valley and potentially encompassing a broad stretch from the inland southeast up through the southern Appalachian Mountains.



Ahead of the storm, oil and gas producers shut down a significant share of offshore production in the US Gulf, which accounts for almost 15 percent of crude pumped annually in the US.

As of Wednesday, about 25 percent of the oil production in the region had been temporarily halted, taking about 511,000 barrels a day off the market, according to the Marine Minerals Administration. It said eight of the Gulf’s 371 manned oil platforms had been evacuated.

With oil prices already high, the production cuts are steep enough to affect markets, though other Gulf hurricanes have caused larger disruptions, said Jim Burkhard, global head of crude oil market research for S&P Global Energy. More concerning, he said, is whether Isaias strikes as a powerful storm near refineries.

When Isaias was first declared a hurricane on Wednesday, it marked the latest date for an Atlantic season’s first hurricane in 121 years, falling just short of the record set in 1905, according to data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The season normally runs from June 1 through November 30.

World.title: Syria calls for independent probe into sinking of ship in Black Sea
World.content:
Syrian authorities questioned why search and rescue operations were called off before the fate of 10 sailors was known.

Share Syria calls for independent probe into sinking of ship in Black Sea on social media

Syria has called for an “independent and transparent” investigation into the sinking of a cargo ship in the Black Sea, demanding answers over the fate of the ship’s 10 crew members, including nine Syrians and an Egyptian, who remain unaccounted for.

The Togolese-flagged Alfa Watan, went down in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone early on Tuesday, amid a rising number of drone strikes hitting Black Sea shipping during the Russia-Ukraine war.

It is unclear who carried out the attack.

Mazen Aloush, from the Syria’s port authority asked the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and Bulgarian authorities to find out why a search and rescue mission was called off, before the missing sailors were found.

“Their fate is still unknown” said Aloush, adding that “the reasons that led to the suspension of search and rescue operations” had to be established.

The attack on Tuesday also hit the Palau-flagged Able, setting it ablaze. Eighteen Turkish and Indian crew members were rescued from the burning vessel, while the Alfa Watan sank.

Both commercial ships were managed by Turkey-based companies, according to the Equasis merchant shipping database.

The Syrian sailors’ union said contact with the ship’s crew had been lost and no survivors had been found after search operations were halted.

Aloush condemned the targeting of a civilian commercial vessel saying it was a serious breach of maritime security and a threat to sailors.



He said Syrian General Authority for Ports and Customs was closely monitoring the incident.

He urged ⁠authorities to use all available technical means to locate and inspect the wreckage to help establish what caused the ship to sink.

He called for international and maritime bodies to strengthen measures to help commercial shipping as attacks in the Black Sea rise.

World.title: US suspends Microsoft and Adobe from visa programme amid fraud claims
World.content:
Visa probe also targets universities for allegedly exploiting international students to reduce US wage costs.

Share US suspends Microsoft and Adobe from visa programme amid fraud claims on social media

The United States government is suspending several major tech companies, including Adobe and Microsoft, from a programme that gives skilled foreign workers a path to permanent residency amid allegations of fraud.

The move comes as the White House ramps up pressure on companies to hire more Americans. “Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” US Vice President JD Vance said at a news conference on Thursday.

Vance claimed that the Redmond, Washington-based tech giant laid off 6,000 American workers while obtaining 6,300 H-1B foreign work visas and almost 3,000 permanent residencies known as green cards.

“You cannot lay off American workers and replace them with foreign indentured servants,” Vance said.

Across the technology sector, there have been more than 131,000 layoffs in 2026 alone, according to Layoffs.fyi, which tracks job cuts across the tech and startup industries.

“When someone comes in, they are completely subordinate to that company. If they lose that job, they have to leave the country.”

Microsoft pushed back on Vance’s claims in a blog post, saying that “80 percent of the visas were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees.”

“The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country,” the company said in the post.

Microsoft is No 5 among US employers when it comes to using H-1B visas, according to data from US Citizenship and Immigration Services. Amazon is No 1.



Adobe did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling also said that several major information technology firms will be suspended from the programme as well. Among them are Indian tech giants Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services.

The H-1B programme has long been a target of supporters of US President Donald Trump who say that the programme undercuts American workers and is rife with abuse.

H-1B visas are meant for high-skilled jobs that are difficult to find US workers to fill. Technology companies are the biggest users, with nearly three-quarters of approvals going to workers from India.

The Department of Labor also said it had uncovered $22bn worth of visa fraud.

“Today we are protecting something far more valuable than any dollar amount. We are protecting the American worker,” Sonderling said.

The news came hours before Trump was to honour Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. India-born Nadella was one of six business leaders to be awarded on Thursday. Five of the leaders were foreign-born, including Tesla boss Elon Musk and Google co-founder Sergey Brin.

Crackdown on universities

During the news conference, officials also announced a crackdown on alleged J-1 visa fraud involving nine universities, including MIT, Harvard, Yale, Stanford and Cal State, amid allegations that they brought in international students to undercut US wages. A J-1 visa allows foreign nationals to enter the US temporarily for education or cultural programmes. Universities use these visas to bring in international PhD candidates or scholars.

Vance claimed that when schools employ an American as a researcher, that person earns $20,000 more than someone brought in under a J-1 visa.

Al Jazeera asked for data supporting this claim, but the White House did not respond.

Microsoft’s stock slumped 1.5 percent on the heels of the news, while Adobe was up 2.1 percent in late day trading on Thursday.

World.title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
World.content:
At least 30 people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the eastern front line city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials say.

Authorities said three people were also killed in the village of Bilenke, part of the Kramatorsk community.

Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting buses carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible.

Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Moscow is trying to seize as part of Russian President Vladimir Putin's claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said: "This strike will not go without our response."

In a post on Telegram, he said: "Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and the world needs to react to this. React harshly - exactly as the Russians deserve for all the deaths they have caused."

Images posted by local prosecutors showed the burning metal shell of the bus along with debris and some of the victims on the road.

Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack. It follows a dramatic surge in Russian attacks across Ukraine and a heavy increase in civilian casualties.

According to the UN, Ukraine saw more civilians killed by August this year than were killed in all of 2025.

In one single attack that destroyed a five-storey block of flats in Pryluky east of Kyiv early on Wednesday, 22 people were killed, including five children. Three of the children were only one year old.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who together with Zelensky visited the site of the Russian strike in Pryluky, said the attack showed Putin's "evil intent and evil strategy".

He announced "more sanctions on Russia, on the war machine of Putin, on the shadow fleet, on the oil companies, on the crypto, on the financing of the war" and told Zelensky the UK would stand with Ukraine "as long as it takes for you to prevail in this conflict".
