World.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
World.content:
Christa Pike is "up and walking" though mentally "foggy" while in hospital after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, her legal team says.

Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September. Experts described it as unprecedented.

Speaking late on Wednesday to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, lawyer Stephen Ferrell said he had not spoken to Pike directly but had learned her arms were swollen and barely functioning as she took her first steps around her hospital room.

A court has ordered state officials to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution.

That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state.

The Pike case is now in uncharted territory, as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

The failed execution was branded a "mess" by the mother of Slemmer, who was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death.

Pike's boyfriend at the time of Slemmer's gruesome murder, Tadaryl Shipp, was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.

Pike was 18 and Shipp was 17 when they beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.

World.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
World.content:
Prosecutors in the United States have accused Venezuela's former leader NicolÃ¡s Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, of conspiracy to commit torture.

The fresh charges against the couple were made public on Thursday and are in addition to the drug-trafficking and weapons charges already brought against them, which they have denied.

Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been in custody since January in a detention centre in Brooklyn, where they were taken after US forces seized them in a pre-dawn raid on their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.

Barry J Pollack, Maduro's attorney, said his client denies the new charges and looks forward to his day in court.

Federal prosecutors also announced on Thursday that Flores was added to the earlier narco-terrorism charge.

The trial for both Maduro and Flores is set to begin in June 2027.

Both are being held in a detention centre in Brooklyn and are expected to remain there after Flores's request to be moved to house arrest was denied by a judge on Thursday.

The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens who were being held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

The superseding indictment unsealed on Thursday accuses the former presidential couple of "entrenching themselves in power" by presiding "over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens".

According to the indictment, the torture included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture".

The prosecutors allege that the psychological torture included threats to kill victims' families, including children.

"All of this was done to ensure that Maduro and Flores retained their power," prosecutors said outside the courthouse on Thursday.

"This conduct, we allege, has caused significant harm to Americans, to US citizens", prosecutors said, calling it "the epitome of corruption".

World.title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis
World.content:
Pierina Nicuray, a 21-year-old university graduate, has spent a week camped out in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square.

Like many of the hundreds of others who have pitched their tents here to protest at Spain's housing crisis, she has no doubts when it comes to diagnosing the cause.

"It's the same problem as always," she says. "A lack of homes."

She adds: "Landlords are taking advantage of the situation to raise rentals, and then there's also Airbnb."

Jorge Moreno, a 19-year-old film-dubbing student who has also been living in a tent here in central Madrid for the last few days, agrees.

"There are so many homes standing empty because they have been bought by vulture funds and investment funds which hike up the rent of people living in properties until they get rid of them," says Jorge, who lives with his mother and fears it will be a long time before he can afford a home of his own.

"They've been making a business of housing for a long time," he adds. "But it's an abusive business which stops Spaniards from being able to live in a decent home."

His and Pierina's diagnoses are frequently voiced by fellow protesters, ordinary Spaniards and even the Spanish government.

On presenting a recent package of emergency measures to tackle the housing problem, Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said he was legislating "against those who consider housing just another object on the market with which to speculate".

Those reforms were rejected by Congress, prompting SÃ¡nchez to call a snap election next month.

Nicuray and Moreno can point to the single case that sparked the current Spanish housing protest movement as proof that profit-driven practices are at the heart of the crisis: the 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home after the investment firm that had bought it tried to persuade her to leave, then sharply increased her rent, which she was unable to pay.

Although the social backlash that followed caused the company to invite Abascal to return to her old home, she never did, dying in hospital on Wednesday.

World.title: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
World.content:
Italy's parliament has approved fiercely contested changes to the country's electoral system championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni ahead of elections due next year.

Lawmakers voted 227 to 164 in favour of moving to a fully proportional system, which Meloni has argued will boost the chance of clear winners and more stable government.

Opposition parties say her right-wing coalition has designed the proposals to improve its chance of retaining power and, in a heated debate on Thursday, accused it of pushing through the "fraudulent" reform to flout democracy.

Meloni had warned she could resign and trigger an early election if the plans were rejected, with the secret ballot seen as a test of her authority.

Meloni's coalition has overseen a rare period of political stability for Italy since her election in 2022, and last month her government became the country's longest-running since World War Two.

The voting reform will see the country move away from its current hybrid voting system, in which about a third of members are chosen through a first-past-the-post vote and the rest through proportional representation.

Parties proposing to form a coalition will be required to put forward their joint candidate for prime minister, and their political programme, before any general election.

A party or coalition which emerges with the largest share of the votes - provided this exceeds 42% - will be awarded 105 additional seats in parliament (70 in the lower house and 35 in the senate), which could turn a narrow victory into a more comfortable majority.

Centre-left members held up signs with slogans including "No to the scam" and "fraudulent law" during a debate ahead of the vote, and accused the government of forcing through the new voting rules.

World.title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says
World.content:
Campaign group Human Rights Watch (HRW) says the deportation of migrants from the US to third-party African countries is against the law and exploits suffering to deter migration.

"Many, if not most" of the deportees have no practical option but to return to their home countries regardless of the harm they face there, HRW says in a report.

Since Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025, more than 500 people have been sent to African countries where they are not citizens, the group says, citing US data.

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said "third country removals are an essential public safety tool that remove the most dangerous criminal illegal aliens from our streets".

Tackling immigration was one of Trump's key pledges during the 2024 election.

Eswatini, which welcomed 32 deportees from the US, says three people - from Yemen, Belize and Laos - "voluntarily departed" to their home countries recently.

According to HRW, some of the countries accepting the deportees have "arbitrarily detained" or sent them to their home countries, where they face "the risk of persecution or torture".

The group said that people sent to Eswatini, Ghana and South Sudan, had been arbitrarily detained and faced ill-treatment while in detention.

In Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and Ghana, the deportees had been sent to their countries of origin despite the risk of "violating the principle of nonrefoulement [that people should not be sent to a country where they face torture, cruel treatment, or threats to their life and freedom]", it said.

The group cited an unnamed US official as having told a Senate hearing that the point for the administration was that it could "threaten people that they will literally be dropped in the middle of nowhere".

"The point is to scare people," HRW said.

"Deporting people to countries where they have never set foot is part of a US policy designed to cause human suffering as a means to deter migration," said Michael Garcia Bochenek, the group's interim US programme director.

In a statement from to the BBC, DHS said: "ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] is given diplomatic assurances from destination countries that the illegal aliens being removed there will be safe. When an individual is no longer in ICE custody, ICE is no longer responsible for them."

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told the BBC that those being sent to third countries were those whose home nations refused to take them or who had court orders preventing them being sent home.

"Any illegal alien who wants to go home, we will arrange a free flight for them and give them a $3,000 check," she said.

None of the African countries named has commented on the report.

World.title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation
World.content:
A former teacher who sexually assaulted a student has been returned to jail in Indonesia after a BBC investigation revealed he was secretly released early.

Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani, known as Bechi, was sentenced to seven years in prison in 2022 after being convicted of sexually assaulting a female student at his father's prominent Islamic boarding school in East Java, where he worked as a teacher.

A BBC Eye undercover investigation revealed he was secretly released on parole in August 2025, after serving less than half his sentence. The woman he had been convicted of assaulting had not been informed - despite her legal right to know.

On hearing he was back in prison, she cried with relief.

"I pray that this doesn't happen to anyone else and that, going forward, the law will be applied justly in Indonesia," the former student, who wished to remain anonymous, told the BBC.

The Ministry of Immigration and Corrections previously told the BBC that Bechi was released because of sentence reductions granted in accordance with regulations.

But the BBC investigation sparked a public outcry and led to calls from lawmakers for an investigation, after which the government announced a comprehensive review.

That review found "errors" resulting in Bechi's parole being revoked. He has now been returned to prison.

Immigration and Corrections Minister Agus Andrianto told the BBC that those responsible for approving Bechi's parole "will certainly face sanctions".

"We want to make sure that such mistakes or irregularities do not happen again," he said.

World.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
World.content:
Police in central Chile have airlifted several residents to safety after rising floodwaters left them trapped in their homes.

Recent torrential rains caused the Mapocho river to burst its banks, flooding large parts of the city of Talagante, 35km (22 miles) south-west of the capital, Santiago.

Santiago has seen 74mm of rainfall in the first seven days of this month, making it the rainiest October for the area in 76 years, meteorologists have said.

They have warned that this year's unusually strong El NiÃ±o climate phenomenon will likely continue to bring unusually wet weather, powerful winds and storms to the region during the southern hemisphere's spring.

Officials said one person had been found dead in a flooded underpass in the city of San Bernardo, south of Santiago, although they have yet to confirm the cause of death.

In Talagante, police used helicopters to rescue people and pets living on the banks of the Mapocho who had been surprised by the fast-rising waters overnight.

Dirt roads turned into rivers in the riverside community which, unlike in July's storms, had not been evacuated ahead of the heavy downpours.

World.title: Everyone has a plan for Africa; but does Africa have the conviction to drive its own? (1), By Dipo Baruwa
World.content:
So why does it often appear that Africa has no plan? Why does everyone else appear able to impose or advance their own agendas on the continent? From my low-plains position, what Africa appears to be in short supply of is collective conviction, effective coordination and sustained implementation… Perhaps, therefore, the statement that “everyone has a plan for Africa except Africa” identifies the symptom but misdiagnoses the disease.

I was on LinkedIn the other day when I came across this screaming headline: “Everyone has a plan for Africa, except Africa.” At first, I was so engrossed by the headline that I thought, wow, what an apt description. The accompanying write-up reinforced the point by citing various engagements between Africa and its external partners, while also drawing attention to the fragmentation within Africa itself.

So yes, the headline is captivating. But it could also be very misleading. Perhaps it is another reminder of the old saying: do not judge a book by its cover.

What is more important to me in this reflection is not what the writer has argued. Rather, the headline triggered a different question for me: what has Africa continually missed because of its persistent tendency to privilege externally generated solutions over confidence in its own capacity?

It brings me to wonder what has happened to the Pan-African drive — an era when bold and incisive ideas of African self-determination were articulated and, in many cases, matched by equally ambitious attempts at implementation. Unfortunately, many of the early believers who articulated these visions were removed, undermined or isolated — sometimes with the complicity of fellow Africans and the support of external interests pursuing their own agendas on the continent.

The irony is difficult to ignore!

Who is Planning for whom, and for What?

There is nothing inherently wrong with other countries or regions having plans for Africa. In fact, it would be strange if they did not. China will naturally design its engagement with Africa around Chinese interests. The United Kingdom will pursue British interests. The European Union, the United States, India, Türkiye, the Gulf states and others will equally approach Africa through the prism of their own strategic, economic and geopolitical priorities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Isn’t that what states do?

The real question, therefore, is not why others have plans for Africa. It is whether Africa possesses sufficient collective agency to engage those plans from the standpoint of clearly articulated African interests.

And yes, that is what it should be: an African plan into which all other plans must fit.

Does Africa Have a Plan?

Across virtually every major development challenge confronting the continent, from infrastructure and industrialisation to trade, food security, energy, technology and human capital, there is hardly a shortage of declarations, protocols, strategies or institutions. The continent has the African Union. It has the African Continental Free Trade Area. It has the African Development Bank. It has Regional Economic Communities. It has Agenda 2063 and numerous continental, regional and national development frameworks.

Clearly, Africa does have a plan!

The Pan-African project must, therefore, confront perhaps its most difficult challenge: its own internal weaknesses. Africa’s future will not be determined primarily by speeches about African unity. It will be determined by whether African governments and institutions can translate collective ambitions into the everyday infrastructure of development: functioning transport corridors, interoperable payment systems, efficient borders…

So why does it often appear that Africa has no plan? Why does everyone else appear able to impose or advance their own agendas on the continent? From my low-plains position, what Africa appears to be in short supply of is collective conviction, effective coordination and sustained implementation.

Perhaps, therefore, the statement that “everyone has a plan for Africa except Africa” identifies the symptom but misdiagnoses the disease.

What Happened to the Pan-African Aspiration?

The early Pan-African idea was more than an emotional appeal to racial or continental solidarity. At its strongest, it represented an argument about agency: the belief that Africans must possess the political, economic and institutional capacity to determine the direction of their own socioeconomic and political development.

Independence was never supposed to end with the lowering of one flag and the raising of another. Political sovereignty for individual African states was intended to provide a foundation for economic transformation, deeper continental cooperation and a stronger African voice in shaping the international system.

Africa is not merely home to a distinct people and history. It also contains the largest number of sovereign states of any continent. Yet it has struggled to translate this numerical and collective weight into corresponding geopolitical and economic influence; somewhere along the journey, the political symbolism of Pan-Africanism appears to have overshadowed its economic and institutional foundations.

Since the creation of the African Union, African leaders have gathered around common declarations but have too often returned home to pursue narrowly defined national political interests. Countries have endorsed regional integration while simultaneously maintaining barriers against their neighbours. Governments celebrate the AfCFTA while trucks remain stranded at borders, customs systems remain poorly connected, and businesses continue to struggle to move goods across the continent.

There is, therefore, a significant difference between agreeing on a continental aspiration and building the institutional capability required to make it work.

And this work must begin within individual countries. Continental capability cannot exist independently of capable states. Strong national institutions, productive economies, efficient infrastructure and functioning domestic markets ultimately aggregate into continental strength.

The Pan-African project must, therefore, confront perhaps its most difficult challenge: its own internal weaknesses. Africa’s future will not be determined primarily by speeches about African unity. It will be determined by whether African governments and institutions can translate collective ambitions into the everyday infrastructure of development: functioning transport corridors, interoperable payment systems, efficient borders, productive industries, reliable energy, skilled labour, deeper financial markets, and institutions capable of coordinating across national boundaries.

That is where Pan-Africanism moves from political symbolism to developmental action.

That process of self-discovery is itself part of development. There will always be opportunities for policy learning, adaptation and knowledge transfer from elsewhere. But the importance of self-discovery in building domestic capability cannot be discounted. An imported solution may tell us what worked somewhere else; it cannot automatically give us the accumulated knowledge of why it worked, how it evolved or what must change for it to work here.

The Danger of Continually Looking Outward

There is another dimension to the problem. African policymaking has often demonstrated considerable confidence in solutions that arrive from elsewhere. We borrow development models. We import institutional templates. We reproduce policy frameworks. We engage consultants to explain what successful countries have done and sometimes proceed as though development were merely a matter of replicating those arrangements locally.

But development rarely works that way; there is, of course, no one-size-fits-all solution!

While the problem is not learning from elsewhere; at least every successful economy has borrowed, adapted and learnt from others. The problem arises when transplantation substitutes for adaptation and domestic institutional learning. This mostly occurs when domestic and continental institutions fail to accumulate their own problem-solving capabilities; the temptation to look elsewhere for ready-made answers becomes even stronger.

Institutions are not merely pieces of organisational architecture that can be lifted from one society and transplanted into another. Behind every successful model lies a history of experimentation, mistakes, adaptation, political negotiation and institutional learning. Before the successful model becomes visible, there is often a much less visible process of failure, learning, self-conviction, purposeful experimentation and commitment to particular objectives.

This matters because when models are imported without sufficient participation by local actors or adaptation to domestic circumstances, what may be acquired is the visible structure without the capability required to make it work.

This is why stumbling should not always be interpreted as failure; learning is achieved by doing. Institutions develop through repeated experimentation. Policies are adjusted when they encounter realities their designers did not anticipate. Governments discover what their economies can produce competitively, which capabilities are missing and which interventions generate unintended consequences.

That process of self-discovery is itself part of development. There will always be opportunities for policy learning, adaptation and knowledge transfer from elsewhere. But the importance of self-discovery in building domestic capability cannot be discounted. An imported solution may tell us what worked somewhere else; it cannot automatically give us the accumulated knowledge of why it worked, how it evolved or what must change for it to work here.

And, that is perhaps where Africa must begin looking inward; not to isolate itself from the world, but to build the capability required to engage it on its own terms.

Dipo Baruwa is a business climate development analyst.

World.title: Leadership and storytelling in election season, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
On the economy, we tell the story of renewal and hard times. As elections draw near, we hear official accounts of macroeconomic progress. But the story must connect today’s pain with tomorrow’s promise. When people ask the government what it has done with savings from the removal of petrol subsidy, for example, they are testing the coherence of the economic narrative. Leaders must answer not only with policy but with story – why this pain, for how long, and toward what end?

I keep a weekly diary, which is my own way of telling different stories about Nigeria and the world, encompassing politics, the economy, society, and our endless search for leaders who can make promises and deliver results. Sometimes, I stir the pot of Nigeria’s public life.

Of course, we know about the danger of the single story, but that’s not what I will address today. Stories shape societies. Compelling stories create impact that shapes the future. And leaders who fail to tell honest stories shape nothing but frustration and disappointment.

A Story from the Trenches

In 2004, in a bedroom in Kaduna, Sam Nda-Isaiah and his wife, Zainab, conceived the idea of a newspaper. She told the story before of how her husband got up in the wee hours, scribbled a few things in a jotter, and asked what she thought. That idea, born in intimacy and nurtured in courage, later became LEADERSHIP newspaper.

The question before us is simple: What stories are today’s leaders telling, and what leaders will those stories produce tomorrow?

Anatomy of Impactful Story-telling

I have learnt over the years that storytelling is not decoration. It is a discipline. Every leader – whether in government, business, civil society, or the media – is a storyteller. The question is not whether you tell stories, but what kind of stories you tell, how you tell them, and whether they have the impact you intend.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Dele Giwa, Ray Ekpu, Chinua Achebe, Wole Soyinka, and Mahmoud Jega are some of my favourite storytellers. Also, I have watched politicians craft narratives that have lifted nations, as I have seen them tell stories that inflame, incite and destroy. I have seen corporate leaders build empires on the back of compelling vision, and others lose everything to the gravity of their own contradictions.

But let me start from home, with a story my mother told me, which I have often shared with my two wonderful grandchildren, Ezhinne, 7, and Ekeneolise, 5.

It’s about two siblings who ventured into parts of a forbidden forest in defiance of their mother’s advice. Thanks to the older sibling’s pressure, the two young girls’ curiosity led them into an evil forest, where evil men captured them.

For days, the girls refused to eat or drink. To survive, they later yielded and took some food.

One day, they caught their watchers off guard and escaped. When the chief priest heard, he charged the strongest demons in the land to pursue the girls, who didn’t know that the meals they had eaten had bound them to the evil forest. What was worse for the fleeing girls was that the people of the evil forest had a song that, when recited, slowed any runaway captive.

The song goes like this: “Ori ni iji nmo, ota n’oka nmo okpiri gbue ye, ndalu ndalu, gbue, gbu, nko, nko, gbue ba’sa ndalu, ndalu, ndalu….”

First, the story must be genuine – and it may be improvised/aspirational, like my mother’s story, or true. Not just technically true, but emotionally, circumstantially, and contextually true and relatable. It also should be morally coherent. A leader who tells a story that people cannot feel in their bones will not lead for long.

The harder the girls ran, the slower they moved, especially as the song’s words echoed behind them. Roughly translated from Ukwani to English, the song invokes the demons to speedily kill whoever has eaten the food of the evil forest.

By sheer instinct, and almost exhausted, the younger of the two girls turned the song around. Here was how she sang it:

“Ori ni iji nmo, ota n’oka nmo okpiri sa’a ya, ndalu ndalu, sa’a ya, nko, nko, sa’a ya be gbue ndalu, ndalu, ndalu….”

Roughly translated, the song says the gods should be merciful and spare whoever has eaten the food of the evil forest.

That response weakened the spell and gave the fleeing girls speed. The ding-dong continued until finally, the girls crossed over to safety, but not without their pursuers leaving a huge mark on their backs, which is the gutter we all bear behind our backs today!

The moral of that story was: if you don’t listen to your parents, there will be consequences that may not only affect you, but outlive you!

Impactful Storytelling

First, the story must be genuine – and it may be improvised/aspirational, like my mother’s story, or true. Not just technically true, but emotionally, circumstantially, and contextually true and relatable. It also should be morally coherent. A leader who tells a story that people cannot feel in their bones will not lead for long.

When Mr Peter Obi speaks, whether you agree with him or not, you feel a sense of conviction or ambivalence. When former Vice President Atiku Abubakar speaks of experience, you hear the burden of six attempts. When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu speaks of renewal, you either feel hope or exhaustion, depending on where you stand.

Second, the story must be timely. A story told too early is ignored. A story told too late could be irrelevant. The art of leadership is knowing when the moment is ripe for the narrative.

Third, the story must be actionable. A story that inspires but does not instruct is entertainment, not leadership.

The story is not over. And I challenge you to tell it. Nigeria’s story is not over. The question is: what kind of story will we tell together, and what kind of leadership will that story produce?.. I believe in Nigeria not because it is perfect, but because its story is still being written. I believe in leadership not because leaders are flawless, but because leaders who tell the right stories can inspire flawed people to do great things.

What Stories Are We Telling?

Let me turn the mirror on ourselves. What stories are Nigeria’s leaders telling today, and what leadership will those stories produce tomorrow?

On the economy, we tell the story of renewal and hard times. As elections draw near, we hear official accounts of macroeconomic progress. But the story must connect today’s pain with tomorrow’s promise. When people ask the government what it has done with savings from the removal of petrol subsidy, for example, they are testing the coherence of the economic narrative. Leaders must answer not only with policy but with story – why this pain, for how long, and toward what end?

The Media Shaping Stories

Let me speak directly to the leaders and organisers of this forum who are building tomorrow’s leaders. We are not just observers of leadership stories; we are co-authors. Commentary is not enough. We must also curate, contextualise, and challenge the stories that leaders tell.

We must tell stories that protect national interest without descending into propaganda.

A Call to Today’s Leaders

To the leaders in this room, and future leaders, whether in government, business, civil society, academia or whatever, I say this: your story is your legacy.

I was a boy from Ajegunle who entered the University of Lagos journalism programme with no patron but plenty of promise. Many years later, I am still here, writing, mentoring, and believing that Nigeria’s story is worth telling, well and often. I have won awards, written books, and stirred controversies.

But the award that matters most is the one I cannot hold: the knowledge that my storytelling has contributed, in some small way, to a better understanding of Nigeria and a stronger commitment to its future.

You have the same opportunity. Your story — told with truth, timed with wisdom, and translated into action – can shape tomorrow’s leadership. Do not waste it.

The Story Continues

The story is not over. And I challenge you to tell it. Nigeria’s story is not over. The question is: what kind of story will we tell together, and what kind of leadership will that story produce?

I believe in Nigeria not because it is perfect, but because its story is still being written. I believe in leadership not because leaders are flawless, but because leaders who tell the right stories can inspire flawed people to do great things.

Learn to tell stories that matter. Tell stories that move. Tell stories that make tomorrow’s leaders proud of the foundations you laid today. It’s your life. It’s your story. Tell it. Live it!

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

This article was adapted from “Storytelling for Impact: Today’s LeadHERS for Tomorrow’s Leadership,” on October 8, a presentation at an event by The Young Communicators Initiative to mark this year’s International Day of the Girl Child.

World.title: Military Plane Crash: Air Chief sets up probe panel, assures adequate support for bereaved families
World.content:
The Chief of Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, an air marshal, says he has directed the constitution of a panel to investigate the recent crash of a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft at Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area, Ondo State.

Mr Aneke disclosed this on Thursday when he visited the crash site.

The aircraft crashed on Monday while on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos.

The NAF authorities said 25 persons were on board the aircraft.

However, three days after the crash, all hope of any survivor has been lost.

Apart from the deployment of heavy machinery, which cleared the bushes around and dug deep into the swamp, the main body of the plane is still trapped beneath the mud.

The air chief, who was accompanied by some senior officers of the force, described the incident as a great loss.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I had informed my Superintendent of Safety and Evaluation to come up with a high-level delegation comprising both military and civilian safety experts, NTSB, Accident and Emergency Management Board, retired senior officers, experienced air force officers, to sit down and get to the bottom of what happened,” he said.

“This is not the time to start speculating, and I plead with you, and the general public, we’ve lost people who are fighting for the nation. The best we can do for them is to be a little bit patient and let those who are the specialists get to the bottom of what has happened.”

Mr Aneke, who did not give further details of the probe, sympathised with the families of those who have lost their loved ones in the tragic incident.

“I basically knew everyone on that flight. I’ve flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. Highly trained, professional, and intelligent officers,” he said.

“I want to assure the families of our loved ones that the Nigerian Armed Forces will keep you on guard in ensuring that you are safe.

“The Nigerian Air Force is putting everything possible to ensure that the families get the necessary support they need.”

READ ALSO: Eight soldiers reported dead as troops foil terror attack in Borno

The air chief commended the people and government of Ondo State for committing resources, time and energy in the recovery efforts.

“The locals here, the residents here, were the first responders. I’ve been briefed by the commander of the Naval base here. Words cannot describe how we Nigerians come together when things go sour,” he added.

The Ondo State Government had deployed two swamp buggies to aid access to the crash site and also assist in digging out the plane.

The state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, however, expressed concerns over the inability of the rescue teams to locate the main body of the plane after putting so much effort in over the last three days.

Only torn clothes, body parts, and pieces of the plane’s panels had been brought to shore.

World.title: Nigerian Photographer Bolaji Alonge’s Photos Featured in New Fela Kuti ‘Zombie’ Vinyl
World.content:
Nigerian photographer Bolaji Alonge’s photographs of the New Afrika Shrine in Lagos have been featured in a new limited-edition vinyl release of Fela Kuti’s Zombie.

The edition is a collaboration between American fashion brand Denim Tears and the Fela Kuti Estate, with designer Tremaine Emory reimagining the album’s packaging.

According to Partisan Records, Emory used photographs of the New Afrika Shrine taken by Mr Alonge, along with elements from Nigerian artist Lemi Ghariokwu’s original artwork. The new design was created to connect the album back to Lagos and the Shrine while paying tribute to Mr Ghariokwu’s original work.

The release, limited to 1,000 vinyl copies, is scheduled for 9 October. The records will be available through Dover Street Market in London, Turntable Lab in the United States, and the online stores of Partisan Records and Fela Kuti.

How Alonge’s Photos Became Part of ‘Zombie’

Mr Alonge’s photographs were taken at the New Afrika Shrine, a Lagos venue closely associated with Fela Kuti’s musical legacy.

Fela’s original Afrika Shrine was the Lagos venue where he built his reputation as a musician and political voice. The New Afrika Shrine later became part of the Kuti family’s efforts to preserve and continue that legacy.

For the new Zombie edition, Mr Emory chose photographs from that contemporary Lagos setting and placed them alongside the original album’s visual language.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The result connects two periods of Fela’s history: the era in which Zombie was created and the present-day cultural life surrounding the New Afrika Shrine.

Mr Alonge has spent years documenting Lagos and Nigerian culture through his photography project, Eyes of a Lagos Boy. His work includes images connected to the Kuti family, Afrobeat, and the New Afrika Shrine.

His photographs now form part of the physical packaging of one of Fela’s most recognised albums.

New look for Fela’s ‘Zombie’

Fela released Zombie in 1976, and the album became one of his best-known works and a major part of his criticism of Nigeria’s military government.

The title track criticised soldiers who blindly followed orders, comparing them to zombies.

The album angered the military government. On February 18, 1977, soldiers attacked Fela’s Kalakuta Republic in Lagos, setting the compound on fire and assaulting people inside. Fela’s mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was thrown from a window during the attack and later died from injuries linked to the incident.

The original Zombie album artwork was designed by Lemi Ghariokwu.

For the new edition, Emory has combined elements of Ghariokwu’s original artwork with Alonge’s photographs of the New Afrika Shrine.

According to Partisan Records, the new packaging was designed to connect the album to Lagos and the Shrine while giving it a new visual identity.

From Lagos to a new generation

The new edition comes as Fela’s music and legacy continue to attract attention worldwide.

Fela was posthumously inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2026 and received the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award this year. His music and influence have also continued to inspire artists across music, fashion and visual culture.

For Alonge, the new edition adds another chapter to his work documenting Lagos and its cultural history.

His photographs, originally made in Lagos, will now appear on a limited physical edition of an album whose history is deeply connected to the city and to Fela’s political and musical legacy.

World.title: Customs seize three live pangolins in suspected wildlife-trafficking operation in Ogun
World.content:
The Nigeria Customs Service has intercepted three live pangolins allegedly being smuggled through Ogun State, in the latest seizure highlighting the illegal trade of one of the world’s most trafficked mammals.

The endangered animals were intercepted by officers of the Ogun I Area Command, Idiroko, at Abeokuta waterside following credible intelligence, according to the command.

It stated that the animals were found confined in wire-mesh cages and concealed inside sacks in what Customs described as an attempt to evade detection. It added that the suspected traffickers fled after sighting the Customs patrol team.

The spokesperson for the command, Chado Zakari, said the manner in which the animals were concealed showed the cruelty associated with the illegal wildlife trade.

“The pangolins were found tightly bound in sacks, a cruel method of concealment used by wildlife traffickers to evade detection,” Mr Zakari said.

He said the packaging also suggested that the seizure may be connected to an organised wildlife-trafficking operation.

“Upon inspection, officers discovered three pangolins confined in wire mesh cages and concealed within a sack. The sophisticated packaging suggests the involvement of an organised smuggling syndicate,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Following the interception, the Acting Customs Area Controller of Ogun I Command, Abdulhamid Ibrahim, handed the three pangolins over to Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation for rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected habitat.

Mr Ibrahim said the seizure demonstrated the command’s commitment to combating wildlife trafficking alongside its conventional anti-smuggling operations.

He, however, warned people involved in the illegal wildlife trade to desist.

“Trafficking pangolins and their derivatives attracts severe penalties. Under the recently passed Endangered Species Conservation and Protection Bill, offenders risk fines of up to A12 million and prison terms of up to 10 years.

“The Nigeria Customs Service, in collaboration with Green Finger Wildlife and other stakeholders, remains resolute in enforcing these laws to protect the nation’s biodiversity,” Mr Ibrahim said.

He commended the officers involved in the operation and said the command would continue working with conservation organisations to tackle the illegal wildlife trade.

Receiving the animals, the Administrative Manager/Supervisor of Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation, Isaac Ime, commended the Customs command for intercepting the animals.

Mr Ime assured that the organisation would provide the necessary care for the rescued pangolins and work towards their rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected environment.

The seizure comes amid growing concern over Nigeria’s role in the international trafficking of pangolin products.

Researchers have identified Nigeria as a major transit hub for pangolin trafficking, with Nigerian-linked seizures involving hundreds of thousands of kilogrammes of pangolin scales over the years.

Why keeping a pangolin is illegal

Pangolins are not animals that individuals can simply capture from the wild and keep as pets or for commercial purposes in Nigeria.

The Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act places pangolin species listed in its schedules under legal protection. The law prohibits the hunting, capture and trade of species listed in its First Schedule.

READ ALSO: Fire guts Customs office in Lagos

Also, NESREA said its enforcement covers the possession and display of endangered wildlife specimens and products.

NESREA specifically warned in March 2026 that individuals cannot possess, display or trade endangered wildlife specimens on social media, listing pangolins among the species affected by the prohibition.

The agency said the restrictions are based on Nigeria’s environmental laws and its obligations under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

In CITES Appendix I, Pangolins were given the highest level of protection against international commercial trade. WhileNigeria’s existing wildlife legislation separately prohibits the hunting, capture or trade of pangolins listed under the Endangered Species Act.

In March, the Federal High Court in Lagos jailed two men after pleading guilty to charges involving the unlawful possession and trade of three live pangolins.

World.title: Lagos records 1,324 fire, building-collapse, other emergency incidents in nine months
World.content:
The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service says it responded to 1,324 emergency incidents between January and September, with fire calls accounting for 1,135 of the cases.

The agency revealed this in its third-quarter activity report, highlights of which spokesperson Maria Fadairo shared in a statement posted on Facebook on Thursday.

The report listed 79 rescue calls, 100 salvage operations, nine collapsed-building incidents and one gas-related explosion among the emergencies handled during the period.

Ms Fadairo explained that 210 people were rescued, while 65 suspected corpses were recovered from emergency scenes.

The service also recorded 341 false emergency calls.

The Controller-General of the service, Margaret Adeseye, noted that the figures highlighted the need for residents to take greater care as the dry season approaches.

“The statistics underscore the importance of sustained consciousness, prompt reporting of emergencies and strict compliance with fire-safety regulations across the State,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Adeseye stressed that false emergency calls could delay firefighters responding to genuine emergencies.

The service estimated that property worth N79.44 billion was saved during the period, while losses were put at N13.24 billion. Property affected was valued at an estimated N92.68 billion.

January recorded highest incidents

January had the highest number of emergency incidents, with 203 cases, followed by March with 201.

September had the lowest, with 94 incidents.

March recorded the highest number of fire calls, with 176, while January had 173. September had the lowest number, with 80.

With the dry season approaching, Ms Adeseye advised residents to avoid indiscriminate burning and to exercise caution when storing or handling flammable materials.

She urged residents to switch off electrical appliances when they are not in use, avoid overloading sockets and ensure fire extinguishers are functional.

Property owners should also keep escape routes and access points clear to allow firefighters to reach buildings during emergencies, she said.

READ ALSO: LAWMA withdraws licences of six waste operators in Lagos

She urged residents to report fires promptly and cooperate with emergency responders at incident scenes.

150 more firefighters approved

The figures come against the backdrop of efforts by the Lagos government to strengthen its emergency response capacity.

In January, the government approved the recruitment of 150 additional firefighters.

Lagos has also recorded major fire incidents this year. In January, firefighters contained a warehouse fire in the Amuwo-Odofin Industrial Layout, where hundreds of 200-litre drums containing highly flammable materials were reportedly stored.

In 2024, the fire service reported 1,607 fire incidents in the state and estimated that property worth N117.12 billion was salvaged.

The service said it would continue with fire prevention, public education and enforcement of fire-safety standards across the state.

World.title: Court reserves ruling on Taraba APC chairmanship primary dispute
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Jalingo, Taraba State, has reserved ruling in a suit challenging the exclusion of Abdulhadi Haruna Lau from the All Progressives Congress (APC) state chairmanship primary.

Justice Mashkur Salisu reserved ruling on Wednesday after lawyers representing the parties adopted their arguments in the case.

Mr Lau is asking the court to invalidate the primary, arguing that he was qualified to contest but was prevented from participating despite completing the processes required by the party.

His lawyer, Musa Attah, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), told the court that Mr Lau paid the required fees and was issued a receipt but was subsequently denied the form needed to contest the election.

“He was denied the form to contest after paying the money,” Mr Attah argued.

The lawyer also urged the court to reject the argument that the dispute was purely an internal matter of the APC and therefore beyond judicial intervention.

He argued that the circumstances surrounding Mr Lau’s exclusion raised issues capable of being examined by the court because they affected his participation in the party’s electoral process.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

APC asks court to dismiss suit

The APC, through its counsel, Festus Kayode, SAN, urged the court to dismiss the suit.

Mr Kayode argued that the documents placed before the court had been properly executed and that the dispute concerned the internal administration of the political party.

He maintained that the court lacked jurisdiction to interfere with the party’s decision on the eligibility of an aspirant to contest its internal election.

Counsel to the second defendant, John Okezie, also opposed the suit.

Mr Okezie argued that although Mr Lau paid for the aspiration form, he failed to fulfil another financial requirement prescribed by the party.

He specifically alleged that the plaintiff did not pay the ‘penalty’ fee required under the APC constitution.

The defence further argued that Mr Lau failed to produce evidence of payment of the penalty fee or documentation from the APC National Working Committee confirming his eligibility to participate in the primary.

Two key issues before court

The opposing arguments have left two major questions for determination: whether Mr Lau fulfilled all the requirements to contest the APC chairmanship position and whether the Federal High Court has jurisdiction to intervene in the party’s decision to exclude him from the primary.

Mr Lau’s legal team maintains that he completed the necessary procedures and was denied the opportunity to contest without a valid justification.

The APC and the second defendant, however, contend that he failed to meet the party’s requirements and that the court should not interfere in the party’s internal affairs.

With the parties having concluded their arguments, Justice Salisu reserved ruling in the matter.

The date for the ruling is expected to be communicated to the parties by the court.

World.title: Outrage over video showing FRSC officers allegedly beating motorist in Nasarawa
World.content:
A video showing officials of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) repeatedly hitting and kicking a man during a roadside encounter in Lafia, Nasarawa State, has triggered outrage online.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 8 a.m. on Tuesday along Makurdi Road in Lafia, with the man identified by his family as Hassan Babalawal.

The footage circulating online shows at least four men dressed in FRSC uniforms confronting Mr Babalawal, who is seen on the ground as some of the officials appear to punch and kick him.

A person filming the incident can be heard questioning the officials’ actions and saying the man had not fought them.

The video has prompted criticism from Nigerians who questioned the use of physical force by officials responsible for road safety and traffic enforcement.

The reactions have largely focused on the apparent imbalance between the officials and the man, particularly the footage showing him on the ground while the confrontation continued.

But the video does not establish what happened before the recording began or what prompted the confrontation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Babalawal’s elder brother told SaharaReporters that an FRSC patrol team stopped his brother along Makurdi Road before the confrontation.

He alleged that the officers assaulted Mr Babalawal despite the family being unaware of any offence he had committed.

The family said the incident caused Mr Babalawal physical and emotional distress and called on FRSC authorities to identify the officers captured in the footage and investigate their conduct.

The family also said it was prepared to provide photographs, medical reports, eyewitness accounts and other evidence that could assist an investigation.

“We are not seeking to obstruct the lawful duties of the FRSC,” the elder brother said, according to SaharaReporters. “Our concern is simply that no citizen should be subjected to unjustified physical assault or harassment.”

The family has specifically appealed to the FRSC Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, and the Nasarawa State Sector Commander to investigate the incident and take appropriate action if the officers are found to have acted unlawfully.

The incident has renewed questions about the conduct of uniformed personnel during roadside enforcement and the limits of force that may be used when motorists or other road users resist or dispute enforcement actions.

The FRSC is responsible for road safety administration, traffic management and enforcement of relevant road-traffic regulations. Its personnel are expected to carry out those duties professionally and within the law.

The Corps has previously investigated viral videos involving alleged misconduct by its personnel.

In one such case reported by PREMIUM TIMES, the FRSC said it investigated a viral video involving a confrontation between its officers and a tricycle rider and said disciplinary measures had been taken against staff involved in the incident.

PREMIUM TIMES contacted the spokesperson of the FRSC in Nasarawa State for the Corps’ reaction to the incident. He said the Sector Commander would issue a statement on the development.

Watch the video of the incident: Video of the alleged FRSC assault in Lafia

World.title: Trump misnames Muslim Senate candidate ‘Mohammed’
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump. Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

A Muslim candidate for US Senate accused Donald Trump of “struggling” on Thursday after the president misnamed him “Mohammed” on social media amid increasingly bitter exchanges between the two men.

Trump attacked the left-wing Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed on his Truth Social platform, baselessly accusing him of being a “Terrorist Sympathizer.”

El-Sayed, an Arab American running for a Michigan Senate seat that could decide which party wins the US upper chamber in knife-edge midterm elections next month, said “I think Donald might be struggling a little bit.”

“He thinks my name’s Mohammed … My name’s Abdul, and you know it. And the only reason he won’t say it is I keep ripping you,” El-Sayed said at a campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

“So try again and get it right because we’re going to teach you how to say it properly,” he added to laughter at a restaurant photo-op, where he was joined by Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer and Delaware Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester.

Like many Muslim men, El-Sayed’s middle name is Mohamed, but he does not use it publicly.

Trump and his supporters have fixated on El-Sayed, accusing him and his family of ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and the Al-Qaeda jihadist group.

Trump said El-Sayed, locked in a knife-edge race with Republican Mike Rogers, was the “best friend” of “America Hating Hasan Piker,” the left-wing influencer who campaigned for El-Sayed during the Democratic primary.

The Michigan Senate seat is considered essential to Democratic hopes of regaining the Senate.

The party aims to retain the Michigan seat in Democratic hands while wresting four other seats in the 100-member chamber from Republicans.

The midwestern state backed Trump in the 2024 presidential election, even as Democrat Elissa Slotkin narrowly defeated Rogers for Michigan’s other Senate seat.

El-Sayed was backed by progressive leaders including Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Elizabeth Warren, as well as the United Auto Workers union.

His platform includes health care for all, higher taxes on billionaires, ending unconditional US military aid to Israel and reducing the role of corporate money in elections.

AFP

World.title: SDP’s Adebayo likens FG’s 30-day petrol discount to ‘Fuji House of Commotion’
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate Prince Adewole Adebayo has likened the Federal Government’s 30-day petrol discount through the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) to the popular television series “Fuji House of Commotion.”

The Federal Government announced the petrol discount on Thursday, giving public transport operators priority under the arrangement.

Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the measure was not a return to subsidy, but an arrangement for NNPC to sell petrol at cost for the initial 30-day period.

Reacting to the announcement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, Adebayo questioned the basis and duration of the intervention, describing it as a temporary gesture rather than a long-term policy.

“I saw the visual and heard of the policy or statement; I don’t know. There is no plan behind it, so I cannot know whether it is a policy or a gesture, but it immediately reminds me of a series on television in the 90s called ‘Fuji House of Commotion.’

“One thing they are presenting is Tinubu’s house of commotion. It does not make any sense in any way.

“Number one, none of those people who are seated there represent the NNPC. Now, there is no account established in the Ministry of Finance that deals with the petroleum subsidy account.

“One month is not short term; it is not medium term; it is not long term; it is a flash in the moment.

“They did not refer to any law that authorises them to do what they are doing.

“So, long and short, it looks to me like the government is genuinely now and sincerely confused because they have created problems for themselves.”

World.title: 10 measures FG announced to cushion rising petrol prices
World.content:
The Federal Government has announced 10 measures aimed at cushioning the impact of rising petrol prices on households, businesses and transport users across Nigeria.

The measures were announced by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during a press briefing on fuel prices and the subsidy question in Abuja on Thursday.

According to the government, the measures are designed to provide relief to Nigerians affected by higher petrol prices without

returning to a blanket fuel subsidy.

Here are the 10 measures announced by the Federal Government:

1. 30-day petrol discount at NNPC stations

The Federal Government will provide a margin discount on petrol sold by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited for the next 30 days.

Priority will be given to public transport operators across the country.

Oyedele said the arrangement would allow petrol to be sold at cost during the period and stressed that it does not amount to a return to fuel subsidy.

2. More crude oil for local refineries

The government plans to increase forward sales of crude oil to domestic refineries as crude production rises.

The move is expected to make more crude available to local refiners and reduce their exposure to fluctuations in international crude prices.

According to the government, the arrangement would help provide greater stability for domestic petrol prices.

3. N1,350 ceiling on petrol landing cost

The Federal Government is negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 per litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol.

Under the proposed arrangement, refiners and importers would absorb the difference when costs rise above the ceiling and recover it when crude prices or the exchange rate become more favourable.

Oyedele said the arrangement was designed to smooth out price fluctuations rather than permanently control petrol prices.

The ceiling would be reviewed monthly, with the figures published for transparency.

4. Removal of illegal levies

The government will work with state governments to tackle illegal road taxes and levies that increase the cost of transporting goods and services.

The measure will be pursued under the 2025 tax reform laws.

The government believes reducing these additional costs could help lower the cost of moving goods across the country.

5. More support for vulnerable Nigerians

The Federal Government plans to increase cash transfers to vulnerable households affected by rising living costs.

It also plans to provide subsidised credit to small businesses and consumers.

The government said it would also work with the National Assembly on enhanced tax relief for low-income earners under the 2027 Finance Bill.

6. Faster rollout of CNG vehicles

The government will accelerate the deployment of compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles across Nigeria.

Federal and state governments are expected to support the rollout, while transport operators will be encouraged to pass savings from the cheaper fuel source on to passengers.

The government sees wider CNG adoption as a way of reducing dependence on petrol and lowering transportation costs.

7. Excess profit tax for operators

The Federal Government said it would consider an excess profit tax for businesses found to be taking undue advantage of the situation along the energy value chain.

Oyedele said proceeds from the measure would be used exclusively to cushion the impact of fuel prices.

The government plans to channel the funds into transport support or vouchers for urban minimum-wage earners who are particularly vulnerable to rising costs.

8. Reduction of regulatory costs

The government will seek to reduce unnecessary regulatory requirements and costs imposed on businesses.

According to the government, these costs ultimately increase the prices of goods and services paid by consumers.

Reducing regulatory burdens is therefore expected to help businesses manage higher operating costs and limit further price increases.

9. Establishment of a National Strategic Fuel Reserve

The Federal Government plans to establish a National Strategic Fuel Reserve to strengthen the country’s fuel supply security.

Under the proposed system, refined petroleum products could be released into the market during global disruptions or periods of artificial scarcity.

The government said the reserve would not be used to fix petrol prices but would help prevent supply disruptions, market manipulation and sudden price shocks.

10. Better traffic and logistics management

The government plans to improve traffic management in urban areas to reduce fuel consumption and logistics costs.

It also intends to use NIPOST address codes to make logistics operations more efficient and cheaper.

The government believes better traffic and delivery systems could reduce the amount of fuel wasted on transportation while lowering the cost of moving goods.

Vanguard News

World.title: Ex-Obi campaign members launch platform for Tinubu
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Former members of the 2023 Presidential Campaign Council of Peter Obi have launched a political platform, Batified Obidients, declaring their support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his Renewed Hope Agenda ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The group said its decision to support Tinubu followed what it described as months of reflection on its experience during Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign.

In a statement signed on Thursday by its National Coordinator, Adesina Fagbenro-Byron, the group said it would work for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 and support efforts to ensure the success of his second term.

The statement was also signed by the group’s regional coordinators: Bala Abubakar, North-West; Ekana Simeon Lamorde, North-East; Daniel Gambo, North-Central; Banwo Mayowa, South-West; Izunna Desmond, South-South; and Odira Alexander, South-East.

The group said it would draw on the professional experience of its members from the Obi campaign to mobilise former Obi supporters, undecided voters and other Nigerians around the Renewed Hope Agenda.

It also said it would work to increase Tinubu’s 2023 presidential vote tally, which stood at 8,794,726, according to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

According to the group, it would particularly focus on states where Obi secured victories in 2023, while seeking to build support for Tinubu across the country.

Why we left Obi — group

Explaining its decision, the group said its members had reached the conclusion that Obi did not possess some of the leadership qualities they considered necessary to govern Nigeria.

It said the assessment was based on its experience working within the 2023 campaign and was not motivated by personal animosity.

The group alleged that it observed what it described as weaknesses in diversity management, talent utilisation and internal conflict resolution during and after the campaign.

It further claimed that some professionals who contributed their expertise to the campaign were not adequately recognised or effectively deployed.

According to the group, those experiences shaped its assessment of leadership, coalition-building, legislative experience, crisis management and national reach.

It also said the Labour Party was not, in its assessment, structurally or ideologically prepared to govern Nigeria.

Group outlines structure

The organisation said it would operate through a National Coordinator and a secretariat comprising a Secretary, Financial Secretary, Publicity Secretary and Operations Secretary.

It would also have regional coordinators for the six geopolitical zones and State Point Men across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The group said the national secretariat would provide direction, while the regional coordinators and State Point Men would implement programmes and report through the established structure.

It stressed that it did not claim to speak for all supporters of Obi.

“We deliberately do not call ourselves the ‘Obidient Movement.’ That name is a proprietary political identity tied to Peter Obi and the Labour Party. We are Batified Obidients — former Obidients who have crossed over to BAT and the Renewed Hope Agenda,” it said.

The group said its support for Tinubu was based on its assessment of his leadership capacity and the country’s current needs.

“We believe in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and we have confidence in his capability, his experience, and his commitment to Nigeria,” it said.

It added that its members were convinced that the administration’s ongoing reforms would benefit the country if sustained to fruition.

“Our mission is clear: re-elect President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, ensure his second term succeeds, and help deliver a Nigeria that works for all,” the group said.

Batified Obidients said its campaign would include explaining the administration’s reforms to the public and building support for the Renewed Hope Agenda ahead of the 2027 election.

The emergence of the group has also been reported as a new platform of former Obi campaign members supporting Tinubu and the APC ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Rescued 20 prospective NYSC members arrive Ibadan
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — The 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members rescued after being abducted while travelling to their orientation camps have arrived in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, and were taken to the Department of State Services (DSS) headquarters for debriefing.

The prospective corps members arrived at the DSS office in the Aleshinloye area of Ibadan South-West Local Government Area on Wednesday, following their release from captivity.

As of the time of filing this report, only representatives of the victims’ parents were allowed access to the DSS premises, while other relatives and sympathisers remained outside the facility.

Recall that 20 of the 30 prospective corps members travelling in two buses from Oyo State to orientation camps in Abia State were abducted by gunmen along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Umunoha, Imo State.

The remaining 10 prospective corps members escaped into the bush during the attack and subsequently made their way to safety.

The 20 abducted victims regained their freedom seven days after they were kidnapped.

The abductors had reportedly initially demanded a ransom of N50 million for each victim, amounting to N1 billion, before allegedly reducing the demand to N5 million per person, or N100 million for the 20 victims.

The abduction had earlier triggered concern among the victims’ parents, who on Saturday visited the private residence of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, in Ibadan to seek his intervention over the continued captivity of their children.

The parents were joined by the Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, and the Aseyin of Iseyinland, Oba Sefiu Adeyeri, in efforts to secure the release of the abducted prospective corps members.

Shortly after the victims regained their freedom, Ladoja announced their release, saying the information was confirmed to him by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma during a telephone conversation.

“The kidnapped graduates have been released. The Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, confirmed this in a telephone conversation at about 5.00pm,” Ladoja said in a statement issued by his media aide, Adeola Oloko, in Ibadan.

The arrival of the rescued prospective corps members in Ibadan marks another stage in efforts to establish the circumstances surrounding their abduction and provide them with the necessary support following their ordeal in captivity.

World.title: Gboko imposes curfew after protest turns violent
World.content:
…Council suspends BEMOA leadership

…Protesters burn two Civil Protection Guards vehicles

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Gboko Local Government Council in Benue State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on the area following unrest that erupted after the killing of a commercial motorcycle operator by unknown gunmen.

The council chairman, Torseer Yina, announced the curfew with effect from Thursday, October 8, 2026, as part of measures to contain the unrest and prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The chairman also suspended the leadership of the Benue Motorcycle Hirers Association (BEMOA), Gboko branch, following a protest by members of the association over the killing, which later turned violent.

The commercial motorcycle operator was allegedly shot at close range in the Gboko South area of the town on Wednesday night, after which his motorcycle was reportedly taken away by the assailant.

The Security Adviser to the Gboko Local Government Council, Akaakohol Nev, said BEMOA members took to the streets on Thursday morning to protest the killing.

According to him, the protest was later hijacked by hoodlums, leading to the destruction of property.

He said protesters marched to the office of the Benue State Civil Protection Guards on Shaahu Road and set two of the agency’s vehicles ablaze.

“They marched to the office of Benue State Civil Protection Guards on Shaahu Road and burnt two of their vehicles on the grounds that the bullet that was used on their member was a cartridge and they believed it was the Guards that carried out the act because their guns use cartridge,” Nev said.

He added that the council received information that a rifle was allegedly stolen from the office during the attack, saying the police were investigating the incident.

Following the development, Yina ordered the immediate suspension of the leadership of BEMOA in Gboko.

The decision was contained in a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the Secretary of the Local Government Security Council.

The statement said the suspension and curfew were necessary to contain the unrest and violent protest that followed the death of the motorcycle operator.

“The Executive Chairman, Gboko Local Government Council, Torseer Yina has suspended the leadership of the Benue Motorcycle Hirers Association (BEMOA), Gboko branch, with immediate effect,” the statement said.

It added that the protest was allegedly hijacked by hoodlums, resulting in the burning of two vehicles belonging to the Benue State Civil Protection Guards.

The council chairman warned that anyone caught violating the curfew or breaching public peace would face sanctions.

The statement, however, said the curfew would exempt the movement of persons and vehicles involved in essential services.

World.title: NDC faults 30-day petrol discount
World.content:
…Calls measure tokenism, questions implementation

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has criticised the Federal Government’s decision to introduce a 30-day discount on petrol sold through NNPC Limited retail outlets, describing the measure as inadequate to address the economic challenges facing Nigerians.

In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party said the temporary discount announced by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, amounted to “tokenism”.

Oyedele had explained that the government would offer a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for an initial period of 30 days, with priority given to public transport operators nationwide.

The minister said the measure was not a return to petrol subsidy but an arrangement under which the government would sell the product at cost.

However, the NDC described the initiative as a “Greek gift”, arguing that the removal of petrol subsidy was implemented without what it considered adequate consultation or measures to cushion its impact on Nigerians.

The party questioned the impact of the subsidy removal on workers, businesses and households, particularly those affected by rising living costs and difficulties accessing essential services.

“What happens to the millions of Nigerians who lost their jobs and whose businesses collapsed as a result of the callous and poorly planned removal of subsidy?” the party asked.

The NDC also questioned the practicality of distributing discounted petrol through designated NNPC retail outlets, asking whether the number of outlets would be sufficient to serve the country’s population.

It warned that concentrating discounted petrol sales at selected filling stations could result in congestion and create safety concerns for motorists and other members of the public.

The party further alleged that the initiative amounted to an attempt to reintroduce petrol subsidy “through the backdoor”, arguing that the policy reflected what it described as difficulties in managing the economy.

“Even the bogus promise to dispense discounted fuel at designated NNPC retail outlets is not pragmatic. How many such outlets exist in Nigeria to serve over 200 million Nigerians?” the statement said.

“Is this not the recipe for another stampede that could have many more Nigerians trampled to death at the filling stations?”

The NDC also criticised the economic policies of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration, alleging that the government had failed to reverse the economic difficulties confronting the country.

The party said several questions remained unanswered regarding the petrol discount and its implementation, adding that it believed the economy required a different policy direction.

NDC backs Obi for 2027

The party said it remained confident that a change of government would provide an alternative direction for the country.

It declared its support for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and other NDC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party urged Nigerians to vote for Obi and other NDC candidates, saying its proposed leadership would pursue what it described as a “New Nigeria”.

“His Excellency Peter Obi, under the NDC, will put Nigeria back on the right track. A New Nigeria is POssible with Obi,” the statement said.

It also urged Nigerians to participate in the January 16, 2027 presidential election and vote for Obi and other NDC candidates.

The NDC concluded by calling for greater scrutiny of the Federal Government’s petrol discount initiative and its broader economic policies.

World.title: 2027: ADC defies INEC warning, vows to publish polling-unit results
World.content:
Amupitan, INEC Chairman.

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to document, collate and share polling-unit results with the public during the 2027 general elections, despite a warning by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) against privately collated results.

The party said it would respect INEC’s exclusive power to declare official results and winners, but insisted that this did not stop political parties and citizens from independently gathering, verifying and sharing election figures.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said its position was based on its constitutional right to collect and share information.

“We are aware of our rights to freedom of expression under the Constitution. We are also aware of the limitations associated with those rights. And we hold that our rights to collate and share election results are not abrogated by any of the limitation clauses,” the party said.

The ADC said its polling agents would document results at polling units while its party structures would collate and verify the figures before making them public.

“The ADC will share our collated results with the public. Our agents will document results, our structures will collate them, and we will communicate verified figures to the public, clearly identifying their source and status,” the party said.

The party said acknowledging INEC’s statutory responsibility to declare election results did not mean that citizens or political parties had surrendered their right to independently collect and disseminate election information.

“Although we recognise INEC’s responsibility to make official declarations of results and to declare winners of elections, that responsibility cannot reasonably abrogate the right of citizens to collect and collate election results and to share them,” the ADC said.

The position comes after INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, warned against the sharing of privately collated election results, reinforcing the commission’s position that official declarations remain its responsibility.

World.title: Marwa Commends Security Agencies Over Rescue of 20 Kidnapped Corps Members
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Chairman/Chief Executive of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd.), has commended the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies for the successful rescue of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and another victim abducted in the South-east.

Marwa, in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Femi Babafemi, described the rescue operation as a victory for the country and evidence of what coordinated and intelligence-driven operations could achieve in the fight against criminality.

He said the safe return of the prospective corps members to their families demonstrated the courage, professionalism and unity of purpose among Nigeria’s security agencies.

“Our corps members are the nation’s best, serving their fatherland with hope and idealism. Nigeria owes them protection, and today our gallant men and women have delivered,” he said.

Marwa, who is a retired military officer, said it was important to draw public attention to the achievements of security agencies and commend them for their efforts in protecting Nigerians.

He also acknowledged other successful rescue operations conducted by security agencies across the country in recent months, saying the operations had freed abducted victims and restored hope to affected families.
