World.title: Madras High Court Registry lodges police complaint for forging its proceedings to get Bangladesh nationals deported
World.content:
CHENNAI

The Madras High Court Registry has lodged a complaint with the Greater Chennai Commissioner of Police in connection with its proceedings having been forged to get five Bangladesh nationals, lodged in a special foreigners camp at Attur in Salem district, deported to their country.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the High Court’s standing counsel S. John Raja Singh reported that a complaint on behalf of the Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi was lodged with the Chennai city police on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) in compliance of the court orders.

Bilal alias Mohammed Bilal Syed, Y. Salim and Bimal Sutrada alias Laxman Das had filed three individual writ petitions in the High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai as well as the State police to take steps for deporting them to their country.

Substantiating their claim, the petitioners had submitted copies of official proceedings supposedly issued by the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court on October 8, 2025 granting clearance for deportation of five Bangladesh nationals to their home country and insisted that they must be sent back forthwith.

Shocked to come across such proceedings, Justice Lakshminarayanan had on September 1, 2026 directed the High Court Registry to verify whether it had issued any such proceedings. The Registrar (Judicial) submitted a report on September 8, 2026 stating it was a forged document.

Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani told the court the petitioners had also annexed a document purportedly issued in favour of them by the Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services but the officer had confirmed that no such document had been issued by his office.

Central government standing counsel M.P. Jaisha, representing the FRRO, told the court that a complaint regarding forgery of government documents had already been lodged with the Central Crime Branch police in 2025 and that a First Information Report too was registered.

After recording their submissions, the judge had directed the High Court Registry to lodge a police complaint with regard to forgery of its proceedings. On being told the complaint was lodged on October 6, the judge called for a status report from the police by November 10, 2026.

World.title: ‘Vote Chor, Gaddi Chod’ slogan trends as thousands turn up for anti-SIR stir
World.content:
“When I landed here in Bengaluru yesterday, I saw social media posts claiming that Dhruv Rathee is coming to change the regime. I am not here to change the regime, neither has Soros funded this trip. I have come here to support this fight against vote theft,” said YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was in Bengaluru for his “first protest” against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which has so far led to deletions of 13 crore names at the draft stage.

Amid a sea of yellow-red Karnataka flags and national flags and shouts of “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chod”, thousands of people turned up for the protest at the Freedom Park, including hundreds whose names had been marked as absent, shifted or dead, as well as people who came to show that they were “eligible voters” and did not want their names deleted, as sought by others through Form 7.

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi must be thinking I have a problem with him, but he should know that now the entire nation has a problem with him. This is not about any party, it is about the ‘Right to Vote.’ Still, BJP voters are not convinced by the claims of vote theft,” said Mr. Rathee.

Key questions

“I have three questions. Modi, Shah or Gyanesh Kumar can answer to dismiss claims of “vote chori” — How were over 75 lakh people removed before the West Bengal elections and then added soon after the elections? These people were on the rolls before the elections and after the elections, but not during the election. Why were these people added back? What happened in Bihar? Over 40 lakh names were deleted, but Gyanesh Kumar did not say a word until the Supreme Court directed that these names be made public. In U.P., over 14 lakh names were ‘added’ suddenly. Who are these people? While in Goa, even though EROs wanted to add names, the ECI did not allow it,” he alleged.

Mr. Rathee was joined by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and spokespersons Saurav Das and Aushotosh Ranka.

Mr. Dipke alleged that Mr. Modi “did vote chori and won”. “People who are alive are being declared dead during the SIR. Mr. Modi has murdered democracy as the Election Commission of India conducted this exercise on the orders of Modi-Shah. Modi wants to have ownership over the people - One Nation, One Election is One Nation, One Party,” he alleged.

Gandhi, Ambedkar and Nehru

“Mahatma Gandhi is the soul of India, Ambedkar is the backbone and Nehru is the mind. Nehru gave voting rights to people who did not even know the meaning of electoral democracy or voting rights. But Mr. Modi is making people prove why their name should not be removed,” Mr. Dipke said, pointing out that even in the South, through delimitation, attempts are being made to limit participation, but “South Indian States will lead the country in the future.”

The protesters were also joined by former Supreme Court judge V. Gopala Gowda, actor Prakash Raj and writer Devanuru Mahadeva.

Nobody on earth can stop this agitation

Mr. Gowda said, “As a former Supreme Court judge, I am here to extend solidarity. I do not agree with the Supreme Court judgment on SIR. It is unconstitutional. Democracy is butchered and people will teach a lesson to those at the helm. Nobody on this earth can stop this agitation.”

Calling SIR an insult to every citizen of this country, actor Mr. Raj said, “The aim of the protest is not just to remove Gyanesh Kumar alone. He will go and another Agyanesh Kumar will come in the Election Commission. The aim is to scrap SIR and file a case against Gyanesh Kumar. Until then, the agitation will not stop.”

World.title: World Sight Day: glaucoma awareness camp for elderly held in Srikakulam on
World.content:
To mark World Sight Day, the Sankar Foundation eye hospital in Srikakulam conducted a glaucoma awareness programme for elderly persons in on Thursday .

Dr. K. Ramchran who conducted tests for the patients at the hospital said: “Blurred and low vision, constant headache, especially in the eyes are symptoms of glaucoma, a common disease among the elderly.” He added that the disease is prevalent among the middle-aged individuals and youth due to changes in their lifestyle.

Hospital managing trustee A. Krishna Kumar said that the Sankar Foundation had conducted 13, 738 tests for outpatients and completed nearly 2,674 surgeries for needy patients.

He said that the Foundation, which has hospitals in other places, had done 18,868 surgeries and ensured testing for 1,06, 776 persons between 1 April and 31 September, 2026. He said that special medical camps would be organised in Tekkali, Palasa, Sompeta, Ichchapuram and other places in the next two months to help poor patients get treatment in their vicinity. Deputy General Manager of the Foundation K. Bangar Raju said that the hospital was extending services free of cost to patients covered under NTR Vaidya Seva scheme.

World.title: ‘Women will bring inquilab’: Thousands join Chappal protest against gender discrimination
World.content:
Raising the slogan “Women will bring inquilab (revolution)”, thousands of people, following a lengthy people’s tribunal protest, joined the ‘Chappal Protest’ to express solidarity with women facing violence and discrimination across the country.

The protest came in the backdrop of the recent alleged assault on a journalist while she was covering a protest in Delhi and the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl near Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi.

Some women carried chappals as a symbol of resistance. Women at the protest spoke about injustices they had faced, ranging from domestic violence and gender-based violence to rape and harassment.

World.title: Slap row: Delhi HC seeks response from police, Parvesh Verma
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Thursday asked the city police and Public Works Department (PWD) Minister Parvesh Verma to respond to a plea seeking an independent probe into the incident where the leader allegedly slapped an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) worker.

Mr. Verma had allegedly slapped a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar on September 27.

Justice Sachin Datta issued a notice on the petition and asked the police to file a status report. The court also asked Mr. Verma to submit his reply to the plea.

During the brief hearing, the counsel for the police raised objection to the maintainability of the petition, which also sought police protection for petitioner Sahib Singh and his family members.

The court said that the matter will be heard next on November 17.

The petition

The petition, filed through advocate Onkar Roy, stated that Mr. Sahib Singh immediately submitted a written complaint to the Station House Officer of Vikas Puri police station, seeking appropriate legal action.

Mr. Sahib Singh claimed that his private mobile number was circulated, following which he began receiving repeated abusive, threatening and intimidating calls, as well as WhatsApp and social media messages from unknown numbers and accounts.

The petitioner sought protection of his life and liberty, preservation of CCTV and electronic evidence, and an independent investigation into his allegations of assault, threats and police inaction.

“In view of the continued threats to the petitioner and his family, the acts concerning the conduct of police personnel and the apprehension regarding the independence of the investigation by the local police, the petitioner has been constrained to approach this court seeking protection of his life and liberty...,” the plea said.

Mr. Sahib Singh stated that, on the day of the incident, he was recording the proceedings on his mobile phone when Mr. Verma allegedly became agitated over questions concerning the quality of road construction.

The petitioner alleged that he was slapped, abused and threatened, after which his mobile phone, containing the video recordings, was forcibly snatched and damaged. He said the incident was recorded and streamed on social media platforms.

He also claimed that while a member of Mr. Verma’s security team pushed him and assisted the minister in leaving the spot, the police officials present there did not intervene.

World.title: Adequate response: on the RBI and inflation
World.content:
After months of waiting and watching, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has decided to act to try to rein in rising inflation. Its decision to raise interest rates by 25 bps seemed increasingly inevitable. The RBI now projects retail inflation at 4.9% in Q2, higher than its August projection of 4.7%. This is set to rise in Q3 to 6% before easing marginally to 5.7% in Q4. Global oil prices have again crossed $100 a barrel following a brief reprieve. India’s oil marketing companies, likely following government instructions, have held off on passing most of this increase on to consumers. However, they cannot withstand such fiscal pressures forever. The impact of higher crude prices has been bad enough, but higher petrol and diesel prices will likely send inflation spiralling. Simultaneously, a deficient monsoon is pushing up food prices and will continue to do so for the rest of the year. When supply-side factors are the primary drivers of inflation, an interest rate hike can only have second-order and largely marginal effects on inflation. In such a scenario, the signal sent by the MPC becomes as important as the actual action. The MPC has used this latest policy review to attempt to dampen inflation expectations, an important area of action. The expectation of high inflation in the near future can often become a self-fulfilling prophecy, independent of the factors driving prices up.

A 25 bps interest rate hike is a careful nudge rather than an inevitably ineffectual bludgeon. The fact that the MPC has changed its stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ from ‘neutral’ is the bigger signal. The question no longer is whether the RBI will hike rates in its next meeting in December, but by how much. The message from this stance change is that the central bank will use all the tools at its disposal to keep inflation in check. The RBI also clearly thinks that the economy can withstand such tightening. It has revised upwards its GDP growth forecast for 2026-27 to 7.1% from the 6.7% projected in August. That said, all economic agencies have, even before interest rates were hiked, been predicting a slowdown in the second half of the year. The growth-inflation trade-off will again test the RBI’s deftness. Higher interest rates may also pause the ongoing exodus of Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), giving the RBI some exchange rate-related breathing room. The central bank has done what it can on inflation so far. The onus is now on the government. It has several tools to control food inflation, such as strategic buffers, import and export controls, anti-hoarding measures, and open market operations. Those need to be used more effectively.

World.title: Robbers kill man for phone, steal device already stolen by  deceased
World.content:
A man who allegedly stole a smartphone from a house in Chevella was killed by two robbers who fled with the device following an argument at the Chevella bus stand late on Wednesday (October 7).

The victim, who is yet to be identified, had reportedly alighted from a city bus and stayed back at the bus stand after services ended for the night.

According to Chevella Inspector K. Narender Reddy, the robbers, identified as Krishna and Sai, both daily wage labourers, approached the man and struck up a conversation before taking him to a secluded area within the bus stand premises.

The robbers were reportedly under the influence of alcohol, and an argument broke out between them. Police said the suspects and the victim were seen in CC cameras arguing for nearly an hour before the confrontation turned violent.

During the altercation, the suspects allegedly attacked the man with an old wooden chair, killing him, and fled with his mobile phone.

The incident came to light early on Thursday when Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) employees arrived for duty and noticed the body. They alerted the police, who reached the spot, examined the scene and shifted the body to a government hospital for post-mortem examination.

During the investigation, police found that the mobile phone taken by the suspects had itself been stolen earlier. The phone belonged to Jai Singh, a watchman residing in Chevella, who told investigators that he had left it charging at his house before it went missing.

Police suspect that the victim had stolen the phone before arriving at the bus stand, although his identity and involvement in the theft are yet to be established.

Investigators are circulating the victim’s photograph to establish his identity. Further investigation is underway.

World.title: Haryana CEO launches three-day drive to clear pending SIR notices
World.content:
The Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Haryana, has launched a special three-day drive to dispose of pending notices issued to voters under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with special camps and house-to-house collection of documents being undertaken from October 7 to 9 at polling stations where documents are still awaited.

As part of the drive, 57,339 pending hearing cases were disposed on October 7 and 8, reducing the number of cases awaiting hearings to 2,85,834 of the total notices generated in the State. The disposal of all pending hearings has been targeted by October 28, ahead of publication of the final electoral roll on November 6.

According to the CEO’s office, 44,91,923 notices were generated across Haryana for unmapped cases and other various discrepancies.

BLOs overworked

A Booth-Level Officer (BLO), who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the notices served on the voters were not received by all BLOs at the same time. “I received 250 notices on August 7, while others got theirs two or three days later. Some had 600, 700, 800 or even 900 notices,” the BLO said. He said that it took him nearly two months to complete the 250 notices, from August 7 to September 30. “If it took me so long to complete 250, those with 800-900 notices will naturally take much longer,” the BLO said, adding that some cases also remained pending as people were reluctant to submit documents during the hearing process. The BLO also flagged difficulties arising from the teachers returning for school and examination duties from October 1.

A woman BLO, who teaches at a government middle school in Sector 14 and requested anonymity, said she had to work until around 6.30 p.m. on several days during the voter-roll revision exercise over the past two months to dispose of the notices. She travelled from Bahadurgarh and often reached home only around 8-8.30 p.m. At her booth, she said, 745 voters remained on the electoral roll after deletions, while 580 were issued notices over various discrepancies. By September 30, 574 of these cases had been disposed of, she said. “For the remaining six voters, I have informed the officer concerned that they are not taking my calls,” she said.

She described the exercise as particularly challenging because many voters were unavailable during daytime, requiring her to visit their homes in the evening. She also cited pressure from senior officials, inadequate workspace and instances of rude behaviour from voters as some of the difficulties faced by her and fellow BLOs.

The strain was also felt inside schools. Rajbala, principal of the school, said eight to nine of its 13-14 teachers were engaged in election duty during the two-month exercise till September 30 to dispose of the notices, leaving only three or four teachers to manage the school.

Another woman teacher from the same school, who worked as an assistant to a BLO, said the polling personnel often struggled to find a proper place to sit. In some cases, local residents offered their houses to them, while another BLO had to sit beside an atta chakki as private schools where booths were located did not allow them to sit inside.

As of September 30, the last date for filing objections and claims, 3,77,987 Form-6 applications for inclusion of names in the electoral roll had been received. Gurugram accounted for the highest number at 39,985, followed by Faridabad (33,463) and Hisar (22,001). A total of 40,162 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names were received, with the highest numbers from Panipat (3,600), Hisar (2,790) and Sirsa (2,539). Meanwhile, 2,14,693 Form-8 applications seeking corrections, changes in address or EPIC details were received.

World.title: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis
World.content:
The Ministry of Information dismissed on Thursday a news report claiming that Pakistan Air Force (PAF) aircraft were being used against the Yemen’s Houthis as “fake and fabricated”.

A New York Times report published on Oct 7, a screenshot of which the ministry shared in an X post, cited an unnamed source as saying that PAF fighter jets were being employed against the group, amid the latter’s escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia.

But the information ministry denied the report, saying in a post on X that the NYT story “attributing the employment of PAF aircraft against Houthis is fake and fabricated”.

“International media houses are again asked to avoid speculative reporting with regards to employment of Pakistan’s military forces under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

“Details of any deployment, if necessary, will be given by the authorities concerned,” it added.

Earlier this week, the ministry also termed a Reuters report claiming the deployment of 30,000 to 40,000 Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia as “speculative”.

The development comes after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance in Riyadh on Monday.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Monday’s meeting under the alliance was held to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

A statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said the member states had “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

Asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

On Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry also said Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

Escalating tensions

The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that they had struck the Saudi capital’s main international airport with a ballistic missile, in another attack on the kingdom claimed by the group.

A day ago, Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports including in the capital Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs.

For its part, a Saudi-led coalition that backs pro-government forces in Yemen said on X that it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack on Riyadh.

The Houthis, who control most of the country’s northwest, are battling for territory against the Saudi-backed forces after the civil war reignited in July and they captured swathes of coastal land.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government this week declared a major counter-offensive and said Houthi fighters were pushed out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha.

But the Houthis say they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

Meanwhile, Pakistan has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

On Sept 18, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

At the same time, Pakistan has also asserted that the alliance is intended for collective deterrence and defensive in nature.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs2.31 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.78 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs2.31 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.78 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs398.96 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.72 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 9 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: No stipulation in Makkah pact bars 'direct involvement' in case of threat to a member: Asif
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Thursday that no stipulation of the Makkah Defence Alliance barred the member states from getting “directly involved” in case of a threat to one of the members.

He said this during ARY News programme ‘Khabar Muhammad Malick Ke Saath’ after he was asked about the possibility of Pakistan sending ground troops to Yemen amid an escalating conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia under the alliance, which comprises Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara.

World.title: PTI's 'doors are open' to Fazl's offer to play a role in breaking deadlock with govt: Junaid Akbar
World.content:
PTI MNA Junaid Akbar on Thursday said that the PTI’s “doors are open” to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s offer to play a role in ending the deadlocked negotiations between the government and opposition.

Over the weekend, the government and opposition held two rounds of talks ahead of the PTI’s march, initially planned for Islamabad, to demand the release of jailed party founder Imran Khan. The talks, however, ended in a stalemate, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points.

Speaking on the Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’ on Thursday evening, Akbar said Fazl had spoken to the PTI leadership and expressed the desire to play his part in ending the deadlock, if agreed to by the party.

“We are political people and we understand that the issue can be solved with dialogue,” he added, emphasising that “the intention of this should be dialogue” rather than an attempt to trap the PTI.

“Whatever role he wants to play in any purposeful dialogue that happens, our doors are open,” he said, adding that the party had been open to this “from the start”.

“We have never run from dialogue; we want that the solution be found through negotiations,” Akbar said, but added that the party was not given “space” for this.

In response to a question, he said that no framework had been put forward by Fazl regarding his role in the negotiations, although he noted that the JUI-F chief had been in touch with PTI leadership while he was away for Umrah.

While the MNA repeatedly stressed that the PTI’s “doors were open” to negotiations, he stressed that this could not be done by force.

“Our doors have always been open, but we will not sit down for negotiations at gunpoint, nor will we agree to them; no one can force us into negotiations,” he said.

The MNA added, “We are ready to sit down with anyone who wants to; we ask that you either convince us, or at least listen to what we have to say.”

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif also appeared to be confirming that efforts to restart negotiations between the Centre and the opposition were under way.

“I wish a positive result comes out of the efforts of those involved in the talks. But, I have little hope. Those making efforts are my brothers and friends, and I wish them well. We should always avoid unnecessary confrontation,” he said during ARY News programme ‘Khabar Muhammad Malick Ke Saath’.

Discussing the matter, he also remarked that Fazl was seemingly involved, either directly or indirectly.

On Wednesday, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also said “the doors for talks are open”, recalling Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s remarks from Tuesday calling on the PTI leadership to sit down with the government for dialogue and abandon their protest plans.

However, he also warned that the PTI could pressure the government into accepting its demands by holding the state “hostage” and creating political instability.

Prior to that, a delegation of opposition parties called on Fazl, who advised the government after the meeting not to obstruct the PTI long march heading towards Islamabad, as protests were a democratic right enjoyed by all political parties.

Speaking to the media alongside opposition leaders outside his residence, the JUI-F leader also urged the government to trust the PTI’s intention regarding a peaceful protest. When political parties say they will remain peaceful, their word should be trusted, he said in a comment on measures taken by the government to stop the PTI protesters from entering the federal capital.

A delegation of the government also visited Fazl on Wednesday amid reports about the possibility of his involvement as a mediator between the two sides.

The hours-long negotiations between the government and the opposition ended in a deadlock on Sunday during a second round of talks. The meeting at Parliament House began on Saturday afternoon and continued into the wee hours of Sunday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s protest march.

After the talks collapsed, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations, saying that he had changed the draft of the agreement despite what had been agreed to earlier.

However, PTI leaders, presenting the opposition’s stance on the failed talks, declared that reconciliation with the government was not possible without including incarcerated party founder Imran Khan in the dialogue process. They said that another reason for the failure of the talks was that the government was not willing to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism.

And following the breakdown of the talks, the PTI launched its long march.

World.title: Bahrain working to 'speed up' approval of Pak-GCC free trade pact, foreign minister says
World.content:
Bahrain on Thursday said it was working to “speed up” the approval of a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).

The remarks came after the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad.

Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

Addressing a joint press briefing with Dar, the Bahraini minister noted that the JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”.

He said both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment, as well as to convene the joint working group on energy next month on oil, gas and minerals.

They also agreed to take forward cooperation in food security, information technology, law enforcement, media, labour mobility, health, education, culture and sports.

“We also committed to finalising the GCC-Pakistan free trade agreement,” he said, referring to the potential deal that was said to be near finalisation in late 2025.

The minister said that Bahrain, having the GCC presidency, was working to “speed up the signing or the approval of the GCC-Pakistan FTA”.

Responding to a query, the visiting dignitary described the bilateral relationship between Pakistan and Bahrain as “very healthy and strong”.

He added that it was “radiant and well-looked after” by Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. “It is really valued by the people of Bahrain,” he added.

Highlighting recent bilateral exchanges between their countries, FM Al Zayani said: “We have a very truthful relationship; we are so frank with each other. We understand the constraints on each other and work accordingly.”

Emphasising the consistency in their ties, with no “ups and downs”, he said, “We are consistent and growing. We feel safe in this relationship.”

Al Zayani expressed Manama’s appreciation for Islamabad’s “principled positions on the ongoing crisis”, including its support in March for a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning Iranian attacks on GCC countries.

The minister also praised Pakistan’s “efforts alongside other partners to facilitate US-Iran dialogue and de-escalation, including by hosting the Islamabad Talks” in April.

The Bahrain FM went on to strongly condemn the recent deadly “terrorist attacks” on Saudi Arabia’s Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport.

He also condemned the “Houthi terrorist militia’s attacks on civilians and civilian facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its assault” on the holy cities of Makkah and Madina.

Noting that targeting of civilian facilities was a “flagrant violation” of international law, Al Zayani affirmed Bahrain’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia “whose security is an integral part of our own and of the GCC”.

The Bahrain FM said he and Dar also discussed the crises in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where “commercial vessels continue to come under attack”.

They underscored the importance of freedom and safety of navigation and respect for international law, he added.

Al Zayani vowed Bahrain and Pakistan will continue “close coordination” at the UNSC and between their Missions in New York.

Furthermore, the visiting FM noted that the two countries will mark 55 years of diplomatic relations on Oct 14.

Al Zayani remarked that the “bonds of brotherhood, trust and solidarity […] gained fresh momentum with the official visits to Bahrain” of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in November 2025 and of President Asif Ali Zardari in January this year.

The minister noted that more than 140,000 Pakistanis in Bahrain contributed to its progress and “form a living bridge between our peoples”.

The Bahrain FM said he would also meet with PM Shehbaz, President Zardari and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit.

Gulf situation, Palestine, IWT discussed

In his remarks, Dar thanked Al Zayani and his delegation for “their constructive engagement and their very valuable contribution to the success of today’s JMC session”.

Noting that the discussions were held in a cordial and constructive atmosphere, he said both sides “reaffirmed our shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation across a broad spectrum of sectors”.

“A key outcome of the session was the strengthening of our institutional framework through the operationalisation of several joint working groups,” Dar said, adding that these mechanisms will help ensure effective implementation of the decisions taken by the JMC.

“Both sides also agreed to enhance cooperation in trade and investment promotion, industrial collaboration, agriculture and food security, skills development, higher education, information technology, logistics and maritime affairs, among many other areas.”

They “particularly welcomed closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries”, the deputy premier added.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training and human resource development, with a view to creating new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers.

Dar noted that he and Al Zayani also exchanged views on the “evolving situation in the Gulf and emphasised the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy”.

“We discussed the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab, given their importance to regional and global food and energy security.”

The ministers also discussed the “grave situation in Palestine” and expressed concern over the “continued expansion of illegal settlements and attempts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif”.

Dar also raised the issue of India’s unilateral decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, terming it a “material breach of international law”.

“Such actions jeopardise the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” the deputy premier stressed.

“Pakistan-Bahrain friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are brotherly nations, with long fraternal ties, cooperating on international foras and meeting very frequently wherever we get an opportunity like brothers,” the DPM affirmed.

He expressed Pakistan’s commitment to “building an even more prosperous future together, God-willing, and taking the trade and economic ties to a new height”.

Dar said Islamabad looked forward to the convening of the JMC’s fourth session in Bahrain in 2027, as both sides will try to hold the meetings every year.

President Zardari meets Bahrain FM

Separately, President Zardari met with the Bahrain foreign minister, who called on him at the President House.

According to a press release by the president’s secretariat, the two leaders first held a restricted meeting, which was followed by a delegation-level meeting.

Zardari, in conversation with Al Zayani, said that Pakistan was “keen to translate strong bilateral political relations into deeper trade and investment ties”, according to the statement.

Noting that the country attached “great importance” to its relations with Bahrain, he expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, highlighting opportunities for this cooperation in “food security, IT and digital services, construction, mining, port handling, research and development, tourism and healthcare”. He also encouraged greater business-to-business engagement between the two countries.

“The president appreciated Bahrain’s warm welcome of the Islamabad MoU and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and its recognition of Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace, security and stability,” the press release said.

It added that President Zardari also appreciated Bahrain’s support and opportunities for over 134,000 Pakistanis residing in the kingdom, and welcomed continued cooperation on matters regarding the Pakistani diaspora.

“The president said Pakistan and Bahrain share a long-standing and trusted defence partnership, reflected in joint exercises, high-level exchanges and institutional cooperation,” it said, adding that he expressed Pakistan’s readiness to further strengthen cooperation in manpower, logistics, training and defence hardware.

On the topic of the regional situation, he expressed Pakistan’s commitment to constructive engagement with all parties to “build trust, bridge gaps and promote lasting peace, security and stability in the region”.

During the meeting, Al Zayani conveyed the greetings of King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the crown prince and prime minister of Bahrain, to the president, the statement added.

He termed the JMC meetings “highly productive” and noted that the president’s visit to Bahrain had left “a significant and positive impact on bilateral relations”.

He commended Pakistan’s courageous efforts to mediate amid the current regional situation and bring warring parties to the table, saying that Pakistan’s actions had “helped save many lives”. He appreciated Pakistan’s peace efforts and congratulated it on its successful tenure as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council.

Meeting with PM Shehbaz

The foreign minister also called on PM Shehbaz, who warmly welcomed him and conveyed his best wishes to the leadership and people of Bahrain, according to a press release by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s “deep appreciation for the longstanding and brotherly relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, founded on shared values, mutual trust, and close people-to-people ties”, the PMO said.

PM Shehbaz expressed his satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations. He emphasised Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Bahrain in diverse fields, “including trade, investment, energy, and human resource development”.

FM Al Zayani, meanwhile, conveyed the greetings and well-wishes of the leadership of Bahrain to the premier, and reaffirmed Bahrain’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across mutually beneficial areas.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and emphasised the importance of continued consultations and coordination on issues of mutual interest,” the statement said.

Al Zayani “appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and mediation efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”, the PMO added.

The prime minister expressed confidence that the JMC session would provide “further impetus” to bilateral cooperation and help deepen the relationship between the two countries.

“The meeting was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, reflecting the close and longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain,” the statement added.

Meeting with CDF Munir

The visiting dignitary also called on Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

During the meeting, the two leaders discussed matters of mutual interest, including the regional security situation and bilateral defence and security, according to a press release issued by the ISPR.

CDF Munir “underscored the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, rooted in shared values and mutual respect”, the statement said.

“He reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in the defence and security domains,” it added.

The press release added that Al Zayani appreciated the “professionalism and operational preparedness” of Pakistan Armed Forces, reiterated Bahrain’s resolve to further enhance bilateral cooperation, and acknowledged Pakistan’s contributions towards regional peace and stability.

JMC meeting

During the JMC meeting, Islamabad and Manama “agreed to deepen collaboration in trade and investment, energy, agriculture and food security, information technology, health, education and labour”, FO said.

They also discussed measures to strengthen connectivity and promote people-to-people exchanges.

Dar “underscored the importance of translating the longstanding and fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain into tangible benefits for their people”.

He further stressed effective implementation of the agreed outcomes through joint working groups, institutional partnerships and regular follow-up, the FO added.

The JMC was attended by high-level delegations from both sides.

The Pakistani team included the secretaries of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and the Economic Affairs Division, along with the acting foreign secretary. The Bahraini side included senior officials and representatives of the Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

In his address to the JMC meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to increase bilateral trade with Bahrain to the $1 billion target set earlier.

Noting the target of doubling trade in three years, of which one has already elapsed, Dar quipped, “But God forbid, if we miss [the target by] a few months, we have a great excuse that this period has been very turbulent.”

Dar also referred to the potential Pakistan-GCC FTA, noting that the GCC secretary general told him the deal was “almost ripe”, with one country yet to give a green light to it.

“I’m sure the signing of the free trade agreement between the GCC and Pakistan will surely help us in achieving our goals,” the deputy premier said, adding that it would lead to an increase in imports and exports.

He requested the Bahraini side to work towards recognising degrees and professional qualifications, while facilitating greater mobility of skilled labour between the two countries.

The two ministers also signed a protocol recording the minutes of the JMC session at the foreign ministry, according to the FO.

“The minutes record understandings on cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture and food security, oil, gas and minerals, maritime affairs, information technology and telecommunications, health, education and labour, among other areas,” the FO said in a separate statement.

It added that both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment at the government level, as an institutional mechanism for “regular consultations, coordination and cooperation on bilateral trade and investment”.

Bilateral meeting

Prior to the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, the two foreign ministers also held a separate meeting after Al Zayani’s arrival at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

In a post on X about the “cordial” meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said the two ministers “reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain relations and expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in high-level engagement between the two countries”.

“They discussed ways to further expand bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly in trade, economic and investment relations, as well as through engagement at multilateral fora.”

The two sides also exchanged views on “regional and international developments of mutual interest and underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the most viable means of addressing challenges and resolving disputes”, the FO added.

According to an earlier FO statement, the two sides were to “review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges”.

“Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” the FO noted.

Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the JMC session.

They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability.

Pak-Bahrain exchanges

Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan.

Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries.

Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC and directed the ministries concerned to pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit.

The Pakistani leadership has also undertaken official visits to the Gulf kingdom in recent years.

PM Shehbaz, accompanied by Dar, made a two-day trip to Bahrain in November 2025, during which he met with the king and crown prince there.

Then, in January this year, President Zardari made a four-day trip to the kingdom, where he highlighted economic opportunities that Pakistan offers.

World.title: Afridi-led convoy enters Peshawar as PTI long march continues for 5th day
World.content:
PESHAWAR: A convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi entered Peshawar on Thursday evening as PTI continued its long march for a fifth consecutive day.

The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4.

While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 8.

A post by the PTI’s official X account shortly after 6pm said the Afridi-led convoy had reached Hayatabad Toll Plaza in Peshawar. It also shared pictures of hundreds of supporters gathered to welcome the KP CM.

“God-willing, by the time it reaches Swabi, this caravan will become the largest long march in Pakistan’s history,” the PTI asserted.

Addressing supporters at the toll plaza, CM Afridi urged them to maintain their determination for the “struggle for true freedom”.

“There might be some discomfort, but this pain is not greater than the pain Imran Khan sahib is enduring in jail for us,” he said.

The PTI leader went on to say, “We shall not hesitate to even sacrifice [our] life for Imran Khan sahib.”

While Afridi said he would announce the next plan of action after proceeding to other areas of Peshawar, he also said the public would be “thrilled” upon hearing his plan when he reaches Swabi.

In a video shared by the PTI, Afridi could be seen raising slogans of “Free Imran Khan”, with supporters chanting in harmony.

Ahead of the protesters’ arrival, an unannounced disruption of mobile and cellular internet services was reported since last night in several areas of the provincial capital.

Long march plan

The caravan seemed to be behind schedule as it was supposed to reach Hayatabad Toll Plaza by 2pm, according to the schedule for Oct 8 shared by Information Minister Shafi Jan in the morning.

It was to pass by Bhana Mari Chungi, Kohati Chowk at Circular Road, Jameel Chowk, Pir Zakori Bridge, Kabootar Chowk, and then plans to reach Charsadda Road.

This screengrab from Google Maps shows the locations along the route specified by PTI for its journey in Peshawar on Oct 8, 2026.

Addressing PTI supporters at Bhana Mari Chowk in Peshawar, the KP CM said their next stop after Peshawar would be Charsadda, where he would share few details of the next course of action. The detailed plan, which he called a “yorker”, would be shared in Swabi.

PTI’s march began from Lakki Marwat on Oct 4, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and then camped overnight on Oct 6 in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar. It then reached Khyber on Oct 7, before proceeding towards Peshawar.

According to an earlier schedule, CM Afridi was to lead his supporters to Khairabad — which borders Punjab’s Attock — on Oct 8 and announce the next plan of action there.

However, the chief minister has now said the march will go all the way to Swabi, where he would announce the PTI’s next move.

This screengrab from Google Maps shows the approximate route taken by the PTI convoy during its journey from Lakki Marwat to Peshawar, along with the next tentative stop of Swabi.

The Centre has warned the party against any protests or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

The march was announced as part of the PTI’s nationwide protest, initially scheduled for Sept 27 but was later postponed to Oct 4.

Gohar calls for reviewing counterterrorism policy

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said on Thursday that his party had never supported terrorism, adding that, however, the country’s counterterrorism policy needed to be reviewed in the light of changing circumstances.

Gohar was speaking to the media in Charsadda, which is expected to be the next stop of the PTI’s march after Peshawar.

The PTI chairperson visited the residences of KP Public Health Engineering Minister Fazal Shakoor and MNA Fazal Mohammad Khan, whom the PTI alleges were abducted by unidentified men amid reports of detentions of its workers and members ahead of the march.

Gohar expressed concern over their disappearance and demanded their immediate and safe recovery.

Speaking to the media at their residences, he noted that 18 days had passed since Shakoor’s alleged abduction and his family had no information about his whereabouts.

He urged the relevant authorities to take immediate notice of the matter and ensure that Shakoor and Khan were recovered and reunited with their families.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan speaks to the media in Charsadda on Oct 8. — Photo by Faiz Muhammad

Gohar said the “enforced disappearances” were a matter of serious concern and stressed the need for rule of law and protection of citizens’ constitutional rights. If such incidents were taking place in KP, they could also occur in other provinces, he further warned.

He also rejected the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency as a solution to the prevailing situation in KP, as federal ministers continue to indicate the possible enforcement of either of the two, citing terrorism. The warning of a possible emergency or governor’s rule had come ahead of the PTI’s long march and as talks between the opposition party in the Centre and the federal government failed earlier this month.

For his part, Gohar said political issues should be resolved through constitutional and democratic means. He called upon the decision-makers to respect the public mandate and elected governments.

On the security situation, he asserted that the PTI, its workers and supporters had never supported terrorism. He said the party stood with the state in the fight against terrorism, but the country’s policy on the issue needed to be reviewed in light of changing circumstances.

“Terrorism, whether in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan or Sindh, is against Pakistan,” he said, adding that the loss of any Pakistani’s life in the fight against terrorism was a national loss. He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan through a unified national policy rather than politicising the issue.

Gohar also defended CM Afridi, saying he had never issued a statement in support of terrorists. He criticised what he described as attempts by some federal ministers to portray PTI as a supporter of terrorism.

The PTI chairperson said his party was still ready for meaningful and positive dialogue with its political opponents and expressed hope that Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman would play a constructive role in the prevailing situation. He thanked the JUI-F, Awami National Party and Jamaat-i-Islami for opposing the imposition of governor’s rule.

On the PTI’s long march, he said it would continue as per the decided schedule, with gatherings planned in Mardan on Oct 10 and Swabi on Oct 11, after which the future course of action would be decided by the party leadership.

He also criticised the imposition of Section 144 in parts of KP, saying elected representatives should be taken into confidence in matters concerning law and order.

He urged all political parties, whether in government or opposition, to play their role in strengthening democracy, an independent judiciary, free elections and the rule of law.

Gohar said the federal government and the opposition needed to set aside their differences and engage in sincere, unconditional dialogue to help the country overcome its political crisis.

Mobile services disrupted

Though there was no word from the provincial government on the unannounced cellular disruption, a Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) official, however, confirmed to Dawn that the authority had ordered the suspension at the directives of higher authorities.

The official told Dawn the suspension was temporary and taken as a security precaution during the long march. The official said the orders were conveyed on Wednesday night.

Special Assistant to the Chief Minister on Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saeed Marwat did not respond to whether his department requested the interior ministry cell phone service suspension. KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was also not available for comment.

Meanwhile, some major private schools across Peshawar also remained closed on Thursday. However, government schools, colleges and universities remained open.

Many parents found out about the school closure on Thursday morning when their children returned home after finding the school gates locked.

Yousaf Khan, a resident of Ring Road, told Dawn that he found out on Thursday morning. “My children were told at the school gate to go back,” he said, adding that he did not hear about the closure due to the suspension of cellular service.

“Due to the prevailing political situation in the city, the school will remain closed tomorrow, i.e, on Oct 8”, a notice from one of the private schools read, adding that classes will resume from Friday.

However, Private Schools Regulatory Authority (PSRA) officials said no order for school closure was issued, and action will be taken against schools that remained closed without government directions.

The authority has also written to the principals of all private schools, stating that certain private educational institutions had been closed by their respective administrations in connection with the ongoing long march, without any notification from the PSRA.

“In view of the above, all heads/principals/administrators of private educational institutions are hereby directed to keep their respective institutions open and ensure regular academic activities until clear directions/notification are issued by this authority,” the letter, seen by Dawn, read.

It said that failure to comply with the directions would be viewed seriously, and strict disciplinary action would be initiated against the concerned institution/management under the relevant rules and regulations.

PHC seeks CM Afridi’s reply to contempt plea

Separately, the Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Thursday sought a reply from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to a contempt petition alleging that he violated a court order by using an official helicopter to participate in the PTI long march.

A bench comprising Chief Justice SM Attique Shah and Justice Ijaz Khan issued notice to the chief minister on a petition filed by PML-N MPA Zahir Khan.

The petitioner alleged that the chief minister violated the court’s Oct 23, 2025 judgment, which barred the use of government vehicles, machinery and manpower for protests, rallies, long marches or political activities.

According to the petition, Afridi used a KP government helicopter on Oct 4 to travel from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat to participate in, launch and lead the PTI’s long march.

Appearing for the petitioner, Barrister M Yaseen Raza Khan recalled the Oct 2025 PHC judgment issued on a 2024 writ petition, in which the KP government was made a respondent.

“Accordingly, we dispose of the writ petition; however, the respondents and all concerned authorities are directed to ensure, with utmost diligence, that no official vehicle, machinery, or manpower under their control is deployed, used, or permitted to be used for any protest, long march, rally, or political activity of any nature,” Barrister Yaseen quoted from the judgment.

He argued that the PHC’s directive was clear, unequivocal and binding upon the provincial government and all authorities and functionaries working under its control.

The lawyer noted that CM Afridi used an official helicopter of the KP government to travel to Lakki Marwat to lead the political long march organised by his party.

“The official helicopter was thus placed at the personal disposal of the respondent for facilitating his participation in an expressly political activity prohibited by the judgment,” the counsel pointed out.

He contended that the violation was not confined merely to the CM’s journey, but the official helicopter’s use necessarily involved deployment of its pilots, crew, fuel, technical staff, ground arrangements, security personnel, protocol officials and other public resources.

He added that the entire official machinery accompanying and facilitating the said flight was employed to enable the chief minister to reach and lead the political long march, in direct violation of the 2025 ruling.

The petitioner sought contempt proceedings against CM Afridi and asked the court to summon him and seek details of the helicopter’s authorisation, flight log and expenditure. The hearing was then adjourned.

World.title: WTO hikes global trade growth forecast, names Pakistan among nations gaining from disruptions amid ME conflict
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The World Trade Organisation on Thursday sharply raised its global trade growth forecast for 2026 — with merchandise trade riding the AI boom — and concluded that some nations, including Pakistan, were actually benefiting from trade disruptions amid the ongoing Middle East conflict in some ways.

In its Global Trade Outlook Update 2026, the Geneva-based global trade watchdog said its economists had upgraded their forecasts for global merchandise trade volume growth to 3.9 per cent for 2026 and 4.1pc for 2027 — up from previous estimates of 1.9pc and 2.6pc, respectively, projected at the start of the US-Iran conflict in March.

The report said that despite the conflict, the global economy had remained resilient, reflecting a stronger-than-expected surge in AI-related capital investment and increased supplies of fuels and fertilisers from countries outside the Middle East.

While several countries faced fuel transport disruptions because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the redistribution of traffic was creating opportunities for various other economies, it said.

“For example, Pakistan’s exports of sea freight transport services rose by 73pc year-on-year in the first half of 2026, as its transport operators benefited from increased traffic,” the WTO said.

Vessel calls at major container terminals in Karachi were still 14pc higher year-on-year in July, it added.

Exports by the United States to the European Union continued to expand while exports to Asia and the Pacific decreased by 2pc in the second quarter.

At the same time, computer services exports by several smaller and emerging players expanded rapidly. In the second quarter, computer services exports from Malaysia rose by 34pc, those from Pakistan by 23pc and by 13pc in Brazil.

The WTO also noted that the rerouting of vessels and containers towards alternative ports and trans-shipment hubs had put pressure on capacity in South Asia, translating into higher charges. In July, the Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) introduced a congestion surcharge of $500 per container on shipments from Northern Europe to India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

“Longer waiting and transit times are increasing costs for carriers and traders, some of which may ultimately be passed on to consumers,” it said.

Stronger-than-expected growth reflects opposing forces

The report revised the forecast for commercial services trade volume growth in 2026 down to 3.3pc from the previous 4.8pc, as the conflict in the Middle East has depressed travel and tourism in the region and raised fuel input costs worldwide.

In 2027, growth rates in volume terms for merchandise and commercial services trade were expected to rise to 4.1pc and 6.4pc, respectively, but this outcome depended on a timely resolution of the Middle East conflict, according to the WTO.

Based on these projections, the volume of global goods and services trade was expected to grow by approximately 3.7pc in 2026 and 4.7pc in 2027, the organisation forecast.

The stronger-than-expected growth in merchandise trade reflects two opposing forces, according to the watchdog. On the one hand, the push from AI-related investment has increased demand for AI-enabling goods, which accounted for 47pc of global merchandise trade growth in value terms in the first half of 2026. On the other hand, reduced shipments of oil, natural gas and fertilisers have weighed on merchandise trade; for the ongoing year to date, the former has outweighed the latter, the WTO said.

It noted that while high commodity prices may persist as a result of bottlenecks constraining the flows of fuels and fertilisers, continued AI investment and the broader digitisation of the global economy were expected to keep merchandise trade growth above the rate of global GDP growth in 2027.

“AI investment and the Middle East conflict are also affecting the services trade outlook, but to different degrees. AI is lifting trade in computer and financial services. However, the impact of the conflict in the Middle East is prevailing in traditional services such as transport, tourism and construction,” it said.

Conversely, services trade growth is expected to remain below trend this year before rebounding in 2027. Asia and North America are expected to see their contributions decline, while those of Europe are expected to remain broadly stable, putting the region on track to account for over half of the growth in export services this year.

Meanwhile, the rest of the world was expected to make a negative contribution, dragged down by a large contraction in the Middle East, the report added. All services sub-sectors are expected to see growth below the March baseline forecast.

However, it noted that the trade forecast remains subject to several significant risks.

“The current wedge between crude oil and refined oil prices is weighing on trade growth by eroding households’ purchasing power. A slowdown or reversal of AI investment spending could also have a significant impact on trade given its high import content,” it said.

Turning to trade statistics in value terms, the WTO said the current US dollar value of world merchandise trade had risen considerably faster than volume in the first half of 2026, up 15pc year-on-year compared to 3.5pc growth in volume terms.

“This marks one of the largest gaps between the value and volume of trade growth in recent years, reflecting higher prices for fuels and electronic components for data centres,” it said.

It noted that trade continued to show “some alignment with geopolitical considerations”, although it pointed out that the gap between intra-bloc and inter-bloc trade had narrowed through 2025 and into 2026, suggesting that “the broader pattern of bloc-based fragmentation has not continued to intensify”.

US-China trade decoupling had, however, accelerated since 2025 and was now the main driver of the bloc divergence, it added.

World.title: US freezes Microsoft, Adobe, Infosys green-card applications over alleged fraud
World.content:
The Trump administration on Thursday froze some green-card filings by Microsoft, Adobe and major IT outsourcers and opened probes into nine elite universities, widening a visa crackdown it says targets fraud and American job losses.

The twin actions mark the broadest strike yet against skilled-worker immigration programmes, potentially blocking a common path to permanent residency for thousands of foreign tech workers while putting some of the country’s most prominent research universities on notice.

The moves come even as the administration cultivates closer ties with the same tech leaders whose companies are now in its crosshairs.

“Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” US Vice President JD Vance said. “There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft.”

Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for allegedly bringing in international students to undercut American wages.

Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling added that some of the largest IT firms in the world would also be suspended from that programme, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.

“We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies,” Sonderling said.

Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro and Capgemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tata Consultancy Services declined to comment.

Under the Labour Department’s permanent labour certification process, known as PERM, which is required for most employment-based green cards, employers must show that hiring a foreign worker will not harm the wages, working conditions or job opportunities of US workers.

Approved applications then go to US Citizenship and Immigration Services.

The freeze does not appear to directly affect current holders of H-1B visas, which allow companies to employ foreign workers temporarily. But it could block a common route by which employers sponsor those workers for permanent residency.

Indian IT firms such as Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL, along with Cognizant, have long been among the biggest users of H-1B visas.

Amazon.com was the largest employer of approved H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal 2026, followed by Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Apple and Microsoft, according to USCIS data.

Microsoft is also the largest filer of PERM applications, according to Permtrack.app, which compiles Labour Department disclosure data.

Crackdown widens

The suspensions are the latest in a series of steps against skilled-worker programmes.

In September last year, the Labour Department launched an enforcement drive called “Project Firewall,” as a White House proclamation imposed a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers hired from abroad.

During President Donald Trump’s second term, companies have faced growing pressure to keep jobs and production in the United States rather than move them overseas.

The action comes despite closer ties between the administration and tech leaders, who are lobbying for lighter AI regulation. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was among the executives at a White House AI summit on September 29.

Universities under scrutiny

The nine universities also include Brown and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Vance accused them of using J-1 exchange-visitor visas to bring in international students and undercut American wages.

Labour Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito said subpoenas had already been served.

“We will investigate whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships, or visa abuse are compromising federally funded research,” D’Esposito said.

“If an American university is breaking the law to save $1 while exposing American research to a foreign adversary, that is not academic excellence. It’s institutional betrayal.”

The probe adds to the administration’s long-running fight with Harvard over foreign students.

Last year, the Department of Homeland Security subpoenaed Harvard for documents on alleged misconduct by international students and its compliance with federal immigration law. Harvard called that subpoena “unfounded retribution” but said it would comply as far as the law requires.
